pt 2, div 1, sdiv 15AB: Ins 2020 No 40, Sch 4.5.

block.txt: Low impact performance of live music or arts is development specified for this code if it is not carried out in a residential zone.
The standards specified for this development are that the development—
must be carried on inside a building, and
must not contravene an existing relevant condition of the most recent development consent that applies to the premises, and
must not contravene the Protection of the Environment Operations Act 1997, and
must not be primarily used for adult entertainment, including, for example, a strip club, and
must not be carried on in connection with a proposed change of use of premises.
In this clause—
existing relevant condition means a condition relating to any of the following—
the number of persons permitted in the building,
hours of operation,
noise, other than a condition mentioned in the Liquor Act 2007, Schedule 1, clause 70(1),
car parking, vehicular movement and traffic generation,
loading management of waste,
landscaping.

The construction or installation of a roof mounted evaporative cooling unit on land in Climate Zone 4 is development specified for this code if it is not carried out on or in a heritage item or a draft heritage item.
For the purposes of this clause, land is in Climate Zone 4 if it is within an area identified as Zone 4 of the Climate Zones for Thermal Design in the Building Code of Australia.
For air-conditioning units see clause 2.5.
The standards specified for that development are that the development must—
be for residential uses only, and
be located at least 3m from each side boundary, and
be not higher than 1.8m above the highest point of the roof of the building on which it is mounted, and
be constructed or installed so that any opening created is adequately weather proofed, and
not involve work that reduces the structural integrity of the building, and
be designed so as not to operate—
during peak time—at a noise level that is more than 5 dB(A) above the ambient background noise level measured at any property boundary, or
during off peak time—at a noise level that is audible in habitable rooms of adjoining residences, and
if it is located on bush fire prone land—be constructed of non-combustible material and be adequately sealed or protected to prevent the entry of embers, and
if it is constructed or installed in a heritage conservation area or a draft heritage conservation area—be located in the rear yard and must not be visible from a public road.
For further information about noise control see the Noise Guide for Local Government (ISBN 978 1 74232 942 0) published by the Department of Environment, Climate Change and Water NSW in October 2010.

heading.b: Farm buildings damaged by natural disasters

block.txt: The demolition of an existing farm building that has been significantly damaged or destroyed by a natural disaster and the erection of a new farm building is development specified for this code if the development is not carried out on or in a heritage item or a draft heritage item or in an environmentally sensitive area.
The following standards are specified for the development—
the existing farm building must have been lawfully erected,
the development must not contravene an existing condition of the most recent development consent that applies to the landholding,
the development must be carried out in accordance with AS 2601—2001, The demolition of structures,
the new structure must be in the same location as the existing structure,
the new structure must be of the same building classification under the Building Code of Australia as the existing structure,
the new structure must not have a height or total footprint greater than the height or total footprint of the existing structure,
the new structure must be constructed of non-combustible material if it is located—
on bush fire prone land, and
within 5m of a dwelling house,

the development must comply with the standards specified in the following provisions, except in relation to the location or height of the new structure or minimum distances other than a distance relating to a waterbody (natural)—
for a farm building other than a stock holding yard, grain silo or grain bunker—clause 2.32,
for a stock holding yard—clause 2.32B,
for a grain silo or grain bunker—clauses 2.32D–2.32F.

heading.b: Farm buildings (other than stock holding yards, grain silos and grain bunkers)

block.txt: The construction or installation of a farm building (other than a stock holding yard, grain silo or grain bunker) that is not used for habitable purposes is development specified for this code if it is—
constructed or installed on land in Zone RU1, RU2, RU3, RU4 or RU6, and
not constructed or installed on or in a heritage item or a draft heritage item or in an environmentally sensitive area, and

not constructed or installed on land shown on any relevant Procedures for Air Navigation Services—Aircraft Operations Map prepared by the operator of an aerodrome or airport operating within 2 kilometres of the proposed development and for which a PANS-OPS surface is identified that may compromise the effective and on-going operation of the relevant aerodrome or airport.

Farm building is defined in the Standard Instrument as a structure the use of which is ancillary to an agricultural use of the landholding on which it is situated and includes a hay shed, stock holding yard, machinery shed, shearing shed, silo, storage tank, outbuilding or the like, but does not include a dwelling.
Subdivisions 16A and 16B make special provision for farm buildings that are stock holding yards, grain silos or grain bunkers.
The following standards are specified for that development—
the development must not be higher than—
for a landholding that has an area of less than 10ha—7m above ground level (existing), and
for a landholding that has an area of 10ha or more—10m above ground level (existing),

if the development is located on land that is identified for the purposes of an environmental planning instrument as “Land with scenic and landscape values” on a Scenic and Landscape Values Map or as “Scenic Protection Area” on a Scenic Protection Map or Scenic Protection Area Map—it must not be higher than 7m,
if the development—
is on a landholding that has an area of more than 4ha, and
is on a landholding in relation to which the natural ground at any point within 100m of the ridgeline of any hill is at least 20m lower than the ridgeline, and
is located within 100m of that ridgeline,
it must be sited on the landholding so that the highest point of the development is at least 5m below that ridgeline,
subject to paragraph (e), the footprint of a farm building must not exceed 200m2,
the footprint of all farm buildings (other than grain bunkers) on a landholding must not exceed the footprint shown in the following table—

entry.txt: Maximum footprint of all farm buildings (other than grain bunkers)
2.5% of the area of the landholding

block.txt: the development must be located at least 20m from any road boundary and have a minimum setback from any other boundary as shown in the table to this paragraph—

a farm building must be located at least 6m from any other farm building (including any farm building that is a stock holding yard, grain silo or grain bunker) on the landholding or on an adjoining landholding,
the development must be located at least 50m from a waterbody (natural),
the development must be designed by, and constructed in accordance with the specifications of, a professional engineer,
if the development is a shipping container, there must not be more than the following number of shipping containers per landholding—
for a landholding that has an area of less than 400ha—1,
for a landholding that has an area of 400ha or more—5,

the development must not penetrate any obstacle limitation surface shown on any relevant Obstacle Limitation Surface Plan that has been prepared by the operator of an aerodrome or airport operating within 2 kilometres of the proposed development and reported to the Civil Aviation Safety Authority,

despite clause 2.30(a), excavation for the purposes of structural supports may exceed a depth of 600mm, measured from ground level (existing), unless the land is identified for the purposes of an environmental planning instrument as Class 1–5 on an Acid Sulfate Soils Map.

In this clause, footprint means the area of the ground surface occupied by a building, including the walls, footings and roofing of the building, and extending to the perimeter of the foundations and other means of structural support to the building, but does not include the area of access ramps, eaves and sunshade devices.
There are other existing legislative requirements relating to the clearance of power lines, substations and Obstacle Limitation Surfaces near airport flight paths.

The consent of the appropriate roads authority is required under section 138 of the Roads Act 1993 for the carrying out of certain works in relation to roads, including the building of any crossover or creating road access.

heading.b: Stock holding yards not used for sale of stock

block.txt: The construction or installation of a farm building that is a stock holding yard that is not used for habitable purposes is development specified for this code if it—
is constructed or installed on land in Zone RU1, RU2 or RU6, and
is used for the purpose of the short-term storage or watering of stock, and
does not include or comprise a stock and sale yard, and

in the case of development that has a footprint greater than 200m2—is not carried out on unsewered land in the Sydney Drinking Water Catchment, if that development will result in a site disturbance area of more than 250m2, and
is not constructed or installed on or in a heritage item or a draft heritage item or in an environmentally sensitive area.

In this clause, footprint means the area of the ground surface occupied by a building, including the walls, footings and roofing of the building, and extending to the perimeter of the foundations and other means of structural support to the building, but does not include the area of access ramps, eaves and sunshade devices.

Stock and sale yard is defined in the Standard Instrument as a building or place that is used on a commercial basis for the purpose of offering livestock or poultry for sale and that may be used for the short-term storage and watering of stock.
The following standards are specified for that development—
a stock holding yard—
must be fenced around its perimeter, and
must not be roofed,
any fencing erected in or around the perimeter of the stock holding yard must not be higher than 4.5m above ground level (existing),
the development must be located at least 10m from any road boundary and at least 200m from any other boundary,

the development must be located at least 200m from any dwelling that is located on land on the opposite side of a road that separates the landholding on which the development is located and that other lot,
the development must be located at least 6m from any other farm building (including any farm building that is a grain silo or grain bunker) on the landholding or on an adjoining landholding,
the development must be located at least 100m from a waterbody (natural).

The consent of the appropriate roads authority is required under section 138 of the Roads Act 1993 for the carrying out of certain works in relation to roads, including the building of any crossover or creating road access.
The construction or installation of a farm building that is a grain silo or grain bunker that is not used for habitable purposes is development specified for this code if it is—
constructed or installed on land in Zone RU1, RU2 or RU6, and
used for the purpose of the storage of grain that has been produced on the landholding, and

not constructed or installed on land shown on any relevant Procedures for Air Navigation Services—Aircraft Operations Map prepared by the operator of an aerodrome or airport operating within 2 kilometres of the proposed development and for which a PANS-OPS surface is identified that may compromise the effective and on-going operation of the relevant aerodrome or airport, and

in the case of development that has a footprint greater than 200m2—not carried out on unsewered land in the Sydney Drinking Water Catchment, if that development will result in a site disturbance area of more than 250m2, and
not constructed or installed on or in a heritage item or a draft heritage item or in an environmentally sensitive area.

In this clause, footprint means the area of the ground surface occupied by a building, including the walls, footings and roofing of the building, and extending to the perimeter of the foundations and other means of structural support to the building, but does not include the area of access ramps, eaves and sunshade devices.
The following standards are specified for that development—
the development must not be constructed or installed on a landholding with an area of less than 40ha,
the development must be located at least 15m from any road boundary and at least 100m from any other boundary,
the development must be located at least 100m from any dwelling,
the development must be located at least 6m from any other farm building (including any farm building that is a stock holding yard) on the landholding or on an adjoining landholding,
the development must be located at least 50m from a waterbody (natural),
if the development—
is on a landholding in relation to which the natural ground at any point within 100m of the ridgeline of any hill is at least 20m lower than the ridgeline, and
is located within 100m of that ridgeline,
it must be sited on the landholding so that the highest point of the development is at least 5m below that ridgeline,

the development must not penetrate any obstacle limitation surface shown on any relevant Obstacle Limitation Surface Plan that has been prepared by the operator of an aerodrome or airport operating within 2 kilometres of the proposed development and reported to the Civil Aviation Safety Authority,
if the development is located within 13km of an airfield or aerodrome—the development must be adequately sealed or protected to prevent the entry of wildlife,

despite clause 2.30(a), excavation for the purposes of structural supports may exceed a depth of 600mm, measured from ground level (existing), unless the land is identified for the purposes of an environmental planning instrument as Class 1–5 on an Acid Sulfate Soils Map.
There are other existing legislative requirements relating to the clearance of power lines and Obstacle Limitation Surfaces near airport flight paths.

The consent of the appropriate roads authority is required under section 138 of the Roads Act 1993 for the carrying out of certain works in relation to roads, including the building of any crossover or creating road access.
The following additional standards are specified for that development if the development is a grain silo—
it must not be higher than—
in the case of a landholding that has an area of 40ha or more but less than 100ha—7m above ground level (existing), and
in the case of a landholding that has an area of 100ha or more—15m above ground level (existing),
it must not have a footprint greater than 200m2,
it must not have a footprint that would result in the footprint of all farm buildings (other than grain bunkers) on the landholding exceeding the footprint shown in the following table—

entry.txt: Maximum footprint of all farm buildings (other than grain bunkers)
2.5% of the area of the landholding

block.txt: if the development is located on land that is identified for the purposes of an environmental planning instrument as “Land with scenic and landscape values” on a Scenic and Landscape Values Map or as “Scenic Protection Area” on a Scenic Protection Map or Scenic Protection Area Map—it must not be higher than 7m,

it must be constructed in accordance with the Code of Practice entitled “Safety Aspects in the Design of Bulk Solids Containers Including Silos, Field Bins and Chaser Bins” as published on the website SafeWork NSW and amended from time to time,
in the case of a grain silo that is sealed—it must be designed and sealed in accordance with sections 2 and 3 of AS 2628—2010, Sealed grain-storage silos—Sealing requirements for insect control,
it must not result in more than 5 silos being erected on a landholding.

In this clause, footprint means the surface area covered by a built structure that has either a roof or a floor installed as a fixture, or both, excluding the area of access ramps, eaves, sunshade devices, hard surfaces for parking or landscaping associated with the structure.
The following additional standards are specified for that development if the development is a grain bunker—
it must not be higher than 7m above ground level (existing),
it must not have a footprint that would result in the footprint of all grain bunkers on the landholding exceeding 7,000m2,

if the development is located on land that is identified as “Land with scenic and landscape values” on a Scenic and Landscape Values Map or as “Scenic Protection Area” on a Scenic Protection Map or Scenic Protection Area Map—it must not have a footprint greater than 200m2,
any structural elements, including any wall or concrete floor slab, of the development must be constructed in accordance with the specifications of a professional engineer,
despite clause 2.30, it must not require cut or fill more than 1m below or above ground level (existing) and any cut or fill must only be carried out wholly within a 50m radius of the grain bunker,
it must not cause the redirection of the flow of any surface water or ground water or cause sediment to be transported onto an adjoining landholding,
it must be not be located over any registered easement, sewer main or water main.

In this clause, footprint means the area of the ground surface occupied by a building, including the walls, footings and roofing of the building, and extending to the perimeter of the foundations and other means of structural support to the building, excluding the area of access ramps, eaves and sunshade devices.
It is an offence to transport waste to a place other than an appropriate and lawful waste facility (see section 143 of the Protection of the Environment Operations Act 1997).

The consent of the appropriate roads authority is required under section 138 of the Roads Act 1993 for the carrying out of certain works in relation to roads, including the building of any crossover or creating road access.
Subdivision 15 of Division 1 of Part 2 contains additional requirements relating to earthworks.
The following development, if carried out on a relevant landholding, is specified for this code—
the use of land for the purposes of farm experience premises,
a change of use from farm experience premises to the previous lawful use of the land.
To be exempt development, the development must not take place—
on significantly contaminated land, or
on land declared to be a special area under the Water NSW Act 2014, or
on land identified on the Agritourism and Farm Stay Accommodation Exempt and Complying Development Map, or
in a floodway, within the meaning of the Flood Risk Management Manual.
In this clause—
relevant landholding means a landholding—
in Zone RU1 Primary Production, Zone RU2 Rural Landscape or Zone RU4 Primary Production Small Lots, or
on which development for the purposes of one of the following is permitted with or without development consent under an environmental planning instrument—
agritourism,
extensive agriculture,
intensive livestock agriculture,
intensive plant agriculture.
The following standards are specified for development referred to in clause 2.32G(1)(a)—
the development must not involve the erection of a new building,
the development must not result in a change of building classification under the Building Code of Australia, unless—
the change is from a class 5 building to a class 6 building, or vice versa, and
the building complies with all the relevant provisions of the Building Code of Australia that apply to the new use,
the development must not involve the use of more than 200m2 of the footprint of an existing building,
the total footprint of all buildings used for the purposes of farm experience premises and farm gate premises on the landholding must be no more than 500m2,
a building used for the purposes of farm experience premises must not be located within—
50m of a property boundary or waterway, or
250m of residential accommodation on neighbouring land, or
250m of a property boundary for land used for the purposes of one of the following—
forestry,
intensive livestock agriculture,
intensive plant agriculture,
mines,
extractive industries,
rail lines,
rural industries,
the activities visitors participate in must not be conducted within the areas referred to in paragraph (e)(ii) and (iii),
notice of the following must be given, at least 1 week before the premises open to visitors, to neighbours likely to be affected by the development—
the location of the premises,
the date on which the premises will open to visitors,
the opening hours of the premises,

for premises located within 1km of residential accommodation or another building on neighbouring land, including a stable, stock yard or poultry shed, used to house animals—the development must not involve amplified noise,

the premises must not be open to visitors, excluding visitors participating in farm tours, horse riding tours and school groups, for more than 52 days each year, including no more than 4 events held on a Friday or Saturday after 6pm that involve amplified noise,
the premises must not be open to visitors outside the following hours—
on Sundays, Mondays, Tuesdays, Wednesdays, Thursdays or public holidays—8am to 6pm,
on Fridays and Saturdays—8am to midnight,

the number of visitors, excluding visitors participating in farm tours, horse riding tours and school groups, to all farm experience premises on the landholding at any one time must not be more than 50,

the total number of visitors, excluding visitors participating in fruit and produce picking, farm tours, horse riding tours and school groups, to all farm experience premises and farm gate premises on the landholding at any one time must not be more than 100,
a tent or marquee erected at the premises is not required to comply with clause 2.118(a)–(c), (l), (m) or (o),
an evacuation diagram displaying the following must be located in a prominent position at or near the premises—
directions to facilitate the safe evacuation of people from the site,
contact details for emergency services, including for a bush fire, flood or other natural disaster,
vehicular or pedestrian access to the premises must not be directly from a freeway, highway or tollway within the meaning of the Roads Act 1993,
an existing vehicular access point to a public road must comply with the lesser of—
a clear sight distance for vehicles leaving the premises of at least 300m, or
the minimum car stopping sight distances set out in the Guide to Road Design Part 3: Geometric Design, Table 5.5, published by Austroads on 26 February 2021,
vehicles must be able to enter and exit the landholding in a forward direction,
car parking spaces must be located wholly within the boundaries of the landholding,
waste generated as a result of the development must be disposed of—
using a sewage reticulation system connected to the landholding, or
using a system of sewage management for which the approval of the council has been obtained under the Local Government Act 1993, section 68, or
at a waste or resource management facility,
the on-site disposal of organic or putrescible waste must not have an adverse impact on the use of adjoining land,
a human waste storage facility on the landholding must be emptied using—
a sewage reticulation system connected to the landholding, or
a system of sewage management for which the approval of the council has been obtained under the Local Government Act 1993, section 68.
The standard for development referred to in clause 2.32G(1)(b) is that the development must not contravene an existing condition of the most recent development consent that applies to the land.

neighbouring land means—
adjacent land outside the landholding, or
land outside the landholding that is separated from the landholding by a road.

heading.b: Development standards—change of use to, or use of manufactured home for, farm stay accommodation

block.txt: The following standards are specified for development referred to in clause 2.32K(1)(a)—
for a change of use from residential accommodation—the existing building must have been lawfully erected,
for the use of a manufactured home—the manufactured home must have been lawfully constructed,
the development must not contravene an existing condition of the most recent development consent that applies to the landholding,
the number of buildings and manufactured homes used for the purposes of farm stay accommodation on the landholding must be no more than 6,
the number of guests, not including guests under 12 years of age, accommodated in the building or manufactured home at any one time must not be more than—

an evacuation diagram displaying the following must be located in a prominent position at or near the accommodation—
directions to facilitate the safe evacuation of people from the site,
contact details for emergency services, including for a bush fire, flood or other natural disaster,

vehicles must be able to enter and exit the landholding in a forward direction,
car parking spaces must be located wholly within the boundaries of the landholding,
waste generated as a result of the development must be disposed of—
using a sewage reticulation system connected to the landholding, or
using a system of sewage management for which the approval of the council has been obtained under the Local Government Act 1993, section 68, or
at a waste or resource management facility,
the on-site disposal of organic or putrescible waste must not have an adverse impact on the use of adjoining land.

heading.b: Development standards—change of use to residential accommodation

block.txt: The following standards are specified for development referred to in clause 2.32K(1)(b)—
the former use must have been a lawful use,
the development must not contravene an existing condition of the most recent development consent that applies to the landholding.

heading.b: Development standards—use of land for campervans, caravans and temporary shelters

block.txt: The following standards are specified for development referred to in clause 2.32K(1)(c)—
the development must not take place on significantly contaminated land,
the landholding must have an area of at least 15ha,

the number of campervans, caravans and other similar moveable dwellings, not including tents, annexes or other similar portable and lightweight temporary shelters, used for the purposes of farm stay accommodation on the landholding must be no more than 6,
the height of each moveable dwelling must be no more than 4.5m above ground level (existing),
the moveable dwellings must not be installed or placed within—
6m of—
a building on the landholding, or
another moveable dwelling, other than a tent or other similar portable and lightweight temporary shelter, on the landholding, or
50m of a property boundary or waterway, or
250m of residential accommodation on—
adjacent land outside the landholding, or
land outside the landholding that is separated from the landholding by a road, or
250m of a property boundary for land used for the purposes of one of the following—
forestry,
intensive livestock agriculture,
intensive plant agriculture,
mines,
extractive industries,
rail lines,
rural industries,
the gross floor area of a part of an existing building used to provide communal amenities or facilities to guests must be no more than 25m2,
the number of guests accommodated in moveable dwellings on the landholding at any one time must not be more than 20,
each guest must not stay on the landholding for more than 21 consecutive days,
an evacuation diagram displaying the following must be located in a prominent position on the site—
directions to facilitate the safe evacuation of people from the site,
contact details for emergency services, including for a bush fire, flood or other natural disaster,
vehicular or pedestrian access to the accommodation must not be directly from a freeway, highway or tollway within the meaning of the Roads Act 1993,
an existing vehicular access point to a public road must comply with the lesser of—
a clear sight distance for vehicles leaving the premises of at least 300m, or
the minimum car stopping sight distances set out in the Guide to Road Design Part 3: Geometric Design, Table 5.5, published by Austroads on 26 February 2021,
vehicles must be able to enter and exit the landholding in a forward direction,
car parking spaces must be located wholly within the boundaries of the landholding,
waste generated as a result of the development must be disposed of—
using a sewage reticulation system connected to the landholding, or
using a system of sewage management for which the approval of the council has been obtained under the Local Government Act 1993, section 68, or
at a waste or resource management facility,
the on-site disposal of organic or putrescible waste must not have an adverse impact on the use of adjoining land,
if there are no human waste storage facilities on the landholding as part of communal amenities or facilities, each moveable dwelling must contain a human waste storage facility,
a human waste storage facility on the landholding must be emptied using—
a sewage reticulation system connected to the landholding, or
a system of sewage management for which the approval of the council has been obtained under the Local Government Act 1993, section 68 located on the landholding or off-site.

heading.b: Development standards—decks, slabs and other platforms

block.txt: The following standards are specified for development referred to in clause 2.32K(1)(d)—
the development must not be carried out on significantly contaminated land,
the number of platforms constructed or installed on the landholding must be no more than—
1 per 5ha, and
6 in total,
the platform must have an area of no more than 25m2,
the height of the platform must be no more than 1m above ground level (existing),
the platform must not be constructed or installed within—
50m of a property boundary or waterway, or
250m of residential accommodation on—
adjacent land outside the landholding, or
land outside the landholding that is separated from the landholding by a road, or
250m of a property boundary for land used for the purposes of one of the following—
forestry,
intensive livestock agriculture,
intensive plant agriculture,
mines,
extractive industries,
rail lines,
rural industries,
a shelter installed on the platform must have an area of no more than 25m2,
a shelter installed on the platform must be no more than 4m tall.

heading.b: Fences (certain residential zones and Zone RU5)

content.txt: pt 2, div 1, sdiv 17, hdg: Subst 2017 (270), Sch 1 [12].

block.txt: The construction or installation of a fence on land within Zone R1, R2, R3, R4 or RU5 is development specified for this code if it is not constructed or installed—
on a lot, or along a common boundary of a lot, that contains a heritage item or a draft heritage item, or
along the boundary of, or within the setback area of, a primary or secondary road within a heritage conservation area or draft heritage conservation area, or
on a flood control lot, or
on land that is identified as being in a foreshore area.
If the fence is a dividing fence, the Dividing Fences Act 1991 also applies.
The standards specified for development specified in clause 2.33 are that the development must—
not be higher than 1.8m above ground level (existing), and
not be of masonry construction to a height that is more than 1.2m above ground level (existing), and
if it includes an entrance gate—not have a gate that opens outwards, and

if it is located in a core koala habitat or potential koala habitat within the meaning of State Environmental Planning Policy No 44—Koala Habitat Protection or in a movement corridor used by koalas—be constructed or installed in accordance with any relevant council policy or guideline under that Policy, and
if it is located on bush fire prone land—be constructed of non-combustible materials or hardwood, and
if it is constructed of metal components—be of low reflective, factory pre-coloured materials, and
not be an electrical fence or use barbed wire.
Despite subclause (1), any fence located along the boundary of, or within the setback area to, a primary or secondary road must—
not be more than 1.2m above ground level (existing), and

be open for at least 20% of the area of the fence that is more than 400mm above ground level (existing), with any individual solid element of the fence above this height being no more than 350mm in width with a minimum aperture of 25mm.

If a lot has a frontage to a secondary road or roads, subclause (2) only applies to 50% of the length of all contiguous secondary road boundaries, measured from the corner with the primary road boundary.
Subclause (2)(b) does not apply to the part of the fence along the side boundary and within the setback area to the primary road.
Despite subclauses (1) and (2), if the fence is erected on a sloping site and stepped to accommodate the fall in the land—
a fence that is required to be not more than 1.2m above ground level (existing), must not be more than 1.5m above ground level (existing) at each step, and
a fence that is required to be not more than 1.8m above ground level (existing), must not be more than 2.2m above ground level (existing) at each step.

heading.b: Fences for swimming pools (certain residential zones and Zone RU5)

block.txt: The construction or installation of a fence on land within Zone R1, R2, R3, R4 or RU5 is development specified for this code if it forms a barrier to a swimming pool.
The standards specified for that development are that the development must comply with the requirements of the Swimming Pools Act 1992.

heading.b: Fences (certain rural zones, environment protection zones and Zone R5)

content.txt: pt 2, div 1, sdiv 18, hdg: Subst 2017 (270), Sch 1 [16].

block.txt: The construction or installation of a fence on land within Zone RU1, RU2, RU3, RU4 or RU6, a conservation zone or Zone R5 is development specified for this code if it is not constructed or installed—
on a lot, or along a common boundary of a lot, that contains a heritage item or a draft heritage item, or
along the boundary of, or within the setback area of, a primary or secondary road within a heritage conservation area or draft heritage conservation area.
If the fence is a dividing fence, the Dividing Fences Act 1991 also applies.
The standards specified for that development are that the development must—
not be higher than 1.8m above ground level (existing), and
not include any masonry construction that extends more than 3m from either side of the entrance to the property from the primary road, and
be constructed using post and wire or post and rail, and
if it includes an entrance gate—not have a gate that opens outwards, and

if it is located in a core koala habitat or potential koala habitat within the meaning of State Environmental Planning Policy No 44—Koala Habitat Protection or in a movement corridor used by koalas—be constructed or installed in accordance with any relevant council policy or guideline under that Policy, and
if it is located on bush fire prone land—be constructed of non-combustible materials or hardwood, and
if it is constructed of metal components—be of low reflective, factory pre-coloured materials, and
if it is electrical fencing—be constructed in accordance with AS/NZS 3014:2003, Electrical installations – Electric fences, and
if it is constructed or installed on a flood control lot—not redirect or interrupt the flow of surface or ground water on that lot.
Despite subclause (1), if the fence is erected on a sloping site and stepped to accommodate the fall in the land the fence may be not more than 2.2m above ground level (existing) at each step.

heading.b: Fences (business, employment, mixed use and industrial zones and Zones SP5 and W4)

block.txt: The construction or installation of a fence within a business, employment, mixed use or industrial zone or Zone SP5 or W4 is development specified for this code if it is not constructed or installed—
on a lot, or along a common boundary of a lot, that contains a heritage item or a draft heritage item, or
along the boundary of, or within the setback area of, a primary or secondary road within Zone E1, E2, E3, MU1, SP5 or W4, or
on a flood control lot, or
on land that is identified as being in a foreshore area.
If the fence is a dividing fence, the Dividing Fences Act 1991 also applies.
The standards specified for that development are that the development must—
not be higher than 3m above ground level (existing), and
not be of masonry construction to a height that is more than 1.2m above ground level (existing), and
if it includes an entrance gate—not have a gate that opens outwards, and

if it is located in a core koala habitat or potential koala habitat within the meaning of State Environmental Planning Policy No 44—Koala Habitat Protection or in a movement corridor used by koalas—be constructed or installed in accordance with any relevant council policy or guideline under that Policy, and
if it is located on bush fire prone land—be constructed of non-combustible materials or hardwood, and
if it is constructed of metal components—be of low reflective, factory pre-coloured materials, and
not be an electrical fence or use barbed wire.
Despite subclause (1)—

any fence located along the boundary of a site that adjoins land within a residential zone must be open for at least 75% of the area of the fence that is more than 1.8m above ground level (existing), and
any fence located on the boundary of, or within the setback area of, a road must be open for at least 75% of the area of the fence that is more than 1.2m above ground level (existing).
The construction or installation of a free-standing flagpole is development specified for this code.
The standards specified for that development are that the development must—
be not higher than 6m above ground level (existing), and
not have a diameter of more than 90mm, and
be located at least 3m from each side and rear boundary.
There must not be more than 1 development per lot.
Any flag flown from the development must not have an area of more than 2.5m2 and must not be used for advertising.
The use of a footway or public open space within the meaning of the Roads Act 1993 as an outdoor dining area associated with lawful food and drink premises is development specified for this code.
The standards specified for that development are that the development must—
be carried out in accordance with an approval granted under section 125 of the Roads Act 1993, including in accordance with any hours of operation to which the approval is subject, and
be carried out in accordance with any approval granted under section 68 of the Local Government Act 1993, and
not be under an awning, unless the awning complies with the requirements set out in the Building Code of Australia, Volume 1, B1P1 and B1P2.

The use of public land or private land as an outdoor dining area is development specified for this code if the use is associated with lawful food and drink premises or artisan food and drink industries.
To be exempt development, the development must not—
be carried out on land—
in a conservation zone or in Zone E5 Heavy Industrial, or
in a place of Aboriginal heritage significance identified in a local environmental plan, or
be associated with a registered club.
This Subdivision does not apply to development to which Subdivision 20A applies.
In this clause—
public land has the same meaning as in the Local Government Act 1993 and includes Crown land within the meaning of the Crown Land Management Act 2016.
The standards specified for the development are—
the development—
must not be located on a rooftop of a building, and
must not cause offensive noise, within the meaning of the Protection of the Environment Operations Act 1997, or other nuisance that affects adjoining owners, and

must not contravene an existing condition of the most recent development consent, other than a complying development certificate, that applies to the associated premises relating to hours of operation, maximum capacity of patrons, waste management, food safety and pollution control, and
must not restrict vehicular or pedestrian access to or from, or entry to a building on, the land on which the development is located, and
must not reduce the existing access to the associated premises, or car parking spaces provided for the associated premises, for people with a disability, and
if carried out on land otherwise used for the purposes of a car park—must be designed to ensure pedestrian and patron safety, and
if located at ground level (existing)—must provide a direct exit from the outdoor dining area to open space or a road, and
must not be under an awning, unless the awning complies with the requirements set out in the Building Code of Australia, Volume 1, B1P1 and B1P2, and
at the end of the use the land must, as far as practicable, be restored to the condition in which it was before the commencement of the use.

Other legal requirements for the consent of the owner of the land and for approvals, licences, permits and authorities still apply. This includes, for example, a requirement for an approval under the Local Government Act 1993, section 68.
In this clause—
associated premises means the food and drink premises or artisan food and drink industries with which the development is associated.
The use of the premises of a registered club as an outdoor dining area associated with lawful food and drink premises is development specified for this code if the premises are located on—
community land within the meaning of the Local Government Act 1993, or
private land.
To be exempt development, the development must not be carried out on land—
in a conservation zone, or
in a place of Aboriginal heritage significance identified in a local environmental plan.
The standards specified for the development are—
the development—
must not be located on a rooftop of a building, and
must not cause offensive noise, within the meaning of the Protection of the Environment Operations Act 1997, or other nuisance that affects adjoining owners, and

must not contravene an existing condition of the most recent development consent, other than a complying development certificate, that applies to the registered club or the food and drink premises, other than in relation to car parking spaces, and
must not restrict vehicular or pedestrian access to or from, or entry to a building on, the land on which the development is located, and
must not reduce the existing access to the registered club, or car parking spaces provided for the registered club, for people with a disability, and
if carried out on land otherwise used for the purposes of a car park—must be designed to ensure pedestrian and patron safety, and
if located at ground level (existing)—must provide a direct exit from the outdoor dining area to open space or a road, and
must not be under an awning, unless the awning complies with the requirements set out in the Building Code of Australia, Volume 1, B1P1 and B1P2, and
at the end of the use the land must, as far as practicable, be restored to the condition in which it was before the commencement of the use.

Other legal requirements for the consent of the owner of the land and for approvals, licences, permits and authorities still apply. This includes, for example, a requirement for an approval under the Local Government Act 1993, section 68.
The construction or installation of a fowl or poultry house is development specified for this code if it is—
constructed or installed on land in a residential or rural zone, and
not constructed or installed on or in a heritage item or a draft heritage item, and
not constructed or installed on land in a foreshore area.
The standards specified for that development are that the development must—
if the development is constructed or installed on land in Zone R1, R2, R3, R4, R5 or RU5—
be not higher than 3m above ground level (existing), and
not have a floor area of more than 15m2, and
be located in the rear yard, and
for development on land in Zone R5—not house more than 10 fowl or poultry, and
for development on any other land—not house more than 5 fowl or poultry and not house any roosters, and
if the development is constructed or installed on land in Zone RU1, RU2, RU3, RU4 or RU6—
be not higher than 7m above ground level (existing), and
not have a floor area of more than 50m2, and
be located at least 3m from each lot boundary, and
if it houses fowls (including guinea fowls) only—be located at least 4.5m from any dwelling, public hall, school or premises used for the manufacture, preparation, sale or storage of food, and
if it houses other types of poultry—be located at least 30m from any dwelling, public hall, school or premises used for the manufacture, preparation, sale or storage of food, and
be enclosed to prevent the escape of poultry, and
be constructed or installed so that roofwater is disposed of without causing a nuisance to adjoining owners, and
to the extent it is comprised of metal components—be constructed of low reflective, factory pre-coloured materials if it is located on land in a residential zone, and
if it is located on bush fire prone land and is less than 5m from a dwelling—be constructed of non-combustible material, and
if it is constructed or installed in a heritage conservation area or a draft heritage conservation area—be located in the rear yard.
There must not be more than 1 development per lot.

The construction or installation of an above ground fuel tank or gas storage facility for agricultural activity is development specified for this code if it is constructed or installed on a lot in a rural zone that is larger than 2ha and is not constructed or installed in an environmentally sensitive area.
The standards specified for that development are that the development must—
not have a capacity of more than—
for a fuel tank—5,000 L, or
for a gas tank—1,000 L, and
be located at least 20m from the primary road frontage of the lot and at least 10m from each other lot boundary, and
be bunded with the capacity to contain at least 110% of the capacity of the tank, and

if a fuel tank—be constructed of prefabricated metal, be freestanding and installed in accordance with the requirements of AS 1940:2017, The storage and handling of flammable and combustible liquids, and
if a gas tank—be designed and constructed in accordance with the requirements of AS/NZS 1596:2014, The storage and handling of LP Gas by a professional engineer, and
not be used for advertising, and
be located at least 1m from any registered easement, sewer main or water main.
Other existing legislative requirements still apply in relation to work place health and safety issues.
The construction or installation of a garbage bin storage enclosure is development specified for this code if it is not carried out on land in a foreshore area.
The standards specified for that development are that the development must—
be for a dwelling house only, and
be located at least 1m behind the building line of any road frontage, and
be located at least 450mm from each side and rear boundary, and
if it is constructed of metal components—be of low reflective, factory pre-coloured materials, and
if it is located on bush fire prone land and is less than 5m from a dwelling—be constructed of non-combustible material, and
if it is constructed or installed on or in a heritage item or a draft heritage item or in a heritage conservation area or a draft heritage conservation area—be located in the rear yard, and
be located at least 1m from any registered easement.
There must not be more than 1 development per lot.

heading.b: Home businesses, home industries and home occupations

block.txt: A home business, a home industry or a home occupation that does not involve the manufacture of food products or skin penetration procedures is development specified for this code.
The standards specified for this development are that the development must—
not involve a change of building use, and
if the development is on land to which a local environmental plan made under section 3.20 of the Act applies, comply with the applicable standards specified under clause 5.4(2) and (3) of that plan.
The elements that must comprise this development are specified in the definition of home business, home industry or home occupation the Standard Instrument.
Under the Building Code of Australia, a change of building use involving a floor area greater than 10% of the floor area of a building would cause the building to contravene the development standard.
The construction or installation of a hot water heater or a hot water storage tank is development specified for this code.
The standards specified for that development are that the development must—
not be a solar hot water system, and
if it uses a heat pump water heater, be designed so as not to operate—
during peak time—at a noise level that is more than 5 dB(A) above the ambient background noise level measured at any property boundary, or
during off peak time—at a noise level that is audible in habitable rooms of adjoining residences, and
if constructed or installed externally and on or in a heritage item or a draft heritage item or in a heritage conservation area or a draft heritage conservation area—
not be located on a roof, and
be located in the rear yard.
See note relating to Solar Hot Water Systems.
For further information about noise control in relation to heat pump water heaters, see the NSW Government’s Noise Guide for Local Government published in 2010 (ISBN 978 1 74232 942 0).

The operation of premises in Zone E1, E2, E3, E4, E5, MU1, B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, B6, B7, B8, IN1, IN2, IN3, IN4, SP5 or W4 in accordance with an existing development consent or complying development certificate at any time outside the hours permitted by the development consent or complying development certificate is development specified for this code.

The trading on or from premises in accordance with an existing development consent or complying development certificate at the following times occurring outside the hours permitted by the development consent or complying development certificate is development specified for this code—
in Zone E1, E2, E3, B1, B2, B3, B5, B6, B7, B8, IN4, SP1, SP2, SP3, SP5 or W4—6am–10pm,
in Zone MU1 or B4—6am–7pm,
in Zone E4, E5, IN1, IN2 or IN3 for relevant premises—
until the end of 31 January 2024—24 hours a day,
from the beginning of 1 February 2024—6am–7pm,
in Zones Zone E4, E5, IN1, IN2 or IN3 for all other premises—24 hours a day.
In this clause—
relevant premises means boat building and repair facilities and vehicle body repair workshops that are located within 100m of a residential zone.
The standards specified for the development are as follows—
the development must comply with the Noise Policy,
the development must not be for purposes referred to in clause 5A.2(2),
the development must not be designated development,
the premises must not require, or be subject to, an environment protection licence under the Protection of the Environment Operations Act 1997.

The construction or installation of a landscaping structure (including a garden arch), other than a retaining wall is development specified for this code if it is not constructed or installed on or in a heritage item or a draft heritage item or on land in a foreshore area.
The standards specified for that development are that the development must—
be not higher than 2.1m above ground level (existing), and
be not wider than 1.5m, and
be located at least 900mm from each lot boundary, and
not comprise masonry construction higher than 1m from ground level (existing), and
if it is constructed or installed in a heritage conservation area or a draft heritage conservation area—be located in the rear yard.

The construction or installation of a letterbox, whether free standing or in banks, is development specified for this code if it is not constructed or installed on or in a heritage item or a draft heritage item.
The standards specified for that development are that the development must—
be not higher than 1.2m above ground level (existing), and
be visible from the road alignment, and
have appropriate numbering that is visible from the road alignment.

heading.b: Maintenance of buildings in draft heritage conservation areas

block.txt: The maintenance of a building in a draft heritage conservation area comprising only—
painting, plastering, cement rendering, or cladding, or
the repair or replacement of an external window, glazing areas or a door (other than those on bush fire prone land), or
the repair or replacement of a non-structural wall or roof cladding, or
the repair or replacement of a balustrade,
is development specified for this code if it is not constructed or installed on or in, or in relation to, a heritage item or draft heritage item.
The standards specified for that development are that the development must—
reproduce the existing materials, finish and design of the building so as not to alter its appearance, and
not result in an increase of floor area or alter the layout of the building, and
not comprise the making of, or an alteration to the size of, any opening in a wall or roof, such as a doorway, window or skylight, and
not reduce the existing fire resistance level of a wall or roof, and
if located on bush fire prone land—
be adequately sealed or protected to prevent the entry of embers, and
use equivalent or improved quality materials, and
not affect any existing fire resisting components of the building, and
if the development involves cladding—
not be carried out on any building other than a 1 or 2 storey dwelling house, attached development or detached development, and
not involve the use of external combustible cladding, and
not affect the means of egress from the building in an emergency.
A minor internal building alteration for the replacement or renovation of—
a doorway, wall, ceiling or floor lining, or
a deteriorated frame member, including stairs and stairwells, or
a bathroom or kitchen, or
a built in fixture such as a vanity, a cupboard or a wardrobe, or
an existing sanitary fixture, such as a grease trap or the like, or
shelving or racking, or
a partition, work station or counter,
is development specified for this code if it is not constructed or installed on or in a heritage item or a draft heritage item.
The installation of new or replacement insulation material in the ceiling, floor or wall of a building is development specified for this code.

A minor internal building alteration consisting of other remedial work necessary to repair or maintain a building is development specified for this code if the work is not carried out on or in a heritage item or a draft heritage item.
The standards specified for that development are that the development must—
not be an alteration to a food preparation area in food and drink premises, and
if it is the replacement or renovation of a deteriorated frame member—be of equivalent or improved quality materials, and
not include a change to the configuration of a room, whether by removal of an existing wall, partition or other means, and
not cause reduced window arrangements for light and ventilation needs, reduce the size of a doorway or involve the enclosure of an open area, and
not affect the load bearing capacity (whether vertical or horizontal) of a building, and
not include a change to the fire resisting components of, or interfere with the entry to, or exit from, or the fire safety measures contained within, a building, and
if it is the installation of a partition, work station or counter—
comply with the requirements set out in the Building Code of Australia, Volume 1, D2D5, and
if located beneath a fire sprinkler—not be higher than 1.5m, and
if it is the installation of new or replacement insulation material in a dwelling, it must be in accordance with the ABCB Housing Provisions Standard, Part 13.2, and

not affect an existing awning, or more than 25% of the gross floor area of an existing building to which an awning is attached, unless the awning complies with the requirements set out in the Building Code of Australia, Volume 1, B1P1 and B1P2.
In this clause—
ABCB Housing Provisions Standard means the Housing Provisions Standard published by the Australian Building Codes Board in 2022.
A minor external non-structural building alteration, such as the following—
painting, plastering, cement rendering, cladding, attaching fittings or decorative work,
the replacement of an external window, glazing areas or a door (other than those on bush fire prone land),
the repair to or replacement of a non-structural wall or roof cladding,
the installation of a security screen or grill to a door or window or a security door,
the repair to or replacement of a balustrade,
restumping or repairing structure foundations without increasing the height of the structure,
other remedial work necessary to repair or maintain the building,

is development specified for this code if it is not constructed or installed on or in a heritage item or a draft heritage item or in a heritage conservation area or a draft heritage conservation area.
The standards specified for that development are that the development must—
not comprise the making of, or an alteration to the size of, any opening in a wall or roof, such as a doorway, window or skylight, and
not reduce the existing fire resistance level of a wall or roof, and
if located on bush fire prone land—
be adequately sealed or protected to prevent the entry of embers, and
use equivalent or improved quality materials, and
not affect any existing fire resisting components of the building, and
if the development involves cladding or is attaching fittings or decorative work—
not be carried out on any building other than a 1 or 2 storey dwelling house, attached development or detached development, and
not involve the use of external combustible cladding, and
not affect the means of egress from the building in an emergency, and
if it is the installation of a security screen or grill to a door or window or a security door—
be for the purposes of a dwelling, or
be for any other purpose so long as—
the screen or grill is installed for a door or window that is situated at least 5m from the boundary of any road, or
the security door is installed at least 5m from the boundary of any road, and
not be under an awning, unless the awning complies with the requirements set out in the Building Code of Australia, Volume 1, B1P1 and B1P2.
See separate entry for skylights.
The carrying out of the retail sale of food, drinks and related products on land from a mobile outlet such as a food truck, van, cart or other similar vehicle is development specified for this code.
The standards specified for that development are that the development must—

have the consent of the owner of the land on which the development is carried out or, if a council or public authority has the control and management of the land, the consent, in writing, of the council or public authority, and
not restrict any vehicular or pedestrian access to or from the land or entry to any building on the land, and
not obstruct the operation of, or access to, any utility services on the land or on adjacent land, and
not be located within the canopy of, or result in damage to, any tree growing on the land or on adjacent land, and
not result in any damage to public property on the land or on adjacent land, and
if carried out on land in a residential zone—only be carried out between 7am and 7pm, and
if carried out on land immediately adjacent to a residential zone—only be carried out between 7am and 10pm, and
if located on a public place—have any approval required under section 68 of the Local Government Act 1993, and
if located on private land—be limited to 1 development on that land and not contravene any conditions of a development consent for any other use carried out on the land.

A registrable vehicle within the meaning of the Road Transport (Vehicle Registration) Regulation 2007, or a cart, bicycle cart or the like must operate in accordance with the Guidelines for mobile food vending vehicles (NSW/FA/F1055/1302) published by the NSW Food Authority in February 2013, and any requirements of the Food Act 2003.
The construction or installation of a pathway or paving, including any paving of a deck, pergola, patio or terrace is development specified for this code.
Subclause (1) does not include any paving of a driveway, hard stand space or turning or parking area to be used by vehicles for any purpose, including the delivery or loading of goods.
The standards specified for that development are that the development must—
be constructed or installed so that any surface water or runoff is disposed of by a drainage system that is connected to the existing stormwater drainage system, and
if constructed or installed in a residential zone or Zone RU5—
not require cut or fill more than 600mm below or above ground level (existing), and
not result in the total area of all paved areas (including driveways and hard stand spaces) on the lot exceeding 15% of the area of the lot or 150m2, whichever is the lesser, and
if constructed or installed in a residential zone—
on a lot that has a width at the front building line of not more than 18m—have at least 25% of the area forward of the building line as landscaped area, and
on a lot that has a width at the front building line of more than 18m—have at least 50% of the area forward of the building line as landscaped area, and
if constructed or installed in a zone (other than a residential zone or Zone RU5)—
not require cut or fill more than 1m below or above ground level (existing), and
not reduce any required landscaped area along a boundary with a road or an adjoining lot on which a dwelling is located.
The Standard Instrument defines landscaped area as a part of a site used for growing plants, grasses and trees, but not including any building, structure or hard paved area.
The construction or installation of playground equipment is development specified for this code.
In this Subdivision—
playground equipment includes slides, swings and trampolines, but does not include skateboard ramps.
The standards specified for that development are that the development must—
be not higher than 2.5m above ground level (existing), and
be located at least 450mm from each side and rear boundary, and
if it is on land in Zone R1, R2, R3 or R4—be located in the rear yard.

heading.b: Portable swimming pools and spas and child-resistant barriers

block.txt: The construction or installation of a portable swimming pool or spa or a child-resistant barrier that is required under the Swimming Pools Act 1992 is development specified for this code if it is not constructed or installed on or in a heritage item or a draft heritage item or on land in a foreshore area.
The standards specified for that development, if it is the construction or installation of a portable swimming pool or spa, are that the development must—
be for residential uses only, and
be located in the rear yard, and
be located at least 1m from each lot boundary, and
not exceed 2,000 L in capacity, and
not require structural work for installation, and
not impact on the structural stability of any building.
A child-resistant barrier must be constructed or installed in accordance with the requirements of the Swimming Pools Act 1992.

The construction or installation of a privacy screen that is not attached to a boundary fence or retaining wall is development specified for this code if it is not constructed or installed on land in a foreshore area.
The standards specified for that development are that the development must—
if attached to a balcony, deck, patio, terrace or verandah—be at least 1.7m, but not more than 2.2m, above the finished floor level of that development, and
if located on the ground—be not higher than 2.5m above ground level (existing), and
be not longer than 5m, and
be located at least 900mm from each lot boundary, and
be located in the rear yard.
There must not be more than 2 such privacy screens erected under this clause on any lot.

The construction or installation of a rainwater tank above ground is development specified for this code if it is not constructed or installed on land in a foreshore area or in an environmentally sensitive area.
The standards specified for that development are that the development must—
if it is on land other than land in Zone RU1, RU2, RU3, RU4, RU6, R5, E2, E3 or E4—
not have a capacity more than 10,000 L, and
be located behind the building line of any road frontage, and
not rest on the footings of an existing building for support, and
not require cut and fill of more than 1m below or above ground level (existing), and
be fitted with a screened rain head designed to ensure self-cleaning and prevent leaf litter entering into the water tank, and
be fitted with a first-flush device incorporating an automatic resetting valve that causes initial run-off rainwater to bypass the tank, and
be constructed or installed with inlets and outlets designed to prevent mosquitoes breeding in it, and
have its overflow connected to an existing stormwater drainage system that does not discharge to an adjoining property, or cause a nuisance to adjoining owners, and
have a sign affixed to it with a statement to the effect that the water in the tank is rainwater, and
if it is constructed or installed on or in a heritage item or a draft heritage item—be located in the rear yard.
Pumps attached to the development must be housed in an enclosure that is soundproofed.

If reticulated water is provided to the lot, the development must not be interconnected with any system supplying drinking water to the lot unless it complies with the relevant water authority’s requirements.
The construction or installation of a rainwater tank below ground is development specified for this code if—
it is constructed or installed on land in Zone RU1, RU2, RU3, RU4, RU6 or R5, and
it is not constructed or installed on land that is identified on an Acid Sulfate Map as being Class 1–5, and
it is not constructed or installed on land that is identified as an environmentally sensitive area.
The standards specified for that development are that the development must—
be fitted with a first-flush device that causes initial run-off rainwater to bypass the tank, and
have a sign affixed to it stating the water in it is rainwater, and
be constructed or installed to prevent mosquitoes breeding in it, and
have its overflow connected to an existing stormwater drainage system that does not discharge to an adjoining property, or cause a nuisance to adjoining owners, and
if it is constructed or installed on or in a heritage item or a draft heritage item—be located in the rear yard.
Pumps attached to the development must be housed in an enclosure that is soundproofed.

If reticulated water is provided to the lot, the development must not be interconnected with any system supplying drinking water to the lot unless it complies with the relevant water authority’s requirements.
Development for the purposes of a single roadside stall is development specified for this code if carried out on a landholding that is—
privately owned, and
in Zone RU1, RU2 or RU4, and
not adjacent to a freeway, highway or tollway within the meaning of the Roads Act 1993, and
not in a floodway within the meaning of the Flood Risk Management Manual.
The following standards are specified for the development—
the gross floor area of the stall must be no more than 9m2,
for a stall located on bush fire prone land—the stall must not be erected or installed within 6m of residential accommodation,
an evacuation diagram displaying the following must be located in a prominent position on or near the stall—
directions to facilitate the safe evacuation of people from the site,
contact details for emergency services, including for a bush fire, flood or other natural disaster,
an existing vehicular access point to a public road must comply with the lesser of—
a clear sight distance for vehicles leaving the premises of at least 300m, or
the minimum car stopping sight distances set out in the Guide to Road Design Part 3: Geometric Design, Table 5.5, published by Austroads on 26 February 2021,
vehicles must be able to enter and exit the landholding in a forward direction,
car parking spaces must be located—
on a road verge, or
wholly within the boundaries of the landholding,
car parking spaces may only be located on a road verge if—
the verge has a maximum average gradient of 1:20, and
there is no vegetation on the verge, and
the parking spaces are at least 3m from a lane of a road, and
the verge is adjacent to a road with a maximum speed limit of 60km/hr or less,
waste generated as a result of the development must be disposed of—
using a sewage reticulation system connected to the landholding, or
using a system of sewage management for which the approval of the council has been obtained under the Local Government Act 1993, section 68, or
at a waste or resource management facility,
the on-site disposal of organic or putrescible waste must not have an adverse impact on the use of adjoining land.
The installation of a roller shutter door on a boundary adjoining a lane is development specified for this code.
The standards specified for that development are that the development must—
be associated with a hard stand, garage or carport, and
have a width of not greater than 4.5m, and
not be higher than 3m above ground level (existing), and
not encroach on the lane, and
comply with AS/NZS 2890.1:2004, Parking facilities, Part 1: Off-street car parking.

heading.b: Screen enclosures (of balconies, decks, patios, pergolas, terraces and verandahs)

block.txt: The construction or installation of a screen by attaching it to a balcony, deck, patio, pergola, terrace or verandah of a dwelling is development specified for this code if it is not constructed or installed on or in a heritage item or a draft heritage item.
The standards specified for that development are that the development must—
not have a solid enclosing wall, and
if it encloses a structure attached to the ground level of a single storey dwelling or the upper level of a two storey dwelling—not be higher than the roof gutter line, and
if it encloses a structure attached to the ground level of a two storey dwelling—not be higher than 3m above the floor level of the structure it is enclosing, and
if it encloses a freestanding structure—not be higher than 3m above the floor level of the structure it is enclosing, and
if it encloses a structure attached to the upper level of a two storey dwelling—not enclose an area of more than 9m2, and
be located behind the building line of any road frontage, and
be located at least 900mm from each lot boundary, and
to the extent it is comprised of metal components—be constructed of low reflective, factory pre-coloured materials, and
if it is connected to a fascia—be connected in accordance with a professional engineer’s specifications, and
if it is not located on bush fire prone land—have at least two-thirds of its perimeter comprising open screen mesh material, and

if it is located on bush fire prone land—cover all openings, including any sub-floor areas, operable windows, vents and eaves, and be made of a non-corrosive metal material with a maximum aperture of 2mm, and
if it is located on bush fire prone land and is less than 5m from a dwelling—be constructed of non-combustible material, and
if it is constructed or installed in a heritage conservation area or a draft heritage conservation area—not be attached to any balcony, deck, patio, pergola, terrace or verandah that faces any road.

heading.b: Security measures for places of public worship

block.txt: The construction or installation of security measures, including bollards, fencing, lighting, security cameras, safety glass and reinforced doors, is development specified for this code.
The standards specified for the development are that the development must—
be associated with a place of public worship, and
be contained entirely within the lot on which the place of public worship is located, and
be at least 450mm from each lot boundary, other than a boundary with a road, and
if connected to a fascia—be connected in accordance with a professional engineer’s specifications, and
if located on bush fire prone land—be constructed of non-combustible material, and
if constructed or installed on a heritage item—be constructed or installed so that it can be removed without irreversibly damaging building fabric, and
not affect any existing fire resisting components of a building, and
not affect the means of evacuation from a building in an emergency, and
not be used for advertising.

heading.b: Shade structures of canvas, fabric, mesh or the like

block.txt: The construction or installation of a shade structure of canvas, fabric, mesh or the like is development specified for this code if it is not constructed or installed on land in a foreshore area.
See separate entry for awnings, blinds and canopies.
The standards specified for that development are that the development must—
not have an area more than—
if for residential uses—20m2, or
if it is constructed or installed for the purposes of a centre-based child care facility in a residential zone—40m2, or
if it is constructed or installed for the purposes of a centre-based child care facility in a zone other than a residential zone—60m2, or
if it is constructed or installed for the purposes of any other use—30m2, and
not cause the total area of all such structures on the lot to be more than 15% of the ground floor area of all buildings on the lot, and
not be higher than 3m from ground level (existing), and
be located at a distance from each lot boundary of at least—
if the development is carried out in Zone RU1, RU2, RU3, RU4, RU6 or R5—5m, or
in any other case—900mm, and
be located behind the building line of any road frontage, and
to the extent it is comprised of metal components—be constructed of low reflective, factory pre-coloured materials, and
if it is connected to a fascia—be connected in accordance with a professional engineer’s specifications, and
not interfere with the functioning of existing drainage fixtures or flow paths, and
if it is located on bush fire prone land and is less than 5m from a dwelling—be constructed of non-combustible material, and
if it is constructed or installed on or in a heritage item or a draft heritage item or in a heritage conservation area or a draft heritage conservation area—be located in the rear yard, and
if it is constructed or installed for the purposes of a centre-based child care facility—be constructed of non-combustible material.

heading.b: Shipping containers (temporary installation and use for storage purposes following a natural disaster)

block.txt: The installation and temporary use of a shipping container for storage purposes on a lot is development specified for this code if—
a building on the lot has been significantly damaged by a natural disaster, or
the lot is in an area declared by an order under the State Emergency and Rescue Management Act 1989, section 33 to be an area where a state of emergency exists.
The standards specified for that development are that the development must—
be carried out within 2 years of the natural disaster or of the declaration being made, and
be removed no more than 2 years after it is installed, and
not be used for a purpose other than storage, and
not result in more than—
1 shipping container on a lot in a residential zone or conservation zone, or
2 shipping containers on a lot in a rural, business, employment, mixed use, industrial or special purpose zone or Zone W4, and
have appropriate foundations and structural support to ensure that it is safe and stable, and
have a maximum height of 3m, and
have a maximum length of 12.5m, and
have a maximum width of 2.5m, and
be at least 1.2m clear of any 150mm diameter sewer main or 2m clear of any 225mm (or greater) diameter sewer main, and
not be installed over any easement, and
not be installed over drainage pipes or any house drainage pipelines unless access to the inspection openings is maintained at all times, and
not be on a flood control lot, and
if in a residential zone—be behind the front building line.

heading.b: Shipping containers and portable offices (temporary installation and use for existing commercial and industrial purposes)

block.txt: The installation and temporary use of a shipping container or portable office on land in a business, employment, mixed use or industrial zone or Zone RU5, SP5 or W4 is development specified for this code if the land—
is part of a lot on which a building has been significantly damaged by a bush fire, and
is in an area declared by an order under section 33 of the State Emergency and Rescue Management Act 1989 to be an area where a state of emergency in respect of bush fires exists.
The standards specified for that development are that the development must—
be carried out within 2 years of the declaration being made, and
be removed no more than 2 years after it is installed, and

not be used for a purpose other than a commercial or industrial purpose for which a building, significantly damaged by a bush fire, on the lot was lawfully used in the 12 months immediately before the building was significantly damaged by the bush fire, and
have appropriate foundations and structural support to ensure that it is safe and stable, and
if it is a shipping container—
have a maximum length of 12.5m, and
have a maximum height of 3m, and
have a maximum width of 2.5m, and
if it is a portable office—
have a maximum area of 36m2, and
have a maximum height of 3m, and
be at least 1.2m clear of any 150mm diameter sewer main or 2m clear of any 225mm (or greater) diameter sewer main, and
be located at a distance from each lot boundary of at least—
if the adjoining lot is used for a residential purpose—5m, or
if the adjoining lot is not used for a residential purpose—1m, and
not result in more than—
2 shipping containers installed on the lot, or
2 portable offices installed on the lot, or
1 shipping container and 1 portable office installed on the lot, and
not affect the means of egress from any building in an emergency, and
be installed so that roof water is disposed of without causing a nuisance to adjoining owners, and
not be installed over any easement, and
not be installed over drainage pipes or any house drainage pipelines unless access to the inspection openings is maintained at all times, and
if it contains plumbing fixtures—have those fixtures connected to an approved waste water treatment device or an approved connection to the sewer.
The Food Act 2003, and the regulations under that Act, may contain additional requirements in relation to premises used by a food business in connection with the handling of food intended for sale.
