heading.b: Other development standards for detached decks, patios, pergolas, terraces and verandahs

block.txt: The maximum finished floor level for any detached deck, patio, pergola, terrace or verandah is 600mm above ground level (existing).
Ground level (existing) has the same meaning as it has in the Standard Instrument.
A detached deck, patio, pergola, terrace or verandah must have a minimum setback from the rear boundary as shown in the following table—

heading.b: Other development standards for detached studios

block.txt: There must only be 1 detached studio on the lot at the completion of the development.
Despite clause 3.18, if a detached studio is within 900mm of a lane and is above a garage, the maximum height is 6m above ground level (existing).
The maximum gross floor area of a detached studio is shown in the following table—
A detached studio must have a minimum setback from each side and rear boundary as shown in the following table—

entry.txt: Lot width at the building line
Minimum setback from each side and rear boundary

block.txt: The rear setbacks specified in subclause (4) do not apply to a lot that only has 3 boundaries.
Despite subclause (4), a detached studio that is within 900mm of a rear lane may be built to 1 or both side boundaries if—
the lot is not a corner lot, and
the lot width measured at the building line is at least 6m, but not more than 8m, and
if there is a building wall on the adjoining lot within 900mm of that boundary—that wall is of masonry construction and does not have a window facing that boundary, and
any wall erected within 900mm of a side boundary will not contain a door, window or any other opening.
Despite subclause (4), a detached studio that is within 900mm of a rear lane may be built to 1 side boundary if—
the lot width measured at the building line is more than 8m, but not more than 12.5m, and
any building wall on the adjoining lot within 900mm of that boundary is of masonry construction and does not have a window facing that boundary, and
any wall erected within 900mm of the side boundary will not contain a door, window or any other opening.

heading.b: Maximum height of built to boundary walls

block.txt: The height of a wall erected within 900mm of a side boundary must not exceed—
3.3m above ground level (existing), or
if the height of the built to boundary wall on the adjoining lot is higher than 3.3m—the height of that wall, but not more than 4.5m, or

if the building on the adjoining lot is subject to the same complying development certificate under clause 126(4) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Regulation 2000—the height of the wall on the adjoining lot, but not more than 4.5m, or
if the wall is part of a detached studio that is above a garage—the height of the built to boundary wall on the adjoining lot, but not more than 6m.
A privacy screen must be provided for any part of a window in a detached studio that is less than 1.5m above the finished floor level of that room if—
the window faces and is less than 3m from a side or rear boundary and the room has a finished floor level more than 1m above ground level (existing), or
the window faces and is at least 3m, but not more than 6m from a side or rear boundary and the room has a finished floor level more than 3m above ground level (existing).

Boundary wall, building line, detached, dwelling house, gross floor area, heritage conservation area, lane, parallel road, primary road, privacy screen, secondary road and setback are defined in clause 1.5.
Building height and ground level (existing) have the same meanings as they have in the Standard Instrument.

heading.b: Development to which side and rear setbacks do not apply

block.txt: The side and rear setback standards specified in this Subdivision do not apply to the following—
downpipes,
driveways,
electricity or gas meters,
fascias,
fences,
gutters,
light fittings,
pathways and paving.

heading.b: Development to which side and rear setbacks do not apply if 450mm from boundary

block.txt: The side and rear setback standards specified in this Subdivision do not apply to the following if they are located at least 450mm from the relevant boundary—
aerials,
antennae,
awnings,
chimneys,
cooling or heating appliances,
eaves,
flues,
pipes,
rainwater tanks not more than 1.8m in height,
structures associated with the provision of a utility service.

heading.b: Development to which road setbacks do not apply

block.txt: The road setbacks specified in this Subdivision do not apply to the following—
driveways,
fences,
pathways and paving,
retaining walls.

heading.b: Rear boundaries with parallel roads or rear lanes

block.txt: Despite any rear setback specified in this Subdivision, if a lot has a rear boundary with a parallel road or lane, the following detached development may be erected within 3m of, or abut, the rear boundary for not more than 50% of the length of that boundary—
a cabana, cubby house, fernery, garden shed, gazebo or greenhouse,
a carport or garage,
a rainwater tank (above ground),
a shade structure or shed.

heading.b: Setbacks do not apply to existing parts of detached development

block.txt: The setback standards specified in this Subdivision do not apply to any existing parts of detached development that will remain on the lot after the complying development is carried out.
Articulation zone, boundary wall, building line, dwelling house and setback are defined in clause 1.5.
Classified road, public reserve and rainwater tank have the same meanings as they have in the Standard Instrument.
Complying development certificate has the same meaning as it has in the Act.

heading.b: Landscape development standards for detached development (other than fences and child-resistant barriers)

content.txt: pt 3, div 4, sdiv 3, hdg: Ins 2017 (269), Sch 1 [14].

block.txt: The minimum landscaped area that must be provided on a lot is shown in the following table—
Each landscaped area must have a minimum width and length of 1.5m.
The minimum landscaped area calculated in accordance with subclause (1) must be provided as follows—
if the lot width measured at the building line is 18m or less—25% of the area forward of the building line must be landscaped,
if the lot width measured at the building line is more than 18m—50% of the area forward of the building line must be landscaped,
50% of the minimum landscaped area must be located behind the building line.
The minimum area of principal private open space that must be provided on a lot is shown in the following table—

entry.txt: Lot width (measured at the building line)

block.txt: The principal private open space must—
be at least 3m wide and 3m long, and
not be steeper than 1:50 gradient.
This clause does not apply to complying development that is the alteration of, or addition to, detached development if the development does not—
increase the footprint of the detached development, or
decrease the landscaped area on the lot.
Building line and principal private open space are defined in clause 1.5.
Landscaped area has the same meaning as it has in the Standard Instrument.

heading.b: Built form development standards for swimming pools, fences and child-resistant barriers

content.txt: pt 3, div 4, sdiv 4, hdg: Ins 2017 (269), Sch 1 [14].

block.txt: A swimming pool must be for private use and associated with a dwelling house.
Water from a swimming pool must be discharged in accordance with an approval under the Local Government Act 1993 if the lot is not connected to a sewer main.
The pump must be—
housed in a soundproofed enclosure, and
located more than 450mm from each lot boundary.
See the regulations under the Protection of the Environment Operations Act 1997 for offences relating to the use of pumps on residential premises.
A heat pump water heater must be designed so as not to operate—
during peak time—at a noise level that is more than 5 dB(A) above the ambient background noise level measured at any property boundary, and
during off peak time—at a noise level that is audible in habitable rooms of adjoining residences.
Coping around a swimming pool must not be more than—
1.4m above ground level (existing), and
300mm wide if the coping is more than 600mm above ground level (existing).
Decking around a swimming pool must not be more than 600mm above ground level (existing).
A swimming pool must be located behind the building line of the dwelling house.
The swimming pool water line must have a setback of at least 1m from a side or rear boundary.
The minimum setback for a swimming pool from a secondary road is the setback of the dwelling house from the secondary road.
Despite subclauses (6) and (7), if the swimming pool is being constructed in a heritage conservation area or a draft heritage conservation area the swimming pool must be located—
behind the building line of the dwelling house that is adjacent to the rear boundary of the lot, and
no closer to each side boundary than the dwelling house.
Building line, dwelling house, heritage conservation area and setback are defined in clause 1.5.
Ground level (existing) and landscaped area have the same meanings as they have in the Standard Instrument.
A child-resistant barrier must be constructed or installed in accordance with the requirements of the Swimming Pools Act 1992.
Requirements relating to excavation for the purposes of a swimming pool are set out in clause 3.30.
A fence may be erected on a lot under this code if it is not constructed or installed—
on a lot, or along a common boundary of a lot that contains a heritage item or a draft heritage item, or
along the boundary of, or within the setback area of, a primary or secondary road within a heritage conservation area or draft heritage conservation area.
A fence erected behind the building line on a lot must—
not be higher than 1.8m above ground level (existing), and
not incorporate barbed wire in its construction or be electrified, and
if it includes an entrance gate—not have a gate that opens outward, and
if it is constructed of metal components—be of low reflective, factory pre-coloured materials, and
if it is on a sloping site and stepped to accommodate the fall in the land—be no higher than 2.2m above ground level (existing) at each step, and
be designed so as not to restrict the flow of any floodwater.
A fence erected forward of the building line on a lot must—
not be higher than 1.2m above ground level (existing), and
not incorporate barbed wire in its construction or be electrified, and
if it includes an entrance gate—not have a gate that opens outward, and
if it is constructed of metal components—be of low reflective, factory pre-coloured materials, and

be open for at least 20% of the area of the fence that is more than 400mm above ground level (existing), with any individual solid element of the fence above that height being no more than 350mm wide with a minimum aperture of 25mm, and
be designed so as not to restrict the flow of any floodwater.
Despite subclause (2)(a), any fence located in the setback area of a primary or secondary road must not be higher than 1.2m above ground level (existing).
A fence erected on bush fire prone land must be constructed of non-combustible material.

A requirement in subclause (2)(f) or (3)(f) is satisfied if a joint report by a professional engineer specialising in hydraulic engineering and a professional engineer specialising in civil engineering states that the requirement is satisfied.
Building line, primary road, secondary road and setback are defined in clause 1.5.
Ground level (existing) and heritage item have the same meanings as they have in the Standard Instrument.
Exempt development standards for fences in certain rural zones, conservation zones and Zone R5 are specified in clause 2.36.

content.txt: pt 3, div 4, sdiv 5, hdg: Ins 2017 (269), Sch 1 [14].

heading.b: Development standards for associated works including earthworks, retaining walls, drainage, protection of walls, protection of trees and conditions under complying development certificates
Earthworks, retaining walls and structural support

block.txt: Excavation for the purposes of development under this code must not exceed a maximum depth, measured from ground level (existing), of—
if located not more than 1m from any boundary—1m, and
if located more than 1m but not more than 1.5m from any boundary—2m, and
if located more than 1.5m from any boundary—3m.
Excavation for the purposes of a pier in a pier and beam foundation may exceed the maximum depth specified in subclause (1) if a professional engineer has certified the depth of the excavation.

Despite subclauses (1) and (1A), the excavation must not exceed a maximum depth, measured from ground level (existing), of 1m if the land is identified as Class 3 or 4 on an Acid Sulfate Soils Map or is within 40m of a waterbody (natural).
Fill must not exceed a maximum height, measured from ground level (existing), of—
if the fill is for the purposes of the erection or alteration of, or an addition to, a dwelling house under this code—1m, or
if the fill is for any other purpose under this code—600mm.
Despite subclause (3), the height of fill is not limited if the fill is contained—
wholly within the footprint of a dwelling house, attached development or detached development, or
by a drop edge beam.

Fill that is higher than 150mm above ground level (existing) and is not contained wholly within the footprint of a dwelling house or any attached development or detached development is limited to 50% of the landscaped area of the lot.
The ground level (finished) of the fill must not be used to measure the height of any dwelling house or any attached development or detached development under this code.
Support for earthworks more than 600mm above or below ground level (existing) must take the form of a retaining wall or other structural support that—
a professional engineer has certified as structurally sound, including in relation to (but not limited to) the ability to withstand the forces of lateral soil load, and
has been designed so as not to redirect the flow of any surface water or ground water, or cause sediment to be transported, onto an adjoining property, and
has adequate drainage lines connected to the stormwater drainage system for the site, and

does not have a total height measured vertically from the base of the retaining wall or structural support to its uppermost portion that is more than the height of the associated excavation or fill, and
is separated from any other retaining wall or structural support on the site by at least 2m, measured horizontally, and
has been installed in accordance with any manufacturer’s specifications, and
if it is an embankment or batter—has a toe or top that is more than 1m from any side or rear boundary.
Excavation, fill and ground level (existing) have the same meanings as they have in the Standard Instrument.
Fill and excavation that is not associated with a building may be exempt development under clauses 2.29 and 2.30.
All stormwater collecting as a result of the carrying out of development under this code must be directed by a gravity fed or charged system to—
a public drainage system, or
an inter-allotment drainage system, or
an on-site disposal system.
Drainage has the same meaning as it has in the Standard Instrument.

All stormwater drainage systems and connections to public drainage systems or inter-allotment drainage systems must either be approved under section 68 of the Local Government Act 1993 or comply with the requirements for the disposal of stormwater contained in the development control plan that is applicable to the land.

Any wall constructed within 900mm of a lot boundary must be built in accordance with the support method proposed by the professional engineer’s report provided with the application for the complying development certificate.
Professional engineer is defined in clause 1.5.
Complying development certificate has the same meaning as it has in the Act.

heading.b: Setbacks of dwelling houses, attached development and detached development from protected trees

block.txt: A complying development certificate for complying development under Division 1 is taken to satisfy any requirement under this Policy for a permit, approval or development consent to remove or prune a tree or other vegetation on the lot if—
the tree is not listed on a register of significant trees kept by the council, and
the tree or vegetation will be within 3m of any building that has an area of more than 25m2, and
the tree or vegetation has a height that is less than—
for development that is the erection of a dwelling house—8m and is not required to be retained as a condition of consent, or
in any other case—6m.
Development under this code must be at least 3m from each protected tree on the lot and an adjoining lot (measured from the base of the trunk of the tree).
Despite subclause (2), the following development can be located within 3m of a protected tree if works do not involve excavation or fill of more than 150mm below or above ground level (existing)—
an access ramp,
a driveway, pathway or paving,
an awning, blind or canopy,
a fence, screen, or child-resistant barrier associated with a swimming pool or spa pool.
Development consent, dwelling house and protected tree are defined in clause 1.5.
Council, excavation, fill, ground level (existing), spa pool and swimming pool have the same meanings as they have in the Standard Instrument.
Complying development certificate has the same meaning as it has in the Act.
A separate permit, approval or development consent may be required if the branches or roots of a protected tree on the lot or on an adjoining lot are required to be pruned or removed.

heading.b: Conditions applying to complying development certificates under this code

block.txt: A complying development certificate for development under this code must be issued subject to the conditions specified in Schedule 6.
Complying development certificate and environmental planning instrument have the same meanings as they have in the Act.

Clause 1.18(1)(b) states that to be complying development for the purposes of this Policy the development must be permissible with consent under an environmental planning instrument applying to the land on which the development is carried out.
Schedule 3 contains variations to this code.

In addition to the requirements specified for development under this code, adjoining owners’ property rights, the applicable common law and other legislative requirements for approvals, licences, permits and authorities still apply. For example, requirements relevant to development in this code may be contained in the Act, the Environmental Planning and Assessment Regulation 2000, various State environmental planning policies, the Protection of the Environment Operations Act 1997, the Roads Act 1993, the Swimming Pools Act 1992 and Acts applying to various infrastructure authorities. If the development is in proximity to infrastructure, including water, stormwater and sewer mains, electricity power lines and telecommunications facilities, the relevant infrastructure authority should be contacted before commencing the development.

heading.b: Development that is complying development under this code

block.txt: This code applies to development that is specified in clauses 3A.2–3A.5 on lots in Zones RU1, RU2, RU3, RU4, RU6 and R5.

heading.b: Development that is not complying development under this code

block.txt: Development on land identified as susceptible to landslide risk in—
an environmental planning instrument applying to the land, or
for land to which Warringah Local Environmental Plan 2011 applies—“Area C” or “Area E” on the Landslip Risk Map within the meaning of that Plan.

heading.b: New single storey and two storey dwelling houses

block.txt: The erection of a new single storey or two storey dwelling house is development specified for this code if the development is erected on a lot—
in Zone RU1, RU2, RU4 or RU6 that has an area of at least 4,000m2, or
in Zone R5.
This clause does not apply if the size of the lot is less than the minimum lot size for the erection of a dwelling house under the environmental planning instrument applying to the lot.
For the purposes of calculating under this code the number of storeys in a dwelling house, any basement (including a garage) is to be counted as a storey.

heading.b: Alterations or additions to existing single storey and two storey dwelling houses

block.txt: Alterations or additions to an existing single storey or two storey dwelling house or the addition of a second storey to an existing single storey dwelling house is development specified for this code if the development is erected on a lot—
in Zone RU1, RU2, RU3, RU4 or RU6 that has an area of at least 4,000m2, or
in Zone R5.
Subclause (1) does not include development specified in the Housing Alterations Code.
The erection of a roof terrace on the topmost roof of—
an existing or a new dwelling house, or
an existing or a new outbuilding that is detached from a dwelling house,
is not development specified for this code.

The erection of new ancillary development, or alterations or additions to existing ancillary development, is development specified for this code if the development is ancillary to a dwelling house and erected on a lot—
in Zone RU1, RU2, RU3, RU4 or RU6 that has an area of at least 4,000m2, or
in Zone R5.
Subclause (1) does not include development specified in the Housing Alterations Code.
Ancillary development that is permitted by a current complying development certificate may be erected on a lot—
if a dwelling house exists on the lot—at any time, or
if there is a current development consent or complying development certificate for the construction of a dwelling house on the lot—before the construction of the dwelling house.
See clause 1.19(1)(a) in relation to development that is detached ancillary development or a swimming pool in a heritage conservation area or a draft heritage conservation area.

heading.b: Calculating lot area and determining lot type

block.txt: For the purpose of calculating the area of a lot, the area of the access laneway is excluded if it is a battle-axe lot.
When determining the lot type for this code, a lane is not to be considered a primary road.

heading.b: When separate permits are not required under this Part

block.txt: A complying development certificate for complying development under Division 1 is taken to satisfy any requirement under this Policy for a permit, approval or development consent to remove or prune a tree or other vegetation on a lot if—
the tree is not listed on a significant tree register or register of significant trees kept by the council, and
the tree or vegetation will be within 3m of development that is a building that has an area of more than 25m2, and
the tree or vegetation has a height that is less than—
for development that is the erection of a new dwelling house—8m and is not required to be retained as a condition of consent to the subdivision of the lot, or
for any other development—6m.
This Division sets out the specified development standards that apply to development specified for this code.
Development specified for this code may only be carried out on a lot that—
at the completion of the development will have only one dwelling house, and
if the lot is in Zone R5 and is not a battle-axe lot—has a width, measured at the building line, of at least 18m, and
if the lot is in Zone R5 and is a battle-axe lot—has an access laneway at least 3m wide and measures at least 12m × 12m, excluding the access laneway.

A lot on which a new single storey or two storey dwelling house is erected must have lawful direct frontage access or a right of carriageway to a public road or a road vested in or maintained by the council (other than a Crown road reserve).

If under section 88B of the Conveyancing Act 1919 a restriction is created that specifies a building envelope for a lot, development specified for this code may only be carried out within the building envelope specified.

heading.b: Maximum site coverage of all development

block.txt: The site coverage of a new dwelling house and all ancillary development on a lot in Zone R5 that has an area of less than 4,000m2 must not be more than 30 per cent.

heading.b: Maximum floor area for new dwelling houses

block.txt: The floor area of a new dwelling house on a lot in Zone R5 that has an area of less than 4,000m2 must not be more than 430m2.

heading.b: Maximum floor area for new outbuildings

block.txt: The floor area of a new outbuilding on a lot in Zone R5 that has an area of less than 4,000m2 must not be more than the following—
500m2, if the only purpose of the outbuilding is for agricultural use,
100m2, in any other case.

heading.b: Setbacks and maximum floor area for balconies, decks, patios, terraces and verandahs

block.txt: The total floor area of all balconies, decks, patios, terraces and verandahs on a lot must not be more than 12m2 if—
any part of the structure is within 6m from a side or the rear boundary, and
the structure has any point of its finished floor level more than 2m above ground level (existing).
A balcony, deck, patio, terrace or verandah must not have any point of its finished floor level—
if it is located within 3m of a side or the rear boundary—more than 2m above ground level (existing), or
if it is located more than 3m but not more than 6m from a side or the rear boundary—more than 3m above ground level (existing), or
if it is located more than 6m from a side or the rear boundary—more than 4m above ground level (existing).

Any detached balcony, deck, patio, terrace or verandah (including any alterations or additions to the detached balcony, deck, patio, terrace or verandah) must not have a floor level that is more than 600mm above ground level (existing).
This clause does not apply to a balcony, deck, patio, terrace or verandah that is located on the front elevation of a dwelling house unless the dwelling house is located on a battle-axe lot.
Development identified in this clause may require privacy screens under clause 3A.23.

heading.b: Maximum heights of dwelling houses and outbuildings

block.txt: The height of a dwelling house or the alterations and additions to an existing dwelling house on a lot in Zone R5 that has an area of less than 4,000m2 must not be more than 8.5m above ground level (existing).

The height of an outbuilding or the alterations and additions to an existing outbuilding on a lot in Zone R5 that has an area of less than 4,000m2 must not be more than 4.8m above ground level (existing).
The height of a dwelling house or the alterations and additions to an existing dwelling house on the following lots must not be more than 10m above ground level (existing)—
a lot in Zone RU1, RU2, RU3, RU4 or RU6,
a lot in Zone R5 that has an area of at least 4,000m2.
The height of an outbuilding, or of the alterations and additions to an existing outbuilding, must not be more than—
if the outbuilding is located on a lot in Zone RU1, RU2, RU3, RU4 or RU6 and the outbuilding is not a farm building or shed—4.8m above ground level (existing), or
if the outbuilding is located on a lot in Zone R5 that has an area of at least 4,000m2 and the outbuilding is not a farm building or shed—4.8m above ground level (existing), or
if the outbuilding is a farm building or shed—7m above ground level (existing).

The highest point of a dwelling house or the alterations and additions to an existing dwelling house referred to in subclause (1) or (3) must be at least 5m below the highest ridgeline of any hill within 100m of the dwelling or alteration.

heading.b: Setbacks of dwelling houses and ancillary development from roads

block.txt: A dwelling house and all ancillary development on a lot in Zone R5 that has an area of less than 4,000m2 must have a setback from the boundary with a primary road that is not a classified road of at least—
the average distance of the setbacks of the nearest 2 dwelling houses having the same primary road boundary and located within 40m of the lot on which the dwelling house is erected, or
in any case where 2 dwelling houses are not located within 40m of the lot, 10m.
A dwelling house and all ancillary development on a lot in the following zones must have a setback from the boundary with a primary road that is not a classified road of at least the following—
if the lot is in Zone R5 and has an area of at least 4,000m2—15m,
if the lot is in Zone RU4—30m,
if the lot is in Zone RU1, RU2, RU3 or RU6—50m.
A dwelling house and all ancillary development on a corner lot must have a setback from a boundary with a secondary road that is not a classified road of at least the following—
if the lot is in Zone R5 and has an area of less than 4,000m2—5m,
if the lot is in Zone R5 and has an area of at least 4,000m2, or is in Zone RU1, RU2, RU3, RU4 or RU6—10m.

A dwelling house and all ancillary development on a lot in Zone R5 that has an area of less than 4,000m2 must have a setback from a boundary with a parallel road that is not a classified road of at least 10m.
If a lot fronts a classified road, a dwelling house and any ancillary development must have a setback from the boundary with the classified road of—
if another environmental planning instrument applying to that lot specifies a setback for those circumstances, the setback specified by the other instrument, or
the setback specified by subclauses (1) and (2),
whichever is the greater.

heading.b: Setbacks of dwelling houses from side boundaries

block.txt: This clause applies to a dwelling house and any carport, garage, balcony, deck, patio, pergola, terrace or verandah that is attached to the dwelling house (a building).
Any point of a building, on a lot to which this code applies, must have a setback from the side boundary nearest to that point of at least the following distance—
if the lot is in Zone R5 and has an area of less than 4,000m2—2.5m,
if the lot is in Zone R5, and has an area of at least 4,000m2, or is in Zone RU1, RU2, RU3, RU4 or RU6—10m.

heading.b: Setbacks of dwelling houses from rear boundaries

block.txt: This clause applies to a dwelling house and any carport, garage, balcony, deck, patio, pergola, terrace or verandah that is attached to the dwelling house (a building).
Any point of the building must have a setback from the rear boundary nearest to that point of at least 15m.

heading.b: Setbacks of outbuildings from side and rear boundaries

block.txt: An outbuilding, or alterations and additions to an existing outbuilding, must have a setback from a side or rear boundary of at least—
if the only purpose of the outbuilding is for agricultural use—10m, or
in any other case—5m.
Despite any other clause in this Subdivision—
a new dwelling house, outbuilding or detached studio must have a setback of at least 3m from a boundary with a public reserve, and

side and rear setbacks and setbacks from the boundary with a road do not apply to the existing parts of a dwelling house or ancillary development where it is proposed to carry out any of the following—
alterations or additions to an existing dwelling house,
alterations or additions to existing ancillary development, and
side and rear setbacks do not apply to—

any aerial, antenna, awning, eave, flue, chimney, pipe, cooling or heating appliance, any rainwater tank greater than 1.8m in height or any other structure associated with the provision of a utility service, if it is located at least 450mm from the relevant boundary, and

any fence, fascia, gutter, downpipe, light fitting, electricity or gas meter, driveway, hard stand space, pathway or paving, if it is located within any required setback area to the relevant boundary, and
the setback from a road does not apply to—
a driveway, fence, hard stand space, pathway, paving or retaining wall, or
any building element that is permitted within the articulation zone, and

a dwelling house or outbuilding must have a setback of at least 40m from the bank of any perennial watercourse identified on a 1:50,000 topographical map published by Spatial Services in the Department of Finance, Services and Innovation, and
a dwelling house or outbuilding must have a setback of at least 250m from a boundary with adjoining land being used for any of the following—
forestry,
intensive livestock agriculture,
intensive plant agriculture,
mines and extractive industries,
railway lines,
rural industries.
For the purpose of determining the nearest 2 dwelling houses in clause 3A.15(1), a battle-axe lot is to be disregarded.
For the purpose of calculating the setbacks of the nearest 2 dwelling houses in clause 3A.15(1)—
any ancillary development is to be disregarded, and
any building element listed in clause 3A.22(2) is not to be included.
For the purpose of calculating the setbacks of a new dwelling house, any building element that is permitted in the articulation zone is not included.
For the purpose of calculating setbacks for a battle-axe lot, the setback on the opposite side of the lot to the rear setback is taken to be a side setback.
This clause applies only to lots in Zone R5 that have an area of less than 4,000m2.
A dwelling house, other than a dwelling house on a battle-axe lot, must have a front door and a window to a habitable room in the building wall that faces a primary road.
A dwelling house, other than a dwelling house on a battle-axe lot, must have a door and a window to a habitable room in the building wall that faces a parallel road.

A dwelling house, other than a dwelling house that has a setback from a primary road of less than 3m, may incorporate an articulation zone that extends from the building line to a distance of 1.5m into the required setback from the primary road.
A new dwelling house on a corner lot must have a window to a habitable room that is at least 1m2 in area and that faces and is visible from a secondary road.

heading.b: Building elements within the articulation zone to a primary road

block.txt: This clause applies only to lots in Zone R5 that have an area of less than 4,000m2.
The following building elements are permitted in an articulation zone in the setback from a primary road—
an entry feature or portico,
a balcony, deck, patio, pergola, terrace or verandah,
a window box treatment,
a bay window or similar feature,
an awning or other feature over a window,
a sun shading feature.
A building element on a dwelling house (other than a pitched roof to an entry feature or portico that has the same pitch as the roof on the dwelling house) must not extend more than—
1m above the gutter line of the eaves of a single storey dwelling house, or
above the gutter line of the eaves of a two storey dwelling house.

The maximum total area of all building elements within an articulation zone, other than a building element listed in subclause (2)(e) or (f), must be not more than 25% of the area of the articulation zone.
This clause applies only to lots in Zone R5 that have an area of less than 4,000m2.

A window in a new dwelling house, or a new window in any alteration or addition to an existing dwelling house, must have a privacy screen for any part of the window that is less than 1.5m above floor level if—
the window—
is in a habitable room that has a finished floor level of more than 1m above ground level (existing), and
has a sill height of less than 1.5m above that floor level, and
faces a side or rear boundary and is less than 3m from that boundary, or
the window—
is in a habitable room that has a finished floor level of more than 3m above ground level (existing), and
has a sill height of less than 1.5m above that floor level, and
faces a side or rear boundary and is at least 3m, but not more than 6m, from that boundary.
Subclause (2) does not apply to a window located in a bedroom where the window has an area of not more than 2m2.

A new balcony, deck, patio, terrace or verandah and any alteration to an existing balcony, deck, patio, terrace or verandah that has a floor area of more than 3m2 must have a privacy screen if the balcony, deck, patio, terrace or verandah is—
within 3m of a side or rear boundary and has a floor level more than 1m above ground level (existing), or
between 3m and 6m of a side or rear boundary and has a floor level more than 2m above ground level (existing).
Any privacy screen required under subclause (4) must be installed—
to a height of at least 1.7m, but not more than 2.2m, above the finished floor level of the balcony, deck, patio, terrace or verandah, and
at the edge of that part of the development that is within the areas specified in subclause (4)(a) or (b) and is parallel to or faces towards the relevant side or rear boundary.
A lot in Zone R5 that has an area of less than 4,000m2 must have at least 45% of its area landscaped.
At least 50% of the area forward of the building line to the primary road must be landscaped.
The landscaped area must be at least 2.5m wide.

heading.b: Setbacks of dwelling houses and ancillary development from protected trees

block.txt: A dwelling house and all ancillary development, and any associated excavation, must have a setback of at least 3m from the base of the trunk of each protected tree on the lot and an adjoining lot.

Despite subclause (1), ancillary development comprising the following is permitted within this setback, if the development does not require a cut or fill of more than 150mm below or above ground level (existing)—
an access ramp,
a driveway, pathway or paving,
an awning, blind or canopy,
a fence, screen or child-resistant barrier associated with a swimming pool or spa pool.
A separate permit, approval or development consent may be required if the branches or roots of a protected tree on the lot or on an adjoining lot are required to be pruned or removed.
A lot in Zone R5 that has an area of less than 4,000m2 and on which a new dwelling house is erected must have principal private open space that—
is at least 24m2, and
is at least 3m wide, and
is not steeper than 1:50 gradient.
This clause applies only to lots in Zone R5 that have an area of less than 4,000m2.
At least one off-street car parking space must be provided on a lot on which a new dwelling house is erected.
At least one off-street car parking space must be retained on a lot on which alterations or additions to an existing car parking space are carried out.
A car parking space under this clause may be an open hard stand space or a carport or garage, whether attached to or detached from the dwelling house.

heading.b: Garages, carports and car parking spaces

block.txt: This clause applies only to lots in Zone R5 that have an area of less than 4,000m2.
A garage, carport or car parking space that is accessed from a primary road must—
if the dwelling house has a setback from the primary road boundary of 4.5m or more—be at least 1m behind the building line of the dwelling house, or
if the dwelling house has a setback from the primary road boundary of less than 4.5m—be at least 5.5m from that boundary.
If the door or doors on a garage face a primary road, a secondary road or a parallel road, the total width of all those door openings must—
be not more than 6m, and
if the lot has a frontage of more than 15m—be not more than 50 per cent of the width of the building, measured at the building line to the relevant property boundary, and
if the lot has a frontage of not more than 15m—be not more than 60 per cent of the width of the building, measured at the building line to the relevant property boundary.
An open hard stand car parking space must measure at least 2.6m wide by 5.4m long.
A lot on which an off-street car parking space is provided or retained under clause 3A.27 must have a driveway to a public road.
A driveway on a lot must be constructed in accordance with AS/NZS 2890.1:2004, Parking facilities, Part 1: Off-street car parking.
Clause 2.28 applies to the construction or installation of a driveway as exempt development.

heading.b: Earthworks, retaining walls and structural support

block.txt: Excavation for the purposes of development under this code must not exceed a maximum depth, measured from ground level (existing), of—
if located not more than 1m from any boundary—1m, and
if located more than 1m but not more than 1.5m from any boundary—2m, and
if located more than 1.5m from any boundary—3m.
Excavation for the purposes of a pier in a pier and beam foundation may exceed the maximum depth specified in subclause (1) if a professional engineer has certified the depth of the excavation.

Despite subclauses (1) and (1A), the excavation must not exceed a maximum depth, measured from ground level (existing), of 1m if the land is identified as Class 3 or 4 on an Acid Sulfate Soils Map or is within 40m of a waterbody (natural).
Fill must not exceed a maximum height, measured from ground level (existing), of—
if the fill is for the purposes of the erection or alteration of, or an addition to, a dwelling house under this code—1m, and
if the fill is for any other purpose under this code—600mm.
Despite subclause (3), the height of fill is not limited if the fill is contained—
wholly within the footprint of a dwelling house or ancillary development, or
by a drop edge beam.

Fill that is higher than 150mm above ground level (existing) and is not contained wholly within the footprint of a dwelling house or ancillary development is limited to 50% of the landscaped area of the lot.
The ground level (finished) of the fill must not be used to measure the height of any dwelling house or ancillary development under this code.
Support for earthworks more than 600mm above or below ground level (existing) must take the form of a retaining wall or other structural support that—
a professional engineer has certified as structurally sound, including in relation to (but not limited to) the ability to withstand the forces of lateral soil load, and
has been designed so as not to redirect the flow of any surface water or ground water, or cause sediment to be transported, onto an adjoining property, and
has adequate drainage lines connected to the stormwater drainage system for the site, and

does not have a total height measured vertically from the base of the retaining wall or structural support to its uppermost portion that is more than the height of the associated excavation or fill, and
is separated from any other retaining wall or structural support on the site by at least 2m, measured horizontally, and
is installed in accordance with any manufacturer’s specifications, and
if it is an embankment or batter—has a toe or top that is more than 1m from any side or rear boundary.
Excavation, fill and ground level (existing) have the same meanings as they have in the Standard Instrument.
Fill and excavation that is not associated with a building may be exempt development under clauses 2.29 and 2.30.
All stormwater drainage collecting as a result of the erection of, or alterations or additions to, a dwelling house or ancillary development must be conveyed by a gravity fed or charged system to—
a public drainage system, or
an inter-allotment drainage system, or
an on-site disposal system.
All stormwater drainage systems within a lot and the connection to a public or an inter-allotment drainage system must—
if an approval is required under section 68 of the Local Government Act 1993, be approved under that Act, or

if an approval is not required under section 68 of the Local Government Act 1993, comply with any requirements for the disposal of stormwater drainage contained in a development control plan that is applicable to the land.
Ancillary development comprising a swimming pool for private use must be located on a lot—
behind the setback area from a primary road, or
in the rear yard.
Development for the purposes of a swimming pool is not complying development under this Code unless it is ancillary to a dwelling house.
The swimming pool water line must have a setback of at least 1m from a side or rear boundary.
Despite subclauses (1) and (2), if the swimming pool is being constructed in a heritage conservation area, the swimming pool must be located—
behind the rear most building line of the dwelling house, and
no closer to each side boundary than the dwelling house.
Decking around a swimming pool must not be more than 600mm above ground level (existing).
Coping around a swimming pool must not be more than—
1.4m above ground level (existing), and
300mm wide if the coping is more than 600mm above ground level (existing).
Water from a swimming pool must be discharged in accordance with an approval under the Local Government Act 1993 if the lot is not connected to a sewer main.
Any pump attached to the development must be housed in an enclosure that is soundproofed.

If the swimming pool is being constructed after, and at a different time to, the erection of a dwelling house on the lot, the development standards for this Code (other than the standards referred to in clauses 3A.24, 3A.24A, 3A.25, 3A.29, 3A.38 and this clause) do not apply to the construction.
A child-resistant barrier must be constructed or installed in accordance with the requirements of the Swimming Pools Act 1992.
Requirements relating to excavation for the purposes of a swimming pool are set out in clause 3A.29.
This clause applies—
to a detached studio, and
in addition to the development standards specified in clause 3A.24.
Clauses 3A.9 and 3A.10 contain development standards that also apply to detached studios.
A detached studio must not be located in a heritage conservation area or draft heritage conservation area.
A detached studio must be located behind the building line of a dwelling house.
No more than one detached studio may be located on a lot.
A detached studio must not have a building height of more than 3.6m.
The floor area of a detached studio must not be more than 35m2.
A detached studio must have a setback from a side or rear boundary of at least—
if the lot is in Zone R5 and has an area of less than 4,000m2—2.5m, or
in any other case—5m.

heading.b: Development standards for outbuildings in heritage conservation areas

block.txt: This clause applies—
to an outbuilding erected on a lot in a heritage conservation area or a draft heritage conservation area to which this code applies, and
in addition to the development standards specified in clauses 3A.10, 3A.14, 3A.18 and 3A.24.
The outbuilding must be located—
behind the rear most building line of the dwelling house, and
no closer to each side boundary than the dwelling house.
The floor area of an outbuilding must not be more than 20m2.
The lot must not adjoin a lane or a secondary or parallel road frontage.

heading.b: Development standards for bush fire prone land

block.txt: This clause applies—

to all development specified for this code that is carried out on a lot that is wholly or partly bush fire prone land (other than development that is the erection of non-habitable ancillary development that is more than 6m from any dwelling house, landscaping, a non-combustible fence or a swimming pool), and
in addition to all other development standards specified for this code.
See clause 1.19A for additional provisions relating to bush fire prone land.
The development may be carried out on the lot only if—
the development conforms to the specifications and requirements of Planning for Bush Fire Protection that are relevant to the development, and
the lot has direct access to a public road or a road vested in or maintained by the council, and
the development is located within 200m of that road, and
there is sufficient access designed in accordance with the acceptable solutions identified in Table 7.4a of Planning for Bush Fire Protection, and

a reticulated water supply is connected to the lot, or a water supply with a 65mm metal Storz outlet with a gate or ball valve is provided for fire fighting purposes on the lot (the gate or ball valve, pipes and tank penetrations are to be designed to allow for a full 50mm inner diameter water flow through the Storz fitting and must be of a metal construction), and
the size of the non-reticulated water supply mentioned in paragraph (f) is—
for a lot with an area no greater than 10,000m2—10,000L, and
for a lot with an area greater than 10,000m2—20,000L, and

reticulated or bottled gas on the lot is installed and maintained in accordance with AS/NZS 1596:2014, The storage and handling of LP Gas and the requirements of relevant authorities (metal piping must be used), and
all fixed gas cylinders on the lot are located at least 10m from flammable materials and are enclosed on the hazard side of the installation, and
any gas cylinders on the lot that are within 10m of a dwelling house—
have the release valves directed away from the dwelling house, and
have metal connections to and from the cylinders, and
there are no polymer sheathed flexible gas supply lines to gas meters adjacent to the dwelling.
The requirements relating to the construction of buildings in bush fire prone areas set out in the Building Code of Australia also apply.

heading.b: Complying development on flood control lots

block.txt: Development under this code must not be carried out on any part of a flood control lot, other than a part of the lot that the council or a professional engineer who specialises in hydraulic engineering has certified, for the purposes of the issue of the complying development certificate, as not being any of the following—
a flood storage area,
a floodway,
a flow path,
a high hazard area,
a high risk area.
Development that is carried out under this code on any part of a flood control lot must meet the following requirements—

if there is a minimum floor level adopted in a development control plan by the relevant council for the lot, the development must not cause any habitable room in the dwelling house to have a floor level lower than that floor level,
any part of the dwelling house or any ancillary development that is erected at or below the flood planning level is constructed of flood compatible material,

any part of the dwelling house or any ancillary development that is erected is able to withstand the forces exerted during a flood by water, debris and buoyancy up to the flood planning level (or if an on-site refuge is provided on the lot, the probable maximum flood level),
the development must not result in increased flooding elsewhere in the floodplain,
the lot must have pedestrian and vehicular access to a readily accessible refuge at a level equal to or higher than the lowest habitable floor level of the dwelling house,
vehicular access to the dwelling house will not be inundated by water to a level of more than 0.3m during a 1:100 ARI (average recurrent interval) flood event,
the lot must not have any open car parking spaces or carports lower than the level of a 1:20 ARI (average recurrent interval) flood event.

The requirements under subclause (2)(c) and (d) are satisfied if a joint report by a professional engineer specialising in hydraulic engineering and a professional engineer specialising in civil engineering states that the requirements are satisfied.
A word or expression used in this clause has the same meaning as it has in the Flood Risk Management Manual, unless it is otherwise defined in this Policy.
A section 10.7 certificate from a Council will state whether or not a lot is a flood control lot.

heading.b: Conditions applying to complying development certificates under this code

block.txt: A complying development certificate for development specified under this code must be issued subject to the conditions specified in Schedule 6.

Clause 1.18(1)(b) states that to be complying development for the purposes of this Policy the development must be permissible with consent under an environmental planning instrument applying to the land on which the development is carried out.

In addition to the requirements specified for development under this code, adjoining owners’ property rights, the applicable common law and other legislative requirements for approvals, licences, permits and authorities still apply. For example, requirements relevant to development in this code may be contained in the Act, the Environmental Planning and Assessment Regulation 2000, various State environmental planning policies, the Protection of the Environment Operations Act 1997, the Roads Act 1993, the Swimming Pools Act 1992 and Acts applying to various infrastructure authorities. If the development is in proximity to infrastructure, including water, stormwater and sewer mains, electricity power lines and telecommunications facilities, the relevant infrastructure authority should be contacted before commencing the development.

heading.b: Manor houses permitted in certain land use zones
Development for the purposes of manor houses

block.txt: Manor houses are, despite any other environmental planning instrument, permitted with consent on land in any of the following land use zones if multi dwelling housing or residential flat buildings (or both) are permitted in the zone—
Zone RU5 Village,
Zone R1 General Residential,
Zone R2 Low Density Residential,
Zone R3 Medium Density Residential.

heading.b: Requirements for complying development under this code
Development that can be complying development under this code

block.txt: The following types of development are complying development under this code—
the erection or alteration of, or addition to—
any 1 or 2 storey dual occupancy, manor house or multi dwelling housing (terraces), or
any attached development or detached development related to any building referred to in subparagraph (i),
the conversion of an existing dwelling to a dual occupancy.
For the purposes of calculating the number of storeys in a building for the purposes of this code, only those parts of a basement that comprise habitable rooms are to be counted as a storey.
Complying development specified for this code may only be carried out on a lot that meets the following requirements—
the lot must be in Zone RU5, Zone R1, Zone R2 or Zone R3,
the lot must have lawful access to a public road at the completion of the development.

heading.b: Erection of attached development and detached development

block.txt: Attached development or detached development may be erected on a lot—
if a dual occupancy, manor house or multi dwelling housing (terraces) exists on the lot, or
if there is a current development consent or complying development certificate for the construction of a dual occupancy, manor house or multi dwelling housing (terraces) on the lot.
Complying development certificate has the same meaning as it has in the Act.
Clauses 1.17A, 1.18 and 1.19(1) set out additional requirements for complying development.

heading.b: Development that is not complying development under this code

block.txt: The following development is not complying development under this code—
the erection or alteration of, or an addition to, a roof terrace on the top most roof of a building,
development that is complying development under the Housing Alterations Code,
development on a battle-axe lot,
development on any lot on which there is a secondary dwelling or group home whether or not the development is attached to the dwelling or home,
the erection of a building over a registered easement,
the alteration of, or an addition to, a garage or carport that is located forward of the building line,
the erection of multi dwelling housing (terraces) on bush fire prone land,

development to which State Environmental Planning Policy (Housing) 2021, Chapter 2, Part 2, Division 1 applies, unless it is development that is being carried out by or on behalf of the New South Wales Land and Housing Corporation constituted by the Housing Act 2001,
development on unsewered land,
development on land identified as susceptible to landslide risk in—
an environmental planning instrument applying to the land, or
for land to which Warringah Local Environmental Plan 2011 applies—“Area C” or “Area E” on the Landslip Risk Map within the meaning of that Plan.
In this code, a reference to a lot is a reference to any of the following lots—
standard lot,
corner lot,
parallel road lot.
Corner lot, lane, parallel road lot and standard lot are defined in clause 1.5.
A lot that adjoins a lane is not a parallel road lot or a corner lot. The lot type depends on which other roads it fronts (if any).
When determining the lot type for this code, a lane is not to be considered a primary road.

heading.b: Complying development on bush fire prone land

block.txt: This clause does not apply to the following complying development under this code—
a non-habitable detached development that is more than 6m from any residential accommodation,
a landscaped area,
a non-combustible fence,
a swimming pool.
See clause 1.19A for additional provisions relating to bush fire prone land.
If complying development under this code is carried out on bush fire prone land, all of the following development standards also apply—
the lot on which the development is to be carried out must have direct access to a public road or a road vested in or maintained by the council,
the dual occupancy or manor house must be able to be connected to mains electricity,
if reticulated or bottled gas is installed and maintained on the lot—
it must be installed and maintained in accordance with AS/NZS 1596:2014, The storage and handling of LP Gas, and
the storage and handling of any LP gas on the lot must comply with the requirements of the relevant authorities (including the use of metal piping),
any gas cylinder stored on the lot within 10m of any dwelling must—
have its release valves directed away from the dwelling, and
be enclosed on the hazard side of the installation, and
have metal connections to and from the cylinder,
there must not be any polymer sheathed flexible gas supply lines to gas meters adjacent to the dual occupancy,
if the development is carried out on a lot in Zone RU5, there must be—
a reticulated water supply connection to the lot and a fire hydrant within 70m of any part of the development, or
a 10,000 L capacity water tank on the lot,
if the development is carried out on a lot in any zone other than Zone RU5, there must be—
a reticulated water supply connection to the lot, and
a fire hydrant within 70m of any part of the development,
the development must conform to the specifications and requirements of Planning for Bush Fire Protection that are relevant to the development.
Attached development, council and detached development are defined in clause 1.5.
Bush fire prone land, landscaped area, road and swimming pool have the same meanings as they have in the Standard Instrument.

heading.b: Complying development on flood control lots

block.txt: Development under this code must not be carried out on any part of a flood control lot, other than a part of the lot that the council or a professional engineer who specialises in hydraulic engineering has certified, for the purposes of the issue of the relevant complying development certificate, as not being any of the following—
a flood storage area,
a floodway,
a flow path,
a high hazard area,
a high risk area.
If complying development under this code is carried out on any part of a flood control lot, the following development standards also apply in addition to any other development standards—

if there is a minimum floor level adopted in a development control plan by the relevant council for the lot, the development must not cause any habitable room to have a floor level lower than that floor level,
any part of a building that is erected at or below the flood planning level is constructed of flood compatible material,

any part of a building that is erected is able to withstand the forces exerted during a flood by water, debris and buoyancy up to the flood planning level (or if an on-site refuge is provided on the lot, the probable maximum flood level),
the development must not result in increased flooding elsewhere in the floodplain,

the lot must have pedestrian and vehicular access to a readily accessible refuge at a level equal to or higher than the lowest habitable floor level of the dual occupancy, manor house or multi dwelling housing (terraces),
vehicular access to any dwelling will not be inundated by water to a level of more than 0.3m during a 1:100 ARI (average recurrent interval) flood event,
the lot must not have any open car parking spaces or carports lower than the level of a 1:20 ARI (average recurrent interval) flood event.

The requirements under subclause (2)(c) and (d) are satisfied if a joint report by a professional engineer specialising in hydraulic engineering and a professional engineer specialising in civil engineering states that the requirements are satisfied.
Without limiting subclause (3), a joint report must—
include a signature made by each professional engineer by whom the report is prepared, and
where conclusions of the report are based on data, surveys or other material—include the name and author of the document on which the conclusions are based.
A word or expression used in this clause has the same meaning as it has in the Flood Risk Management Manual, unless it is otherwise defined in this Policy.
A planning certificate from a council will state whether or not a lot is a flood control lot.

heading.b: Development standards for land near Siding Spring Observatory

block.txt: If complying development under this code is carried out on land in the local government area of Coonamble, Gilgandra, Warrumbungle Shire or Dubbo Regional, the development standards in this clause also apply in addition to any other development standards.
Complying development specified for this code may only be carried out if it does not result in residential accommodation on land in the local government area of—
Coonamble, Gilgandra, Warrumbungle Shire or Dubbo Regional with an outside light fitting other than a shielded light fitting, and
Coonamble, Gilgandra or Warrumbungle Shire with more than 7 shielded outside light fittings or more than 5 such light fittings that are not automatic light fittings.

heading.b: Development standards for certain dual occupancies and attached development

block.txt: This Division sets out the development standards that apply to the following types of complying development under this code—
the conversion of an existing dwelling to a dual occupancy,
the erection or alteration of, or an addition to, a dual occupancy where no part of a dwelling is located above any part of another dwelling,
the erection or alteration of, or addition to, attached development that is related to any such dual occupancy.
Clauses 1.17A, 1.18 and 1.19(1) set out additional requirements for complying development.
The area of the parent lot must not be less than whichever is the greater of the following—

the minimum lot area specified for dual occupancies in the environmental planning instrument, other than State Environmental Planning Policy (Housing) 2021, Chapter 6, Part 2, Division 2, that applies to the land concerned.

Despite subclause (1), the area of the parent lot in development carried out by or on behalf of the Aboriginal Housing Office, the Land and Housing Corporation or a registered community housing provider, within the meaning of State Environmental Planning Policy (Housing) 2021, must not be less than 400m2.
The width of the parent lot must not be less than the following when measured at the building line—
if the car parking space for the parent lot is accessed only from a secondary road, parallel road or lane—12m,
otherwise—15m.
The maximum height for a dual occupancy and any attached development is 8.5m above ground level (existing).
Ground level (existing) is defined in the Standard Instrument as the existing level of a site at any point.

heading.b: Maximum gross floor area of all buildings

block.txt: The maximum gross floor area of all buildings on a lot is shown in the following table—

heading.b: Minimum setbacks and maximum height and length of boundary walls

block.txt: The setback of a dual occupancy and any attached development from a primary road must not be less than the average setback from the primary road of the 2 nearest dwelling houses or dual occupancies within 40m of the lot and on the same side of the primary road.
Clause 3B.12 contains certain exclusions from, and exceptions to, the setbacks in this clause.
For the purpose of determining the setbacks from the primary road of the 2 nearest dwelling houses or dual occupancies, the following are not to be included—
dwelling houses or dual occupancies on battle-axe lots,
any attached development or detached development on other lots,
building elements in the articulation zone.

If there are not 2 dwelling houses or dual occupancies within 40m of the lot on the same side of the primary road, the dual occupancy and any attached development must have a minimum setback from the boundary with the primary road as shown in the following table—

entry.txt: Minimum setback from primary road boundary

block.txt: The following buildings must have a minimum setback from a side boundary as shown in the table to this subclause—
a dual occupancy,
a garage or an attached carport,
a balcony, deck, patio, pergola, terrace or verandah,
a cabana, cubby house, garden shed, gazebo, fernery, greenhouse or shed.

entry.txt: Width of parent lot at the building line
Minimum required setback from each side boundary

block.txt: Each part of a dual occupancy (other than a detached dual occupancy on a corner lot) and any carport, garage, balcony, deck, patio, pergola, terrace or verandah must have a minimum setback from the rear boundary as shown in the following table—
Certain exceptions to the rear setbacks apply if the lot has a rear boundary with a lane (see clause 3B.12(4)).

heading.b: Secondary road setbacks for corner lots

block.txt: Despite any other setback specified in this clause, a dual occupancy and any attached development must have a minimum setback from a boundary with a secondary road as shown in the following table—

entry.txt: Minimum setback from secondary road boundary

block.txt: In many cases the primary road and secondary road may be different for each of the dwellings comprising a dual occupancy (detached) on a corner lot. This is because for each dwelling the primary road is the road that the dwelling faces. Accordingly, the setbacks for each of these dwellings will not necessarily align.

heading.b: Dual occupancy (detached) on a corner lot

block.txt: If a dual occupancy on a corner lot has a dwelling fronting different roads, the rear of each dwelling is to be treated as a side for the purposes of determining the setbacks required under this clause.

heading.b: Parallel road setbacks for parallel road lots

block.txt: Despite any other setback specified in this clause, a dual occupancy and any attached development must have a setback from a boundary with a parallel road of at least 3m unless, in the case of a dual occupancy (attached), 1 of the dwellings in the dual occupancy faces the parallel road, in which case the setback must be the same as if the parallel road were a primary road.

The primary road and parallel road may be different for each of the dwellings comprising a dual occupancy (detached) if the dwellings face in opposite directions. This is because for each dwelling the primary road is the road that the dwelling faces.
Despite any other setback specified in this clause, a dual occupancy and any attached development must have a setback from a boundary with a classified road of at least 9m.
Despite any other setback specified in this clause, a dual occupancy and any attached development must have a setback from a boundary with a public reserve of at least 3m.

Articulation zone, attached development, battle-axe lot, boundary wall, building element, building line, detached development, dwelling house, lane, primary road, setback and standard lot are defined in clause 1.5.
Building height, classified road and public reserve have the same meanings as they have in the Standard Instrument.

heading.b: Development to which side and rear setbacks do not apply

block.txt: The setback standards specified in clause 3B.11(4) and (5) do not apply to the following—
access ramps,
downpipes,
driveways or hard stand spaces,
electricity or gas meters,
fascias,
fences,
gutters,
light fittings,
pathways and paving,
steps.

heading.b: Development to which side and rear setbacks do not apply if 450mm from boundary

block.txt: The setback standards specified in clause 3B.11(4) and (5) do not apply to the following if they are at least 450mm from the relevant boundary—
aerials,
antennae,
awnings,
chimneys,
cooling or heating appliances,
eaves,
flues,
pipes,
privacy screens,
rainwater tanks,
structures associated with the provision of a utility service.

heading.b: Development to which road setbacks do not apply

block.txt: The setback standards specified in clause 3B.11(1), (3), (6), (8) and (9) do not apply to the following—
access ramps,
driveways,
eaves,
pathways and paving,
retaining walls,
any building elements that are permitted within a primary road articulation zone,
steps.
Despite clause 3B.11(5), if the lot has a rear boundary with a lane, a building to which that subclause applies may be erected within 900mm of, or abut, the rear boundary for a maximum length of 7m.

heading.b: Setbacks do not apply to existing parts of dual occupancy or attached development

block.txt: The setbacks standards specified in clause 3B.11 do not apply to any existing parts of a dwelling house, dual occupancy or attached development that will remain on a lot after the complying development is carried out.
Articulation zone, attached development, dwelling house, primary road and setback are defined in clause 1.5.
Each dwelling must face a public road.
No dwelling must be located behind another dwelling on the same lot (except on a corner lot or a parallel road lot where each dwelling fronts a different road).
The 2 buildings comprising a dual occupancy (detached) (including any attached development) must be located at least 3m from each other.
The 2 buildings comprising a dual occupancy (attached) must share a common wall.
Each dwelling, including an off-street car parking space for the dwelling, must have a minimum width, measured at the building line, of—
if the car parking space is accessed from a primary road—6.5m, or
otherwise—5m.
The width of a dwelling is to be measured from the centre of a side wall if that wall adjoins another building or from the outside of the side wall if that wall is an external wall.

heading.b: Other development standards for new balconies, decks, patios, terraces and verandahs attached to side or rear of dual occupancy

block.txt: The maximum height of the floor level of the balcony, deck, patio, terrace or verandah is 4m above ground level (existing).
The floor level of the balcony, deck, patio, terrace or verandah must be the same as the floor level of the part of the dual occupancy to which it is attached.

Any attached side or rear balcony, deck, patio, terrace or verandah that has a floor level of more than 2m above ground level (existing) must have a setback from side and rear boundaries of at least 3m.
The total floor area of all attached decks having a floor level of more than 2m above ground level (existing) must not be more than 12m2 for each dwelling.
Attached, building line and floor area are defined in clause 1.5.
Ground level (existing) has the same meaning as it has in the Standard Instrument.
A balcony may require a privacy screen—see clause 3B.17.
The minimum landscaped area that must be provided is 50% of the parent lot area minus 100m2.
At least 25% of the area of the lot forward of the building line must be landscaped.
At least 50% of the area required to be landscaped under subclause (1) must be located behind the building line.
Each landscaped area must have—
a minimum width of 1.5m, and
a minimum length of 1.5m.
Principal private open space must be provided for each dwelling that—
is at least 16m2, and
is at least 3m wide.
This clause does not apply to complying development that is the alteration of, or addition to, a dual occupancy or attached development if the development does not—
increase the footprint of the dual occupancy or attached development, or
decrease the landscaped area on the lot, or
decrease the principal private open space for a dwelling.
Building line and principal private open space are defined in clause 1.5.
Landscaped area has the same meaning as it has in the Standard Instrument.

heading.b: Primary and secondary road articulation zones

block.txt: A dual occupancy may have the following articulation zones—
a primary road articulation zone that extends up to 1.5m forward of the minimum required setback from the primary road,
a secondary road articulation zone that extends up to 1m forward of the minimum required setback from the secondary road.
The following building elements can be located in the primary road articulation zone or secondary road articulation zone—
an entry feature or portico,
a balcony, deck, pergola, terrace or verandah,
a window box treatment,
a bay window or similar feature,
an awning or other feature over a window,
a sun shading feature,
an eave,
an access ramp.

The maximum total area of all building elements in the articulation zone, other than a building element specified in subclause (2)(e), (f), (g) or (h), must not comprise more than 25% of the area of the articulation zone.
Each habitable room that has a wall facing a road must have a window in that wall.
Articulation zone, building element, primary road, secondary road and setback are defined in clause 1.5.

heading.b: Privacy screens for windows and certain attached development
Windows in habitable rooms near boundaries or other dwellings

block.txt: A window in a habitable room must have a privacy screen over any part of that window that is less than 1.5m above the floor level of the room in the following cases—
the floor level of the habitable room is 1m or more, but not more than 3m, above ground level (existing) and the window faces a side or rear boundary and is less than 3m from that boundary,
the floor level of the habitable room is more than 3m above ground level (existing) and the window faces a side or rear boundary and is less than 6m from that boundary,
the floor level of the habitable room is 1m or more, but not more than 3m, above ground level (existing) and the window faces a dwelling on the same lot and is less than 6m from that dwelling,
the floor level of the habitable room is more than 3m above ground level (existing) and the window faces a dwelling on the same lot and is less than 12m from that dwelling.
Subclause (1) does not apply to—
a habitable room with a floor level not more than 1m above ground level (existing), or
a window that faces a road or public space, or
a bedroom window that has an area of not more than 2m2.

heading.b: Balconies, decks, patios, terraces or verandahs near boundaries or other dwellings

block.txt: The edge of a balcony, deck, patio, terrace or verandah must have a privacy screen with a height of at least 1.5m above the floor level of a balcony, deck, patio, terrace or verandah in the following cases—

the floor level of the balcony, deck, patio, terrace or verandah is 1m or more, but not more than 3m, above ground level (existing) and the edge faces a side or rear boundary and is less than 3m from that boundary,
the floor level of the balcony, deck, patio, terrace or verandah is more than 3m above ground level (existing) and the edge faces a side or rear boundary and is less than 6m from that boundary,

the floor level of the balcony, deck, patio, terrace or verandah is 1m or more, but not more than 2m, above ground level (existing) and the edge faces a dwelling on the same lot and is less than 6m from that dwelling,
the floor level of the balcony, deck, patio, terrace or verandah is more than 2m above ground level (existing) and the edge faces a dwelling on the same lot and is less than 12m from that dwelling.
Subclause (3) does not apply to a balcony, deck, patio, terrace or verandah—
with a floor level not more than 1m above ground level (existing), or
that faces a road or public space, or
that has an area of not more than 2m2.

heading.b: Existing windows, balconies, decks, patios, terraces or verandahs

block.txt: This clause does not apply to any existing parts of a dwelling house, dual occupancy or attached development that will remain on the lot after the complying development is carried out.
Habitable room and privacy screen are defined in clause 1.5.
Ground level (existing) has the same meaning as it has in the Standard Instrument.

heading.b: Car parking and vehicle access requirements

block.txt: This clause applies to—
the erection of a dual occupancy, or
the alteration of, or addition to, a dwelling house that causes a dual occupancy to be on the lot.
At least 1 off-street car parking space must be provided for each dwelling.
The off-street car parking space may be an open hard stand space or a carport or garage, whether attached to or detached from the dual occupancy.
All off-street car parking spaces and vehicle access must comply with AS/NZS 2890.1:2004, Parking facilities, Part 1: Off-street car parking.

In the case of a lot that has a width of less than 15m measured at the building line any car parking space must be provided at the rear of the lot or in a basement and must be accessed only from a secondary road, parallel road or lane.
A garage, carport or car parking space at ground level (existing) and accessed from a primary road, secondary road or parallel road must have a minimum setback as shown in the following table—

block.txt: Attached, building line, detached, hard stand space, lane, parallel road, primary road, secondary road and setback are defined in clause 1.5.
Clause 2.28 applies to the construction or installation of a driveway as exempt development.
Alterations or additions to a garage or carport that is forward of the building line is not complying development under this code (see clause 3B.2(g)).
The design of a dual occupancy must be consistent with the relevant design criteria in the Low Rise Housing Diversity Design Guide.
However, the requirements of this Part prevail to the extent that the Guide is inconsistent with this Part.

heading.b: Development standards for manor houses, certain dual occupancies and attached development

block.txt: This Division sets out the development standards that apply to the following types of complying development under this code—
the conversion of an existing dwelling to a dual occupancy,
the erection or alteration of, or an addition to, a manor house,
the erection or alteration of, or an addition to, a dual occupancy (attached) where part of a dwelling is located above part of another dwelling,
the erection or alteration of, or addition to, attached development that is related to any such dual occupancy or manor house.
Clauses 1.17A, 1.18 and 1.19(1) set out additional requirements for complying development.
The lot must meet the following requirements—
in the case of a manor house—the area of the lot must not be less than whichever is greater of the following—

the minimum lot area specified for manor houses in the environmental planning instrument, other than State Environmental Planning Policy (Housing) 2021, Chapter 6, Part 4, Division 2, that applies to the land concerned,
in the case of a dual occupancy—the area of the lot must not be less than whichever is the greater of the following—
