the minimum lot area specified for dual occupancies in the environmental planning instrument, other than State Environmental Planning Policy (Housing) 2021, Chapter 6, Part 2, Division 2, that applies to the land concerned,
the width of the lot must not be less than 15m measured at the building line.
The maximum height for a manor house, dual occupancy and any attached development is 8.5m above ground level (existing).
This clause does not apply to any existing part of a building that is more than 8.5m above ground level (existing) before the relevant complying development takes place.
Ground level (existing) is defined in the Standard Instrument as the existing level of a site at any point.

heading.b: Maximum gross floor area of all buildings

block.txt: The maximum gross floor area of all buildings on a lot is 25% of the lot area plus 150m2, to a maximum of 400m2.

heading.b: Minimum setbacks and maximum height and length of boundary walls

block.txt: The setback of a manor house, dual occupancy and any attached development from a primary road must not be less than the average setback from the primary road of the 2 nearest buildings within 40m of the lot and on the same side of the primary road that are residential accommodation.
For the purpose of determining the setbacks from the primary road of the 2 nearest buildings that are residential accommodation, the following are not to be included—
buildings on battle-axe lots,
attached development and detached development on other lots,
building elements in the articulation zone.
Setbacks for boundaries with classified roads and public reserves are set out in subclauses (9) and (10).

If there are not 2 buildings that are residential accommodation within 40m of the lot on the same side of the primary road, the manor house or dual occupancy and any attached development must have a minimum setback from the boundary with the primary road as shown in the following table—

entry.txt: Minimum setback from primary road boundary

block.txt: A manor house, dual occupancy or any attached development must have a minimum setback from a side boundary of 1.5 m.

Despite subclause (4), any part of a manor house, dual occupancy or any attached development that is more than 10m behind the building line and that is more than 4.5m above ground level (existing) must have a minimum setback from a side boundary of—
s is the minimum setback in metres.
h is the height of the part of the building in metres.
Each part of a manor house or dual occupancy and any attached development must have a minimum setback from the rear boundary as shown in the following table—
Certain exceptions to the rear setbacks apply if the lot has a rear boundary with a lane (see clause 3B.25(4)).

heading.b: Secondary road setbacks for corner lots

block.txt: Despite any other setback specified in this clause, a dual occupancy, manor house and any attached development must have a minimum setback from a boundary with a secondary road as shown in the following table—

entry.txt: Minimum setback from secondary road boundary

heading.b: Parallel road setbacks for parallel road lots

block.txt: Despite any other setback specified in this clause, a dual occupancy, manor house and any attached development must have a setback from a boundary with a parallel road of at least 3m.
Despite any other setback specified in this clause, a dual occupancy, manor house and any attached development must have a setback from a boundary with a classified road of at least 9m.
Despite any other setback specified in this clause, a dual occupancy, manor house and any attached development must have a setback from a boundary with a public reserve of at least 3m.

Articulation zone, attached development, battle-axe lot, boundary wall, building element, building line, detached development, dwelling house, lane, primary road, setback and standard lot are defined in clause 1.5.
Building height, classified road and ground level (existing) have the same meanings as they have in the Standard Instrument.

heading.b: Development to which side and rear setbacks do not apply

block.txt: The setback standards specified in clause 3B.24(4), (5) and (6) do not apply to the following—
access ramps,
downpipes,
driveways and hard stand spaces,
electricity or gas meters,
fascias,
fences,
gutters,
light fittings,
pathways and paving,
steps.

heading.b: Development to which side and rear setbacks do not apply if 450mm from boundary

block.txt: The setback standards specified in clause 3B.24(4), (5) and (6) do not apply to the following if they are at least 450mm from the relevant boundary—
aerials,
antennae,
awnings,
chimneys,
cooling or heating appliances,
eaves,
flues,
pipes,
privacy screens,
rainwater tanks,
structures associated with the provision of a utility service.

heading.b: Development to which road setbacks do not apply

block.txt: The setback standards specified in clause 3B.24(1), (3), (7), (8) and (9) do not apply to the following—
access ramps,
driveways,
eaves,
pathways and paving,
retaining walls,
any building elements that are permitted within a primary road articulation zone,
steps.
Despite clause 3B.24(6), if the lot has a rear boundary with a lane, the building may be erected within 900mm of, or abut, the rear boundary for a maximum of 50% of the length of the boundary.

heading.b: Certain attached development may be built within parallel road setback

block.txt: Despite clause 3B.24(8), a cabana, cubby house, fernery, garden shed, gazebo, greenhouse or shed may be built within 3m of, or abut, a parallel road boundary for a maximum of 50% of the length of that boundary if the parallel road is not a classified road.

heading.b: Setbacks do not apply to existing parts of dual occupancy, manor house or attached development

block.txt: The setback standards specified in clause 3B.24 do not apply to any existing parts of a dual occupancy, manor house or attached development that will remain on a lot after the complying development is carried out.
Dwelling house, primary road and setback are defined in clause 1.5.
Classified road and public reserve have the same meanings as they have in the Standard Instrument.

heading.b: Other development standards for new balconies, decks, patios, terraces and verandahs attached to side or rear of dual occupancy or manor house

block.txt: The maximum height of the floor level of a balcony, deck, patio, terrace or verandah is 4m above ground level (existing).
The floor level of the balcony, deck, patio, terrace or verandah must be the same as the floor level of the part of the dual occupancy or manor house to which it is attached.

Any attached side or rear balcony, deck, patio, terrace or verandah that has a floor level of more than 2m above ground level (existing) must have a setback from side and rear boundaries of at least 3m.

The total floor area of all attached side or rear balconies, decks, patios, terraces and verandahs having a floor level of more than 2m above ground level (existing) must not be more than 12m2 for each dwelling.
Attached, building line and floor area are defined in clause 1.5.
Ground level (existing) has the same meaning as it has in the Standard Instrument.
A balcony may require a privacy screen—see clause 3B.29.
A manor house must face a public road.
The minimum landscaped area that must be provided on a lot is 50% of the lot area minus 100m2.
At least 25% of the area of the lot forward of the building line must be landscaped.
At least 50% of the area required to be landscaped under subclause (1) must be located behind the building line.
Each landscaped area must have—
a minimum width of 1.5m, and
a minimum length of 1.5m.
The principal private open space that must be provided for each dwelling is—
for a 1 bedroom dwelling or a studio—8m2 with a minimum width of 2m, and
for a dwelling with 2 bedrooms—12m2 with a minimum width of 2m, and
for a dwelling with 3 or more bedrooms—16m2 with a minimum width of 2m.
This clause does not apply to complying development that is the alteration of, or addition to, a dual occupancy or manor house if the development does not—
increase the footprint of the dual occupancy or manor house, or
decrease the landscaped area on the lot, or
decrease the principal private open space for a dwelling, or
change the number of dwellings on the lot.
Building line and principal private open space are defined in clause 1.5.
Landscaped area has the same meaning as it has in the Standard Instrument.
A dual occupancy or manor house may have a primary road articulation zone that extends up to 1.5m forward of the minimum required setback from the primary road.
The following building elements can be located in the primary road articulation zone—
an entry feature or portico,
a balcony, deck, pergola, terrace or verandah,
a window box treatment,
a bay window or similar feature,
an awning or other feature over a window,
a sun shading feature,
an eave.

The maximum total area of all building elements in the articulation zone, other than a building element specified in subclause (2)(e), (f) or (g), must not comprise more than 25% of the area of the articulation zone.
Each habitable room that has a wall facing a road must have a window in that wall.
Articulation zone, building element, habitable room, primary road and setback are defined in clause 1.5.

heading.b: Privacy screens for windows and certain attached development
Windows in habitable rooms near boundaries or other dwellings

block.txt: A window in a habitable room must have a privacy screen over any part of that window that is less than 1.5m above the floor level of the room in the following cases—
the floor level of the habitable room is 1m or more, but not more than 3m, above ground level (existing) and the window faces a side or rear boundary and is less than 3m from that boundary,
the floor level of the habitable room is more than 3m above ground level (existing) and the window faces a side or rear boundary and is less than 6m from that boundary,
the floor level of the habitable room is 1m or more, but not more than 3m, above ground level (existing) and the window faces a dwelling on the same lot and is less than 6m from that dwelling,
the floor level of the habitable room is more than 3m above ground level (existing) and the window faces a dwelling on the same lot and is less than 12m from that dwelling.
Subclause (1) does not apply to—
a habitable room with a floor level not more than 1m above ground level (existing), or
a window that faces a road or public space, or
a bedroom window that has an area of not more than 2m2.

heading.b: Balconies, decks, patios, terraces or verandahs near boundaries or other dwellings

block.txt: The edge of a balcony, deck, patio, terrace or verandah must have a privacy screen with a height of at least 1.5m above the floor level of a balcony, deck, patio, terrace or verandah in the following cases—

the floor level of the balcony, deck, patio, terrace or verandah is 1m or more, but not more than 3m, above ground level (existing) and the edge faces a side or rear boundary and is less than 3m from that boundary,
the floor level of the balcony, deck, patio, terrace or verandah is more than 3m above ground level (existing) and the edge faces a side or rear boundary and is less than 6m from that boundary,

the floor level of the balcony, deck, patio, terrace or verandah is 1m or more, but not more than 2m, above ground level (existing) and the edge faces a dwelling on the same lot and is less than 6m from that dwelling,
the floor level of the balcony, deck, patio, terrace or verandah is more than 2m above ground level (existing) and the edge faces a dwelling on the same lot and is less than 12m from that dwelling.
Subclause (3) does not apply to a balcony, deck, patio, terrace or verandah—
with a floor level not more than 1m above ground level (existing), or
that faces a road or public space, or
that has an area of not more than 2m2.

heading.b: Existing windows, balconies, decks, patios, terraces or verandahs

block.txt: This clause does not apply to any existing parts of a dwelling house, dual occupancy or attached development that will remain on the lot after the complying development is carried out.
Habitable room and privacy screen are defined in clause 1.5.
Ground level (existing) has the same meaning as it has in the Standard Instrument.

heading.b: Car parking and vehicle access requirements

block.txt: This clause applies to—
the erection of a dual occupancy or manor house, or
the alteration of, or addition to, a dwelling house, dual occupancy or manor house that causes an increase in the number of dwellings on the lot.
One parking space must be provided for each dwelling.
The car parking space may be an open hard stand space or a carport or garage, whether attached to or detached from the dual occupancy or manor house.
All off-street car parking spaces and vehicle access must comply with AS/NZS 2890.1:2004, Parking facilities, Part 1: Off-street car parking.

A garage, carport or car parking space at ground level (existing) and accessed from a primary road, secondary road or parallel road must have a minimum setback from the relevant road boundary as shown in the following table—

entry.txt: Setback of building from road boundary
Minimum off-street parking setback from road boundary

block.txt: The maximum width of all garage doors accessed from a primary road, parallel road or secondary road is 6m.
Attached, building line, detached, hard stand space, lane, parallel road, primary road, secondary road and setback are defined in clause 1.5.
Clause 2.28 applies to the construction or installation of a driveway as exempt development.
Alterations or additions to a garage or carport that is forward of the building line is not complying development under this code (see clause 3B.2(g)).
The design of a dual occupancy or a manor house must be consistent with the relevant design criteria in the Low Rise Housing Diversity Design Guide.
However, the requirements of this Part prevail to the extent that the Guide is inconsistent with this Part.

heading.b: Development standards for multi dwelling housing (terraces) and attached development

block.txt: This Division sets out the development standards that apply to the following types of complying development under this code—
the erection or alteration of, or an addition to, multi dwelling housing (terraces),
the erection or alteration of, or addition to, attached development that is related to multi dwelling housing (terraces).
Clauses 1.17A, 1.18 and 1.19(1) set out additional requirements for complying development.
The area of the parent lot must not be less than the following—

the minimum lot area specified for multi dwelling housing (terraces) in the environmental planning instrument, other than State Environmental Planning Policy (Housing) 2021, Chapter 6, Part 3, Division 2, that applies to the land concerned,

if no minimum lot area is specified for multi dwelling housing (terraces) in that environmental planning instrument—the minimum lot area specified for multi dwelling housing in the environmental planning instrument, other than State Environmental Planning Policy (Housing) 2021, Chapter 6, Part 3, Division 2, that applies to the land concerned,
600m2, but only if—
the minimum lot area specified in the environmental planning instrument referred to in paragraph (a) or (b) is less than 600m2, or
no minimum lot area is specified in that environmental planning instrument.
The width of the lot must not be less than 21m measured at the building line.
The maximum height for a multi dwelling housing (terraces) and any attached development is 9m above ground level (existing).
Ground level (existing) is defined in the Standard Instrument as the existing level of a site at any point.

heading.b: Maximum gross floor area of all buildings

block.txt: The maximum gross floor area of all buildings on a parent lot is shown in the following table—

entry.txt: Land use zone in which development is carried out
Zone RU5, Zone R1 or Zone R2

heading.b: Minimum setbacks and maximum height and length of boundary walls

block.txt: The setback of multi dwelling housing (terraces) and any attached development (on land in Zone RU5, Zone R1 or Zone R2) from a primary road must not be less than the average setback from the primary road of the 2 nearest buildings within 40m of the lot and on the same side of the primary road that are any of the following—
dwelling house,
dual occupancy,
multi dwelling housing (terraces).
Clause 3B.37 contains certain exclusions from, and exceptions to, the setbacks in this clause.

For the purpose of determining the setbacks from a primary road of the 2 nearest buildings that are dwelling houses, dual occupancies or multi dwelling housing (terraces), the following are not to be included—
buildings on battle-axe lots,
any attached development or detached development on other lots,
building elements in the articulation zone.

If there are not 2 buildings that are dwelling houses, dual occupancies or multi dwelling housing (terraces) within 40m of the lot on the same side of the primary road or if the development is on land in Zone R3, the multi dwelling housing (terraces) and any attached development must have a minimum setback from the boundary with the primary road of 3.5m.
Multi dwelling housing (terraces) and any attached development must have a minimum setback from a side boundary of 1.5m.

Each part of multi dwelling housing (terraces) and any carport, garage, balcony, deck, patio, pergola, terrace or verandah must have a minimum setback from the rear boundary as shown in the following table—
Certain exceptions to the rear setbacks apply if the lot has a rear boundary with a lane (see clause 3B.37(4)).

heading.b: Secondary road setbacks for corner lots

block.txt: Despite any other setback specified in this clause, multi dwelling housing (terraces) and any attached development must have a minimum setback from a boundary with a secondary road as shown in the following table—

entry.txt: Minimum setback from secondary road boundary

heading.b: Parallel road setbacks for parallel road lots

block.txt: Despite any other setback specified in this clause, multi dwelling housing (terraces) and any attached development must have a setback from a boundary with a parallel road of at least 3m unless 1 of the dwellings in the multi dwelling housing (terraces) faces the parallel road, in which case the setback must be the same as if the parallel road were a primary road.
Despite any other setback specified in this clause, multi dwelling housing (terraces) and any attached development must have a setback from a boundary with a classified road of at least 9m.
Despite any other setback specified in this clause, multi dwelling housing (terraces) and any attached development must have a setback from a boundary with a public reserve of at least 3m.

Articulation zone, attached development, battle-axe lot, boundary wall, building element, building line, detached development, dwelling house, lane, primary road, setback and standard lot are defined in clause 1.5.
Building height, classified road and ground level (existing) have the same meanings as they have in the Standard Instrument.

heading.b: Development to which side and rear setbacks do not apply

block.txt: The setback standards specified in clause 3B.36(4) and (5) do not apply to the following—
access ramps,
downpipes,
driveways or hard stand spaces,
electricity or gas meters,
fascias,
fences,
gutters,
light fittings,
pathways and paving,
steps.

heading.b: Development to which side and rear setbacks do not apply if 450mm from boundary

block.txt: The setback standards specified in clause 3B.36(4) and (5) do not apply to the following if they are at least 450mm from the relevant boundary—
aerials,
antennae,
awnings,
chimneys,
cooling or heating appliances,
eaves,
flues,
pipes,
privacy screens,
rainwater tanks,
structures associated with the provision of a utility service.

heading.b: Development to which road setbacks do not apply

block.txt: The setback standards specified in clause 3B.36(1), (3), (6), (7) and (8) do not apply to the following—
access ramps,
driveways,
eaves,
pathways and paving,
retaining walls,
any building elements that are permitted within a primary road articulation zone,
steps.
Despite clause 3B.36(5), if the lot has a rear boundary with a lane, the building may be erected within 900mm of, or abut, the rear boundary for a maximum length of 7m.

heading.b: Setbacks do not apply to existing parts of multi dwelling housing (terraces) or attached development

block.txt: The setbacks standards specified in clause 3B.36 do not apply to any existing parts of any multi dwelling housing (terraces) or attached development that will remain on a lot after the complying development is carried out.
Articulation zone, attached development, dwelling house, primary road and setback are defined in clause 1.5.
Classified road and public reserve have the same meanings as they have in the Standard Instrument.
Environmental planning instrument has the same meaning as it has in the Act.
Each dwelling must face a public road.
No dwelling must be located behind another dwelling on the same lot.
Each terrace must share a common wall with each adjoining terrace.
Each terrace, including any car parking space accessed from the primary road, must have a minimum width, measured at the building line, of 6m.
The width of a terrace is to be measured from the centre of a side wall if that wall adjoins another terrace or from the outside of the side wall if that wall is an external wall.
In this clause—
terrace means a single dwelling in multi dwelling housing (terraces).

heading.b: Other development standards for new attached side or rear balconies, decks, patios, terraces or verandahs

block.txt: The maximum height of the floor level of a balcony, deck, patio, terrace or verandah is 4m above ground level (existing).
The floor level of the balcony, deck, patio, terrace or verandah must be the same as the floor level of the part of the multi dwelling housing (terraces) to which it is attached.

Any attached side or rear balcony, deck, patio, terrace or verandah that has a floor level of more than 2m above ground level (existing) must have a setback from side and rear boundaries of at least 3m.
The total floor area of all attached decks having a floor level of more than 2m above ground level (existing) must not be more than 12m2 for each dwelling.
Attached, building line and floor area are defined in clause 1.5.
Ground level (existing) has the same meaning as it has in the Standard Instrument.
A balcony may require a privacy screen—see clause 3B.42.
The minimum landscaped area that must be provided for each resulting lot where concurrent Torrens title subdivision is proposed is shown in the following table—

entry.txt: Land use zone in which development is carried out
Zone RU5, Zone R1 or Zone R2

block.txt: The minimum landscaped area that must be provided on a lot where concurrent Torrens title subdivision is not proposed is shown in the following table—

entry.txt: Land use zone in which development is carried out
Zone RU5, Zone R1 or Zone R2
30% of the parent lot area of which at least 54m2 is apportioned to each dwelling
20% of the parent lot area of which at least 36m2 is apportioned to each dwelling

block.txt: At least 25% of the area of the lot forward of the building line must be landscaped.
At least 50% of the area required to be landscaped under subclause (1) or (1A) must be located behind the building line.
Each landscaped area must have—
a minimum width of 1.5m, and
a minimum length of 1.5m.
The area of principal private open space that must be provided for each terrace is at least 16m2 with a minimum width of 3m.
This clause does not apply to complying development that is the alteration of, or addition to, multi dwelling housing (terraces) or attached development if the development does not—
increase the footprint of the multi dwelling housing (terraces) or attached development, or
decrease the landscaped area on the lot, or
decrease the area of principal private open space for a terrace.
Building line and principal private open space are defined in clause 1.5.
Landscaped area has the same meaning as it has in the Standard Instrument.
In this clause—
terrace means a single dwelling in multi dwelling housing (terraces).

heading.b: Primary and secondary road articulation zones

block.txt: Multi dwelling housing (terraces) may have a primary road articulation zone and a secondary road articulation zone that each extend up to 1.5m forward of the minimum required setback from the primary road or secondary road.
The following building elements can be located in the primary road articulation zone or secondary road articulation zone—
an entry feature or portico,
a balcony, deck, pergola, terrace or verandah,
a window box treatment,
a bay window or similar feature,
an awning or other feature over a window,
a sun shading feature,
an eave.

The maximum total area of all building elements in the articulation zone, other than a building element specified in subclause (2)(e), (f) or (g), must not comprise more than 25% of the area of the articulation zone.
Each habitable room that has a wall facing a road must have a window in that wall.
Articulation zone, building element, primary road, secondary road and setback are defined in clause 1.5.

heading.b: Privacy screens for windows and certain attached development
Windows in habitable rooms near boundaries or other dwellings

block.txt: A window in a habitable room must have a privacy screen over any part of that window that is less than 1.5m above the floor level of the room in the following cases—
the floor level of the habitable room is 1m or more, but not more than 3m, above ground level (existing) and the window faces a side or rear boundary and is less than 3m from that boundary,
the floor level of the habitable room is more than 3m above ground level (existing) and the window faces a side or rear boundary and is less than 6m from that boundary,
the floor level of the habitable room is 1m or more, but not more than 3m, above ground level (existing) and the window faces a dwelling on the same lot and is less than 6m from that dwelling,
the floor level of the habitable room is more than 3m above ground level (existing) and the window faces a dwelling on the same lot and is less than 12m from that dwelling.
Subclause (1) does not apply to—
a habitable room with a floor level not more than 1m above ground level (existing), or
a window that faces a road or public space, or
a bedroom window that has an area of not more than 2m2.

heading.b: Balconies, decks, patios, terraces or verandahs near boundaries or other dwellings

block.txt: The edge of a balcony, deck, patio, terrace or verandah must have a privacy screen with a height of at least 1.5m above the floor level of a balcony, deck, patio, terrace or verandah in the following cases—

the floor level of the balcony, deck, patio, terrace or verandah is 1m or more, but not more than 3m, above ground level (existing) and the edge faces a side or rear boundary and is less than 3m from that boundary,
the floor level of the balcony, deck, patio, terrace or verandah is more than 3m above ground level (existing) and the edge faces a side or rear boundary and is less than 6m from that boundary,

the floor level of the balcony, deck, patio, terrace or verandah is 1m or more, but not more than 2m, above ground level (existing) and the edge faces a dwelling on the same lot and is less than 6m from that dwelling,
the floor level of the balcony, deck, patio, terrace or verandah is more than 2m above ground level (existing) and the edge faces a dwelling on the same lot and is less than 12m from that dwelling.
Subclause (3) does not apply to a balcony, deck, patio, terrace or verandah—
with a floor level not more than 1m above ground level (existing), or
that faces a road or public space, or
that has an area of not more than 2m2.

heading.b: Existing windows, balconies, decks, patios, terraces or verandahs

block.txt: This clause does not apply to any existing parts of multi dwelling housing (terraces) or attached development that will remain on the lot after the complying development is carried out.
Habitable room and privacy screen are defined in clause 1.5.
Ground level (existing) has the same meaning as it has in the Standard Instrument.

heading.b: Car parking and vehicle access requirements

block.txt: This clause applies to—
the erection of multi dwelling housing (terraces), or
the alteration of, or addition to, multi dwelling housing (terraces) that causes an increase in the number of dwellings on the lot.
At least 1 off-street car parking space must be provided for each dwelling.
The off-street car parking space may be an open hard stand space or a carport or garage, that is attached development or detached development.
All off-street car parking spaces and vehicle access must comply with AS/NZS 2890.1:2004, Parking facilities, Part 1: Off-street car parking.

A garage, carport or car parking space at ground level (existing) and accessed from a primary road, secondary road or parallel road must have a minimum setback from the relevant road boundary as shown in the following table unless the road is a lane—

entry.txt: Setback of multi dwelling housing (terraces) from road boundary
Minimum off-street parking setback from road boundary
1m or more behind the building line of the multi dwelling housing (terraces)

block.txt: The maximum width of all garage door openings facing a primary, secondary or parallel road is shown in the following table—

entry.txt: Maximum width of garage door openings

block.txt: Attached, building line, detached, hard stand space, lane, parallel road, primary road, secondary road and setback are defined in clause 1.5.
Clause 2.28 applies to the construction or installation of a driveway as exempt development.
Alterations or additions to a garage or carport that is forward of the building line is not complying development under this code (see clause 3B.2(g)).
The design of multi dwelling housing (terraces) must be consistent with the relevant design criteria in the Low Rise Housing Diversity Design Guide.
However, the requirements of this Part prevail to the extent that the Guide is inconsistent with this Part.
This Division sets out the development standards that apply to the erection of detached development and to the alteration of, or an addition to, detached development under this code.
Clauses 1.17A, 1.18 and 1.19(1) set out additional requirements for complying development.

heading.b: Built form development standards for detached development (other than swimming pools and fences)

block.txt: The parent lot must meet the following requirements—
the area of the lot must not be less than 400m2,
the width of the lot must not be less than 12m measured at the building line.
The maximum height for any detached development is 4.5m above ground level (existing).
Detached development is defined in clause 1.5.
Ground level (existing) is defined in the Standard Instrument as the existing level of a site at any point.

heading.b: Maximum gross floor area of certain detached development

block.txt: The maximum gross floor area of all of the following detached development that relates to multi dwelling housing (terraces) or a dual occupancy where no part of a dwelling is located above any part of another dwelling is 45m2—
a deck, patio, pergola, terrace or verandah,
a cabana, cubby house, fernery, garden shed, gazebo or greenhouse,
a carport or garage,
a shed.

The maximum gross floor area of all of the following detached development that relates to a manor house or dual occupancy (attached) where part of a dwelling is located above part of another dwelling is shown in the table to this clause—
a deck, patio, pergola, terrace or verandah,
a cabana, cubby house, fernery, garden shed, gazebo or greenhouse,
a carport or garage,
a shed.
The maximum gross floor area of detached studios is set out in clause 3B.52.

heading.b: Minimum setbacks and maximum height and length of built to boundary walls

block.txt: Detached development (other than a detached garage or carport) must be located behind the building line of a building that is residential accommodation that is adjacent to any primary road or secondary road.
Primary and secondary road setbacks for detached garages and carports are set out in clause 3B.50.
Clause 3B.54 contains certain exclusions from, and exceptions to, the setbacks specified in this clause.
Detached development that is any of the following must have a minimum setback from the side boundary of a lot of 900mm—
a deck, patio, pergola, terrace or verandah,
a cabana, cubby house, fernery, garden shed, gazebo or greenhouse,
a carport or garage,
a rainwater tank (above ground),
a shade structure or a shed.
Side boundary setbacks for detached studios are set out in clause 3B.52.
Despite subclause (2), detached development that is referred to in that subclause may be built to 1 or both side boundaries if—
the detached development relates to a dual occupancy or multi dwelling housing (terraces), and
any building wall on the adjoining lot that is within 900mm of that boundary is of masonry construction and does not have a window facing that boundary, and
any wall erected within 900mm of a side boundary will not contain a door, window or any other opening facing that boundary,
but if the lot width measured at the building line is more than 8m, but not more than 12.5m the detached development may be built to 1 side boundary only.

heading.b: Maximum height of built to boundary walls

block.txt: The height of a wall erected within 900mm of a side boundary must not exceed—
3.3m above ground level (existing), or
if there is a building wall on the adjoining lot within 900mm of that boundary that is higher than 3.3m—the height of that wall, but not more than 4.5m, or

if the building on the adjoining lot is subject to the same complying development certificate under clause 126(4) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Regulation 2000—the height of the wall on the adjoining lot, but not more than 4.5m, or
if the detached development is a detached studio that is above a garage—the height of the built to boundary wall on the adjoining lot, but not more than 6m.

heading.b: Maximum length of built to boundary walls

block.txt: The length of all walls on the lot that are within 900mm of a side boundary must not exceed 10m.
Despite subclause (5), the length of a wall erected within 900mm of a side boundary must not exceed—
if the length of the built to boundary wall on the adjoining lot is longer than the maximum length calculated under subclause (5)—the length of that wall, or

if the building on the adjoining lot is subject to the same complying development certificate under clause 126(4) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Regulation 2000—the length of the wall on the adjoining lot.

Any of the following detached development that relates to a dual occupancy where no part of a dwelling is located above any part of another dwelling or that relates to multi dwelling housing (terraces) must have a minimum setback from the rear boundary of a lot of 900mm (unless there is a wall of a building on the adjoining lot that is within 900mm of the boundary and that wall is of masonry construction and does not have a window facing the boundary)—
a cabana, cubby house, fernery, garden shed, gazebo or greenhouse,
a rainwater tank (above ground),
a shade structure or a shed.

Any of the following detached development that relates to a dual occupancy (attached) where part of a dwelling is located above part of another dwelling or that relates to a manor house must have a minimum setback from the rear boundary of a lot as shown in the table to this subclause—
a cabana, cubby house, fernery, garden shed, gazebo or greenhouse,
a rainwater tank (above ground),
a shade structure or a shed.
Rear setbacks for detached garages and carports, detached decks, patios, pergolas, terraces and verandahs and detached studios are set out in clauses 3B.50, 3B.51 and 3B.52, respectively.

heading.b: Parallel road setbacks for parallel road lots

block.txt: Detached development on a lot must have a minimum setback from a parallel road of 3m.
Clause 3B.54(4) contains exceptions to this setback for certain types of detached development.
Despite any standard for a setback specified by this clause, detached development must have a setback from a boundary with a classified road of at least—

in the case of detached development related to a dual occupancy—the setback for a dual occupancy from a classified road specified by any other environmental planning instrument applying to the land, or
in the case of detached development related to a manor house—the setback for a manor house from a classified road specified by any other environmental planning instrument applying to the land, or

in the case of detached development related to multi dwelling housing (terraces)—the setback for multi dwelling housing (terraces) from a classified road specified by any other environmental planning instrument applying to the land, or
if no setback is specified for the purposes of paragraph (a), (b) or (c)—9m.
Despite any standard for a setback specified by this clause, the following detached development must have a setback from a boundary with a public reserve of at least 3m—
a cabana, cubby house, fernery, garden shed, gazebo or greenhouse,
a carport or garage,
a deck, patio, pergola, terrace or verandah,
a rainwater tank (above ground),
a shade structure or shed.
Public reserve has the same meaning as it has in the Standard Instrument.

heading.b: Other development standards for detached garages and carports
Car parking and vehicle access requirements

block.txt: All off-street car parking spaces and vehicle access must comply with AS/NZS 2890.1:2004, Parking facilities, Part 1: Off-street car parking.
A detached garage or carport that is accessed from a primary road must have a minimum setback as shown in the following table—

entry.txt: Primary road setback of dwelling house
Minimum required garage or carport setback from primary road boundary
At least 1m behind the building line of the building that is the residential accommodation to which the garage or carport relates

block.txt: A detached garage or carport on a corner lot must have a minimum setback from a secondary road or parallel road as shown in the following table—

entry.txt: Minimum setback from secondary or parallel road boundary

block.txt: A detached garage or carport must have a minimum setback from the rear boundary as shown in the following table—

Despite subclause (4), a detached garage or carport of masonry construction may be built to the rear boundary if there is a wall of a building on the adjoining lot within 900mm of that boundary, the wall is of masonry construction and does not have a window facing that boundary.
A detached garage must be at least 3m from any building that is residential accommodation on the same lot.

The maximum width of all detached garage and carport door openings (except where the garage or carport is to the rear of the building that is residential accommodation to which it relates) facing a primary, secondary or parallel road is 6m.
Boundary wall, building line, corner lot, detached, dwelling house, gross floor area, lane, parallel road, primary road, secondary road and setback are defined in clause 1.5.
Building height and ground level (existing) have the same meanings as they have in the Standard Instrument.

heading.b: Other development standards for detached decks, patios, pergolas, terraces and verandahs

block.txt: The maximum floor level for any detached deck, patio, pergola, terrace or verandah is 1m above ground level (existing) unless the deck, patio, pergola, terrace or verandah is less than 900mm from a side or rear boundary in which case the maximum floor level is 600mm above ground level (existing).
Ground level (existing) has the same meaning as it has in the Standard Instrument.
A detached deck, patio, pergola, terrace or verandah must have a minimum setback from the rear boundary of a lot as shown in the following table—

heading.b: Other development standards for detached studios

block.txt: At the completion of the development, there must be no more than 1 detached studio for each dwelling in the dual occupancy or multi dwelling housing (terraces).
Despite clause 3B.47, if a detached studio is within 900mm of a lane and is above a garage, the maximum height is 6m above ground level (existing).
The maximum gross floor area of a detached studio is 36m2.
A detached studio must have a minimum setback from each side boundary as shown in the following table—

entry.txt: Lot width at the building line
Minimum setback from each side boundary

block.txt: A detached studio must have a minimum setback from the rear boundary of 3m.

Despite subclause (5), if the lot has a rear boundary with a lane, the detached studio may be erected within 900mm of, or abut, the rear boundary for a maximum length of 50% of the length of that boundary.
Despite subclause (4), a detached studio that is within 900mm of a rear lane may be built to 1 or both side boundaries if—
the lot is not a corner lot, and
the lot width measured at the building line is at least 6m, but not more than 8m, and
if there is a building wall on the adjoining lot within 900mm of that boundary—that wall is of masonry construction and does not have a window facing that boundary, and
any wall erected within 900mm of a side boundary will not contain a door, window or any other opening.
Despite subclause (4), a detached studio that is within 900mm of a rear lane may be built to 1 side boundary if—
the lot width measured at the building line is more than 8m, but not more than 12.5m, and
any building wall on the adjoining lot within 900mm of that boundary is of masonry construction and does not have a window facing that boundary, and
any wall erected within 900mm of the side boundary will not contain a door, window or any other opening.

heading.b: Maximum height of built to boundary walls

block.txt: The height of a wall erected within 900mm of a side boundary must not exceed—
3.3m above ground level (existing), or
if the height of the built to boundary wall on the adjoining lot is higher than 3.3m—the height of that wall, but not more than 4.5m, or

if the building on the adjoining lot is subject to the same complying development certificate under clause 126(4) of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Regulation 2000—the height of the wall on the adjoining lot, but not more than 4.5m, or
if the wall is part of a detached studio that is above a garage—the height of the built to boundary wall on the adjoining lot, but not more than 6m.
A detached studio must be at least 3m from any building on the same lot that is residential accommodation.
A privacy screen must be provided for any part of a window in a detached studio that is less than 1.5m above the floor level of that room in the following cases—

the floor level of the studio is 1m or more, but not more than 3m, above ground level (existing) and the window faces a side or rear boundary (other than a boundary to a lane) and is less than 3m from that boundary,
the floor level of the studio is 3m or more above ground level (existing) and the window faces a side or rear boundary (other than a boundary to a lane) and is less than 6m from that boundary.
Any window in a detached studio with a floor level of more than 1.5m above ground level (existing) must not have an area of more than 2m2.

heading.b: Other development standards for detached cabanas, cubby houses, ferneries, garden sheds, gazebos, greenhouses, rainwater tanks, shade structures or sheds

block.txt: A cabana, cubby house, fernery, garden shed, gazebo, greenhouse, rainwater tank (above ground), shade structure or shed must have a minimum setback from the rear boundary of 3m unless the lot has a rear boundary with a lane, in which case it may be erected within 900mm of, or abut, the rear boundary for a maximum length of 7m.

heading.b: Development to which side and rear setbacks do not apply

block.txt: The side and rear setback standards specified in this Subdivision do not apply to the following—
access ramps,
downpipes,
driveways and hard stand spaces,
electricity or gas meters,
fascias,
fences,
gutters,
light fittings,
pathways and paving,
steps.

heading.b: Development to which side and rear setbacks do not apply if 450mm from boundary

block.txt: The side and rear setback standards specified in this Subdivision do not apply to the following if they are at least 450mm from the relevant boundary—
aerials,
antennae,
awnings,
chimneys,
cooling or heating appliances,
eaves,
flues,
pipes,
privacy screens,
rainwater tanks,
structures associated with the provision of a utility service.

heading.b: Development to which road setbacks do not apply

block.txt: The road setbacks specified in this Subdivision do not apply to the following—
access ramps,
driveways,
eaves,
fences,
pathways and paving,
retaining walls,
steps.

heading.b: Rear boundaries with parallel roads or rear lanes

block.txt: Despite any rear setback specified in this Subdivision, if a lot has a rear boundary with a parallel road or lane, the following detached development may be erected within 3m of, or abut, the rear boundary for up to 50% of the length of that boundary—
a cabana, cubby house, fernery, garden shed, gazebo or greenhouse,
a rainwater tank (above ground),
a shade structure or shed.

heading.b: Setbacks do not apply to existing parts of detached development

block.txt: The setbacks standards specified in this Subdivision do not apply to any existing parts of detached development that will remain on the lot after the complying development is carried out.
Articulation zone, attached development, dwelling house, primary road and setback are defined in clause 1.5.
Classified road and public reserve have the same meanings as they have in the Standard Instrument.

heading.b: Landscape development standards for detached development (other than fences and child-resistant barriers)

block.txt: The minimum landscaped area that must be provided on a lot is the minimum landscaped area required under this Part in respect of the residential accommodation to which the detached development relates.
Landscaped area and residential accommodation have the same meanings as they have in the Standard Instrument.

heading.b: Built form development standards for swimming pools and fences

block.txt: A swimming pool must be associated with a dual occupancy or manor house and be for the use of residents of the dual occupancy or manor house.
Water from a swimming pool must be discharged in accordance with an approval under the Local Government Act 1993 if the lot is not connected to a sewer main.
The pump must be—
housed in a soundproofed enclosure, and
located more than 450mm from each lot boundary.
See the regulations under the Protection of the Environment Operations Act 1997 for offences relating to the use of pumps on residential premises.
A heat pump water heater must be designed so as not to operate—
during peak time—at a noise level that is more than 5 dB(A) above the ambient background noise level measured at any property boundary, and
during off peak time—at a noise level that is audible in habitable rooms of adjoining residences.
Coping around a swimming pool must not be more than—
1.4m above ground level (existing), and
300mm wide if the coping is more than 600mm above ground level (existing).
The pool must be designed so that it cannot be filled to a height of more than 1.2m above ground level (existing).
A swimming pool must be located in the rear yard of the dual occupancy or manor house with a minimum setback of 1m from any side or rear boundary.

The construction of a swimming pool for an existing manor house or for an existing dual occupancy (attached) where part of a dwelling is located above part of another dwelling must not decrease the landscaped area, or the principal private open space for a dwelling, below the amounts specified in relation to the manor house or dual occupancy in clause 3B.27.
The minimum setback for a swimming pool from a secondary road is the setback of the dual occupancy or manor house from the secondary road.
Ground level (existing) and landscaped area have the same meanings as they have in the Standard Instrument.
A child-resistant barrier must be constructed or installed in accordance with the requirements of the Swimming Pools Act 1992.
Requirements relating to excavation for the purposes of a swimming pool are set out in clause 3B.58.
A fence must not be erected under this code if—
it is erected along a common boundary of a lot, that contains a heritage item or a draft heritage item, or
Clause 1.19(3A) prevents the erection of a fence under this code on a lot that contains a heritage item or a draft heritage item.
it is erected along the boundary of, or within the setback area of, a primary or secondary road within a heritage conservation area or draft heritage conservation area, or
it incorporates barbed wire in its construction or it is electrified, or
it is constructed of metal components that are not low reflective materials, or
it is erected on bush fire prone land and is constructed of combustible material, or
the design of the fence will restrict the flow of floodwater.

In the case of development on a flood control lot, the requirement in subclause (1)(f) is satisfied only if a joint report by a professional engineer specialising in hydraulic engineering and a professional engineer specialising in civil engineering states that the design of the fence will not restrict the flow of floodwater.
A fence erected behind the building line on a lot must—
not be higher than 1.8m above ground level (existing), and
if it is on a sloping site and stepped to accommodate the fall in the land—not be higher than 2.2m above ground level (existing) at each step.
A fence erected forward of the building line on a lot must—
not be higher than—
1.2m above ground level (existing), or
if it is erected adjacent to a public reserve—1.5m above ground level (existing), or
if it is located in the setback area of a classified road—2.1m above ground level (existing), and
not have an entrance gate that opens outward, and
be open for at least 20% of the area of the fence that is more than 400mm above ground level (existing), with a minimum aperture of 25mm, and
if it is located in the setback area of a classified road—be setback at least 1.5m from the relevant boundary with a landscaped area between the fence and the boundary.
Building line, primary road, secondary road and setback are defined in clause 1.5.
Ground level (existing) and heritage item have the same meanings as they have in the Standard Instrument.

heading.b: Development standards for associated works including earthworks, retaining walls, drainage, protection of walls, protection of trees and conditions under complying development certificates
Earthworks, retaining walls and structural support

block.txt: Excavation for the purposes of development under this code must not exceed a maximum depth, measured from ground level (existing), of—
if located not more than 1m from any boundary—1m, and
if located more than 1m but not more than 1.5m from any boundary—2m, and
if located more than 1.5m from any boundary—3m.
Excavation for the purposes of a pier in a pier and beam foundation may exceed the maximum depth specified in subclause (1) if a professional engineer has certified the depth of the excavation.
Despite subclauses (1) and (1A), the excavation must not exceed a maximum depth, measured from ground level (existing), of 1m if—
the land is identified as Class 3 or 4 on an Acid Sulfate Soils Map, or
the land is within 40m of a waterbody (natural), or
the excavation is an aquifer interference activity within the meaning of the Water Management Act 2000.
Before an excavation exceeding a maximum depth, measured from ground level (existing), of 1m is carried out on a lot—
a geotechnical investigation report for the lot must be obtained, and
the report must show—
no groundwater is present on the part of the lot where the excavation is to be carried out, or
groundwater is present on the part of the lot but is below the level of the excavation.
The geotechnical investigation report required under subclause (3) must—
be prepared by a professional engineer specialising in geotechnical engineering, and
be prepared in accordance with AS 1726:2017, Geotechnical site investigations.
Fill must not exceed a maximum height, measured from ground level (existing), of—
if the fill is for the purposes of the erection or alteration of, or an addition to, a dual occupancy or manor house under this code—1m, and
if the fill is for any other purpose under this code—600mm.
Despite subclause (4), the height of fill is not limited if the fill is contained—
wholly within the footprint of a building, attached development or detached development, or
by a drop edge beam.

Fill that is higher than 150mm above ground level (existing) and is not contained wholly within the footprint of a building or any attached development or detached development is limited to 50% of the landscaped area of the lot.
The ground level (finished) of the fill must not be used to measure the height of any building or any attached development or detached development under this code.
Support for earthworks more than 600mm above or below ground level (existing) must take the form of a retaining wall or other structural support that—
a professional engineer has certified as structurally sound, including in relation to (but not limited to) the ability to withstand the forces of lateral soil load, and
has been designed so as not to redirect the flow of any surface water or ground water, or cause sediment to be transported, onto an adjoining property, and
has adequate drainage lines connected to the stormwater drainage system for the site, and

does not result in a retaining wall or structural support with a total height measured vertically from the base of the retaining wall or structural support to its uppermost portion that is more than the height of the associated excavation or fill, and
is separated from any retaining wall or structural support on the site by at least 2m, measured horizontally, and
has been installed in accordance with the manufacturer’s specifications (if any), and
if it is an embankment or batter—has a toe or top that is more than 1m from any side or rear boundary.

If a retaining wall has a height of more than 600mm above ground level (existing) and is located within the front setback of a building, a landscaped area with a minimum depth of 600mm must be provided in front of the wall (on the low side).
Excavation, fill and ground level (existing) have the same meanings as they have in the Standard Instrument.
Fill and excavation that is not associated with a building may be exempt development under clauses 2.29 and 2.30.
All stormwater collecting as a result of development erected, altered or added to under this code must be directed by a gravity fed or charged system to—
a public drainage system, or
an inter-allotment drainage system, or
an on-site disposal system.
Drainage has the same meaning as it has in the Standard Instrument.

All stormwater drainage systems and connections to public drainage systems of inter-allotment drainage systems must either be approved under section 68 of the Local Government Act 1993 or comply with the requirements for the disposal of stormwater contained in the development control plan that is applicable to the land.

Any wall constructed within 900mm of a lot boundary must be built in accordance with the support method proposed by the professional engineer’s report provided with the application for the complying development certificate.
Professional engineer is defined in clause 1.5.
Complying development certificate has the same meaning as it has in the Act.

heading.b: Setbacks of dual occupancies, manor houses, multi dwelling housing (terraces), attached development and detached development from protected trees

block.txt: A complying development certificate for complying development under Division 1 is taken to satisfy any requirement under this Policy for a permit, approval or development consent to remove or prune a tree or other vegetation on the lot if—
the tree is not listed on a register of significant trees kept by the council, and
the tree or vegetation will be within 3m of any building that has an area of more than 25m2, and
the tree or vegetation has a height that is less than—
for development that is the erection of a new dual occupancy or manor house—8m and is not required to be retained as a condition of consent, or
in any other case—6m.
Development under this code must be at least 3m from each protected tree on the lot and any adjacent lot (measured from the base of the trunk of the tree).
Despite subclause (2), the following development can be located within 3m of a protected tree if works do not involve excavation or fill of more than 150mm below or above ground level (existing)—
an access ramp,
a driveway, pathway or paving,
an awning, blind or canopy,
a fence, screen, or child-resistant barrier associated with a swimming pool or spa pool.
Development consent, dwelling house and protected tree are defined in clause 1.5.
Council, excavation, fill, ground level (existing), spa pool and swimming pool have the same meanings as they have in the Standard Instrument.
Complying development certificate has the same meaning as it has in the Act.
A separate permit, approval or development consent may be required if the branches or roots of a protected tree on the lot or on an adjoining lot are required to be pruned or removed.
A complying development certificate for development specified under this code must be issued subject to the conditions specified in Schedule 6A.

heading.b: Deferred application of Part to land in certain local government areas

block.txt: This Part (other than this clause) does not apply to or in respect of land in a deferred area.
For the purposes of this clause, land is in a deferred area if the land is in any of the following local government areas—

Bathurst Regional, Bayside, Bellingen, City of Blue Mountains, Burwood, Byron, Camden, City of Campbelltown, Canada Bay, Canterbury-Bankstown, Central Coast, City of Coffs Harbour, Cumberland, Georges River, City of Hawkesbury, Hilltops, Hornsby, Hunter’s Hill, Inner West, Kiama, City of Liverpool, Mid-Coast, Mid-Western Regional, Moree Plains, Mosman, Northern Beaches, City of Parramatta, City of Penrith, City of Randwick, City of Ryde, City of Shellharbour, City of Shoalhaven, Snowy Monaro Regional, Strathfield, Sutherland Shire, City of Sydney, Tamworth Regional, The Hills Shire, Tweed, Upper Lachlan Shire, City of Willoughby, Wingecarribee, Wollondilly, City of Wollongong, Woollahra, Yass Valley.
This clause ceases to have effect on 1 July 2020.
A word or expression used in this part has the same meaning as in the Standard Instrument unless it is otherwise defined in this part.
In this part—
pattern means a pattern published by the Department in July 2025.
This part applies as follows—
for Lot 411, DP 1278302—from the commencement of this part,
for other land—from 30 July 2025.

heading.b: Requirements for complying development under this code
Development that is complying development under this code

block.txt: This clause applies to land in Zone R1 General Residential, Zone R2 Low Density Residential and Zone R3 Medium Density Residential.

Development for the purposes of dual occupancies and associated attached development or detached development is development specified for this code if the development is carried out in accordance with the development standards, location requirements, technical drawing set and technical information specified in the pattern identified as—
“Semis 01 by Anthony Gill Architects”, or
“Semis 02 by Sibling Architecture”.

Development for the purposes of manor houses and associated attached development or detached development is development specified for this code if the development is carried out in accordance with the development standards, location requirements, technical drawing set and technical information specified in the pattern identified as “Manor Homes 01 by Studio Johnston”.

Development for the purposes of multi dwelling housing and associated attached development or detached development is development specified for this code if the development is carried out in accordance with the development standards, location requirements, technical drawing set and technical information specified in the pattern identified as “Row Homes 01 by SAHA”.

Development for the purposes of multi dwelling housing (terraces) and associated attached development or detached development is development specified for this code if the development is carried out in accordance with the development standards, location requirements, technical drawing set and technical information specified in the pattern identified as—
“Terraces 01 by Carter Williamson”, or
“Terraces 02 by Sam Crawford Architects”, or
“Terraces 03 by Officer Woods Architects”, or
“Terraces 04 by Other Architects x NMBW”.

Development for the purposes of secondary dwellings associated with development carried out under subclause (5)(d) is development specified for this code if the development is carried out in accordance with the development standards, location requirements, technical drawing set and technical information specified in the pattern identified as “Terraces 04 by Other Architects x NMBW”.
Clauses 1.17A, 1.18 and 1.19 set out additional requirements for complying development.
Subclauses (2)–(5) do not apply to a lot if—
the size of the lot is less than—
if the development is for the purposes of dual occupancies—the minimum lot size for the erection of dual occupancies under an environmental planning instrument applying to the lot, or
if the development is for the purposes of manor houses—the minimum lot size for the erection of manor houses under an environmental planning instrument applying to the lot, or
if the development is for the purposes of multi dwelling housing—the minimum lot size for the erection of multi dwelling housing under an environmental planning instrument applying to the lot, or

if the development is for the purposes of multi dwelling housing (terraces)—the minimum lot size for the erection of multi dwelling housing (terraces) under an environmental planning instrument applying to the lot, or
the lot will not have lawful access to a public road at the completion of the development.
Subclause (7)(a) does not apply to a lot if the lot is on land within the low and mid rise housing area.
In this clause—
low and mid rise housing area has the same meaning as in State Environmental Planning Policy (Housing) 2021, Chapter 6.

This clause applies to land on which development for the purposes of dual occupancies, multi dwelling housing or multi dwelling housing (terraces) has been or will be carried out, but only if no part of a dwelling is located above any part of another dwelling.

If a single complying development certificate application proposes both the erection of a building to which this clause applies and the Torrens title subdivision of the land on which the development will be carried out, the subdivision of the land is complying development.
A Torrens title subdivision of land is also complying development if development located on the land satisfies the following—
the development is development to which this clause applies,
the development is development for which a complying development certificate has been issued under this part.
Subclauses (2) and (3) do not apply unless—
there will be only 1 dwelling on each resulting lot at the completion of the development, and
dual occupancies, multi dwelling housing or multi dwelling housing (terraces) are permissible, with consent, under an environmental planning instrument applying to the land.
Subclause (4)(a) does not apply if the development that has or will be carried out on the land includes a secondary dwelling permitted by clause 3BA.3(6). or clause 3BA.14(2).
A compliance certificate may be issued by an accredited certifier for a subdivision under this clause.
This clause applies to land on which development for the purposes of dual occupancies, manor houses, multi dwelling housing or multi dwelling housing (terraces) has been or will be carried out.

If a single complying development certificate application proposes both the erection of a building to which this clause applies and the strata subdivision of the land on which the development will be carried out, the strata subdivision of that land is complying development.
A strata subdivision of land is also complying development if development located on the land satisfies the following—
the development is development to which this clause applies,
the development is development for which a complying development certificate has been issued under this part.
Subclause (3) does not apply if the subdivision would contravene a condition of a complying development certificate that applies to the land.
A compliance certificate may be issued by an accredited certifier for a subdivision under this clause.

heading.b: Development that is not complying development under this code

block.txt: The following development is not complying development under this code—
development on bush fire prone land,
development on a flood control lot,
development that is complying development under the Housing Alterations Code,
development on a battle-axe lot,
development on any lot on which there is a secondary dwelling or group home, whether or not the development is attached to the dwelling or home,
the erection of a building over a registered easement,

development to which State Environmental Planning Policy (Housing) 2021, Chapter 2, Part 2, Division 1 applies, unless it is development that is being carried out by or on behalf of the New South Wales Land and Housing Corporation constituted by the Housing Act 2001,
development on unsewered land,
development on land identified as susceptible to landslide risk in—
an environmental planning instrument applying to the land, or
for land to which Warringah Local Environmental Plan 2011 applies—“Area C” or “Area E” on the Landslip Risk Map within the meaning of that plan.
A planning certificate from a council will state whether or not a lot is a flood control lot.

heading.b: Development standards for land near Siding Spring Observatory

block.txt: If complying development under this code is carried out on land in the local government area of Coonamble, Dubbo Regional, Gilgandra or Warrumbungle Shire, the development standards in this clause apply in addition to any other development standards.
Complying development specified for this code may only be carried out if it does not result in residential accommodation on land in the local government area of—
Coonamble, Dubbo Regional, Gilgandra or Warrumbungle Shire with an outside light fitting other than a shielded light fitting, and
Coonamble, Gilgandra or Warrumbungle Shire with more than 7 shielded outside light fittings or more than 5 such light fittings that are not automatic light fittings.

heading.b: Development standards for associated works, including earthworks, retaining walls, drainage, protection of walls, protection of trees and conditions under complying development certificates
Earthworks, retaining walls and structural support

block.txt: Excavation for the purposes of development under this code must not exceed a maximum depth, measured from ground level (existing), of—
if located not more than 1m from any boundary—1m, or
if located more than 1m but not more than 1.5m from any boundary—2m, or
if located more than 1.5m from any boundary—3m.
Excavation for the purposes of a pier in a pier and beam foundation may exceed the maximum depth specified in subclause (1) if a professional engineer has certified the depth of the excavation.
Despite subclauses (1) and (2), the excavation must not exceed a maximum depth, measured from ground level (existing), of 1m if—
the land is identified as Class 3 or 4 on an Acid Sulfate Soils Map, or
the land is within 40m of a waterbody (natural), or
the excavation is an aquifer interference activity within the meaning of the Water Management Act 2000.
Before an excavation exceeding a maximum depth, measured from ground level (existing), of 1m is carried out on a lot—
a geotechnical investigation report for the lot must be obtained, and
the report must show—
no groundwater is present on the part of the lot where the excavation is to be carried out, or
groundwater is present on the part of the lot but is below the level of the excavation.
The geotechnical investigation report required under subclause (4) must—
be prepared by a professional engineer specialising in geotechnical engineering, and
be prepared in accordance with AS 1726:2017, Geotechnical site investigations.
Fill must not exceed a maximum height, measured from ground level (existing), of—
if the fill is for the purposes of the erection or alteration of, or an addition to, a dual occupancy or manor house under this code—1m, or
if the fill is for any other purpose under this code—600mm.
Despite subclause (6), the height of fill is not limited if the fill is contained—
wholly within the footprint of a building, attached development or detached development, or
by a drop edge beam.

Fill that is higher than 150mm above ground level (existing), and is not contained wholly within the footprint of a building or any attached development or detached development, is limited to 50% of the landscaped area of the lot.
The ground level (finished) of the fill must not be used to measure the height of any building or any attached development or detached development under this code.
Support for earthworks more than 600mm above or below ground level (existing) must take the form of a retaining wall or other structural support that—
a professional engineer has certified as structurally sound, including in relation to (but not limited to) its ability to withstand the forces of lateral soil load, and
has been designed so as not to redirect the flow of any surface water or groundwater, or cause sediment to be transported, onto an adjoining property, and
has adequate drainage lines connected to the stormwater drainage system for the site, and

does not result in a retaining wall or structural support with a total height measured vertically from the base of the retaining wall or structural support to its uppermost portion that is more than the height of the associated excavation or fill, and
is separated from any retaining wall or structural support on the site by at least 2m, measured horizontally, and
has been installed in accordance with the manufacturer’s specifications (if any), and
if it is an embankment or batter—has a toe or top that is more than 1m from any side or rear boundary.

If a retaining wall has a height of more than 600mm above ground level (existing) and is located within the front setback of a building, a landscaped area with a minimum depth of 600mm must be provided in front of the wall on the low side.
All stormwater collecting as a result of development erected, altered or added to under this code must be directed by a gravity fed or charged system to—
a public drainage system, or
an inter-allotment drainage system, or
an on-site disposal system.

All stormwater drainage systems and connections to public drainage systems of inter-allotment drainage systems must either be approved under the Local Government Act 1993, section 68 or comply with the requirements for the disposal of stormwater contained in the development control plan applicable to the land.

A wall constructed within 900mm of a lot boundary must be built in accordance with the support method proposed by the professional engineer’s report provided with the application for the complying development certificate.

A complying development certificate for complying development under this part is taken to satisfy any requirement under this policy for a permit, approval or development consent to remove or prune a tree or other vegetation on the lot if—
the tree is not listed on a register of significant trees kept by the council, and
the tree or vegetation will be within 3m of any building that has an area of more than 25m2, and
the tree or vegetation has a height that is less than—
for development that is the erection of a new dual occupancy or manor house—8m and is not required to be retained as a condition of consent, or
in any other case—6m.
Development under this code must be at least 3m from each protected tree on the lot and any adjacent lot, measured from the base of the trunk of the tree.
Despite subclause (2), the following development can be located within 3m of a protected tree if works do not involve excavation or fill of more than 150mm below or above ground level (existing)—
an access ramp,
a driveway, pathway or paving,
an awning, blind or canopy,
a fence, screen, or child-resistant barrier associated with a swimming pool or spa pool.
Development consent and protected tree are defined in clause 1.5.

heading.b: Conditions specified in Schedule 6A and 6B apply

block.txt: A complying development certificate for development specified in clause 3BA.3 must be issued subject to the conditions specified in Schedule 6A, other than condition 28.
Schedule 6A, condition 17 is taken to apply to the erection of multi dwelling housing for the purposes of this code.
A complying development certificate for development specified in clause 3BA.4 or 3BA.5 must be issued subject to the conditions specified in Schedule 6B, other than condition 2.
This division applies to Lot 411, DP 1278302 (Landcom site).

Development for the purposes of multi dwelling housing (terraces) and associated attached or detached development is development specified for this code if the development is carried out in accordance with the development standards, location requirements, technical drawing set and technical information specified in the pattern identified as “Terraces 04 by Other Architects x NMBW”.

Development for the purposes of secondary dwellings associated with development carried out under subclause (1) is development specified for this code if the development is carried out in accordance with the development standards, location requirements, technical drawing set and technical information specified in the pattern identified as “Terraces 04 by Other Architects x NMBW”.
Clauses 1.17A, 1.18 and 1.19 set out additional requirements for complying development.
Clause 3BA.6(a) does not apply to development carried out under this clause.

Clause 1.18(1)(b) states that to be complying development for the purposes of this Policy the development must be permissible with consent under an environmental planning instrument applying to the land on which the development is carried out.

Clause 1.18(1)(c) states that to be complying development for the purposes of this Policy the development must meet the relevant provisions of the Building Code of Australia. Clause 136A of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Regulation 2000 requires a complying development certificate to be issued subject to the conditions specified in that clause, including a condition that building work must be carried out in accordance with the requirements of that Code.

In addition to the requirements specified for development under this code, adjoining owners’ property rights, the applicable common law and other legislative requirements for approvals, licences, permits and authorities still apply. For example, requirements relevant to development in this code may be contained in the Act, the Environmental Planning and Assessment Regulation 2000, various State environmental planning policies, the Protection of the Environment Operations Act 1997, the Roads Act 1993, the Swimming Pools Act 1992 and Acts applying to various infrastructure authorities. If the development is in proximity to infrastructure, including water, stormwater and sewer mains, electricity power lines and telecommunications facilities, the relevant infrastructure authority should be contacted before commencing the development.

heading.b: Requirements for complying development under this code
Land to which this code applies

block.txt: This code applies to land within the Greenfield Housing Code Area.
Land in the Greenfield Housing Code Area may still be subject to general exclusions from complying development provided for in this code.

heading.b: Development that is complying development under this code

block.txt: The following development is complying development under this code—
the erection of a new 1 or 2 storey dwelling house and any attached development,
the alteration of, or an addition to, a 1 or 2 storey dwelling house (including any addition that results in a 2 storey dwelling house) and any attached development,
the erection of detached development and the alteration of, or an addition to, any detached development.
For the purposes of calculating the number of storeys in a dwelling house under this code, any basement (including a garage) is to be counted as a storey.

Although a basement is to be counted as a storey for the purposes of calculating the number of storeys in a dwelling house, a basement is a type of attached development for the purposes of complying development under this code.

Storey is defined in the Standard Instrument as a space within a building that is situated between one floor level and the floor level next above, or if there is no floor above, the ceiling or roof above, but does not include—
a space that contains only a lift shaft, stairway or meter room, or
a mezzanine, or
an attic.
Complying development specified for this code may only be carried out on a lot that meets the following requirements—
the lot must be in Zone R1, R2, R3, R4 or RU5,
the area of the lot must not be less than 200m2,
the width of the lot must be at least 6m measured at the building line,
there must only be 1 dwelling house on the lot at the completion of the development,
the lot must have lawful access to a public road at the completion of the development,
if the development is on a battle-axe lot—the lot must be at least 12m by 12m (not including the access laneway) and must have an access laneway that is at least 3m wide,
if the development is on a corner lot—the width of the primary road boundary of the lot must be at least 6m.
A secondary dwelling with development consent or a complying development certificate is not a dwelling house for the purpose of subclause (3)(e).

heading.b: Erection of attached development and detached development

block.txt: Complying development specified for this code that is attached development or detached development may be carried out on a lot—
if a dwelling house exists on the lot—at any time, or
if there is a current development consent or complying development certificate for the construction of a dwelling house on the lot—before the construction of the dwelling house.
Attached development, battle-axe lot, building line, detached development, development consent and dwelling house are defined in clause 1.5.
