heading.b: Specified development and development standards under this code

block.txt: Bed and breakfast accommodation is development specified for this code if it is—
permissible with development consent under an environmental planning instrument applying to the land on which the development is carried out, and
not constructed or installed on bush fire prone land.
The standards specified for that development are that the development must—
be in an existing dwelling house, and

consist of not more than 4 guest bedrooms or, if there is a local environmental plan applying to the land that was made under section 3.20 of the Act, the maximum number of bedrooms specified in clause 5.4(1) of that plan, and
have at least 1 guest bathroom, and
have a fire extinguisher and fire blanket in the kitchen, and
have at least 1 off-road car parking space per guest bedroom, and
not display any advertisement on the premises (other than a notice or sign indicating the name and occupation of the resident), and

if the dwelling house is subject to the Strata Schemes Management Act 1996 or the Community Land Management Act 2021—have the prior approval of the owners corporation, or the community, precinct or neighbourhood association.

The use of a dwelling as bed and breakfast accommodation will result in a change of building class for the dwelling under the Building Code of Australia. There will be new fire safety and access requirements.
A home business that involves the manufacture of food is development specified for this code.
The standards specified for that development are that the development must—
not involve a change of building use, and
if the development is on land to which a local environmental plan made under section 3.20 of the Act applies—comply with the applicable standards under clause 5.4(2) of that plan, and
be carried out in premises that comply with the relevant requirements of AS 4674—2004, Design, construction and fit-out of food premises.
The Food Act 2003, and the regulations under that Act, may contain additional requirements in relation to premises on which food is manufactured.
The elements that must comprise this development are specified in the definition of home business in the Standard Instrument.
Under the Building Code of Australia, a change of building use involving a floor area greater than 10% of the floor area of a building would cause the building to contravene the development standard.

heading.b: Tents, marquees or booths for community events

block.txt: The construction or installation of a tent, marquee or booth used for a community event is development specified for this code if it is not exempt development and is carried out on any of the following land—
land in the following zones—
a business zone,
an employment zone, other than Zone E5,
a mixed use zone,
an industrial zone, other than a heavy industrial zone,
an open space zone,
a special purpose zone,
Zone W4,
land that is unzoned.
The standards specified for that development are that—
each tent, marquee or booth must not have a total floor area exceeding 500m2, and
for all tents, marquees and booths being used at the same time—the development must not have a total floor area exceeding 1,000m2, and

each tent, marquee or booth must be located at least 3m from any boundary of the land unless the land is under the ownership, control or management of a council or public authority and that council or public authority has provided its consent in writing to the temporary use of the land for the erection of the tent, marquee or booth, and

each tent, marquee or booth must be erected so as to ensure that there is a distance of at least 1.5m from any other tent, marquee or booth that is unobstructed so as to allow for pedestrian circulation unless that other tent, marquee or booth is attached with no separation, and
each tent or marquee with an area exceeding 300m2 must be located at least 6m from any other tent or marquee, and from any booth, to minimise the risk of fire spread, and

each tent or marquee with an area exceeding 300m2 must be provided with a system of emergency lighting and an additional electrical supply capable of providing emergency lighting in the event of a power failure, and
each tent or marquee must have the following number of exits arranged so as to afford a ready means of egress from all parts of the tent or marquee to open space or a road—
if the tent or marquee has a floor area of not more than 25m2—1 exit,
if the tent or marquee has a floor area of not more than 100m2—2 exits,
in any other case—4 exits, and
if any tent or marquee will include internal seating, stalls, tables or other obstructions, a clear path of travel to any exit no greater than 40m in length must be provided, and
each tent, marquee or booth must have a width for each exit of at least—
if the floor area of the tent, marquee or booth is less than 150m2—850mm, or
in any other case—1m, and
no tent or marquee can have a height for the walls exceeding 6m, and
each tent, marquee or booth must have a height, as measured from the surface on which the tent or marquee is erected to the highest point of the tent, marquee or booth, not exceeding 8m, and
each tent, marquee or booth must resist loads determined in accordance with the following Australian and New Zealand Standards—
AS/NZS 1170.0:2002, Structural design actions, Part 0: General principles,
AS/NZS 1170.1:2002, Structural design actions, Part 1: Permanent, imposed and other actions,
AS/NZS 1170.2:2011, Structural design actions, Part 2: Wind actions, and

if on land in the local government area of Coonamble, Gilgandra, Warrumbungle Shire or Dubbo Regional, any tent, marquee or booth must not have an outside light fitting other than a shielded light fitting and any such shielded light fitting must be downward facing.

heading.b: Stages or platforms for community events

block.txt: The construction or installation of a stage or platform used for a community event is development specified for this code if it is not exempt development and is carried out on any of the following land—
land in the following zones—
a business zone,
an employment zone, other than Zone E5,
a mixed use zone,
an industrial zone, other than a heavy industrial zone,
an open space zone,
a special purpose zone,
Zone W4,
land that is unzoned.
The standards specified for that development are that—
the stage or platform must not have a floor area exceeding 100m2, and

each stage or platform must be located at least 3m from any boundary of the land unless the land is under the ownership, control or management of a council or public authority, and that council or public authority has provided its consent in writing to the temporary use of the land for the erection of the stage or platform, and
the stage or platform must have a height as measured from the surface on which the stage or platform is erected to the floor of the stage or platform not exceeding 2m, and
the stage or platform must resist loads determined in accordance with the following Australian and New Zealand Standards—
AS/NZS 1170.0:2002, Structural design actions, Part 0: General principles,
AS/NZS 1170.1:2002, Structural design actions, Part 1: Permanent, imposed and other actions,
AS/NZS 1170.2:2011, Structural design actions, Part 2: Wind actions, and

if on land in the local government area of Coonamble, Gilgandra, Warrumbungle Shire or Dubbo Regional, any stage or platform must not have an outside light fitting other than a shielded light fitting and any such shielded light fitting must be downward facing.

The internal or external alteration or addition to a major event venue (other than Newington Armoury) situated on the Sydney Olympic Park site, including a new or replacement large format video screen within a stadium or auditorium, is development specified for this code if it is carried out on land within the Sydney Olympic Park site.
In this Subdivision, major event venue and Sydney Olympic Park site have the same meanings as in Part 23 of Schedule 3 to State Environmental Planning Policy (Major Development) 2005.
The standards specified for that development are that the development must—
not add more than 100m2 to the external envelope of the major event venue, and
not add a new seating area to the major event venue of more than 1,000m2.

Structural repairs to, the replacement of, or the carrying out of maintenance works in relation to, existing lawful boat sheds, cranes, davits, jetties, marinas, pontoons, slipway rails, winches, water recreation structures and wharf or boating facilities is development specified for this code if it is not carried out on or in a heritage item or a draft heritage item.
Development specified for this code may be carried out on land whether or not the land is within an environmentally sensitive area.
The standards specified for that development are that the development must—
not reduce the amount of light penetration to any water below, and
not change the classification of any building under the Building Code of Australia, and
not involve disturbance of or injury to the bed of any waterway or injury to any marine vegetation (as defined under the Fisheries Management Act 1994), and
not increase the height or site coverage of the building concerned, and
in the case of the repair or replacement of any crane, davit, slipway rails or winch—not be larger in size or capacity than the one being repaired or replaced, and
not result in a pile being exposed within the waterway, and
comply with AS 3962:2020, Marina design and AS 4997—2005, Guidelines for the design of maritime structures, and
if an approval is required under the Fisheries Management Act 1994—be approved under that Act, and
if an approval is required under the Protection of the Environment Operations Act 1997—be approved under that Act.
Despite subclause (1)(c), if the development is for the purpose of the removal or the replacement of damaged or degraded piles, the following additional standards are specified for that development—
the development must not cause a deterioration in water quality,
the development must use silt curtains or similar effective methods to control pollution,
the development must not dispose of spoil in the waterway.

heading.b: Conditions applying to complying development certificates under this code

block.txt: A complying development certificate for development specified under this code must be issued subject to the conditions specified in Schedule 7.

Clause 1.18(1)(b) states that to be complying development for the purposes of this Policy the development must be permissible with consent under an environmental planning instrument applying to the land on which the development is carried out.
Schedule 3 contains variations to this code.

In addition to the requirements specified for development under this code, adjoining owners’ property rights, the applicable common law and other legislative requirements for approvals, licences, permits and authorities still apply. For example, requirements relevant to development in this code may be contained in the Act, the Environmental Planning and Assessment Regulation 2000, various State environmental planning policies, the Protection of the Environment Operations Act 1997, the Roads Act 1993, theDisability (Access to Premises—Buildings) Standards 2010 of the Commonwealth and Acts applying to various infrastructure authorities. If the development is in the proximity of infrastructure, including water, stormwater and sewer mains, electricity power lines and telecommunications facilities, the relevant infrastructure authority should be contacted before commencing the development.

heading.b: Specified development and development standards under this code

block.txt: An internal alteration to a building that is used, or is the subject of a development consent for use, for any purpose (other than for the purpose of residential accommodation, sex services premises or restricted premises) is development specified for this code.
The standards specified for that development are as follows—

the alteration must not result in an increase in the gross floor area of any building within which it is carried out, except if the increase is required for the alteration to comply with the Premises Standards,

the alteration must not involve the conversion of any area that is excluded from the measurement of gross floor area of the building (such as a basement, plant room, car parking space, loading space or void),

if the alteration is to a building used for the purposes of an entertainment venue (such as a cinema, theatre, hall or auditorium) in a registered club or used as an entertainment facility, the alteration must not increase the floor area used for those purposes,
if the alteration involves food and drink premises, the alteration must be carried out in accordance with AS 4674—2004, Design, construction and fit-out of food premises,
the alteration must not relate to the cooking of food at the premises by barbecue or charcoal methods,

if the alteration involves the amalgamation of retail premises located in a building, the amalgamation must not result in 1 retail premises having more than 50% of the total floor area of the building that is used for the purposes of retail premises,

the alteration must not affect an existing awning, or more than 25% of the gross floor area of an existing building to which an awning is attached, unless the awning complies with the requirements set out in the Building Code of Australia, Volume 1, B1P1 and B1P2.
If the alteration involves premises that are a food business within the meaning of the Food Act 2003, the premises must comply with the requirements under that Act.

If the alteration involves premises at which a skin penetration procedure, within the meaning of the Public Health Act 2010, is carried out, the premises must comply with the requirements under that Act, and Part 4 of the Public Health Regulation 2012.
Subclause (1)(e) does not apply to development in connection with a tertiary institution.
The following requirements of the Building Code of Australia are also standards specified for that development—
if the building that is being altered is subject to a performance solution relating to a fire safety requirement—the alteration must be consistent with that performance solution,
if the alteration involves an area of more than 500m2of commercial premises, or an area of more than 1,000m2 of premises used for light industry or a warehouse or distribution centre—that area must—
comply with the requirements set out in the Building Code of Australia, Volume 1, D1P2–D1P5, and
comply with the number of sanitary and other facilities set out in the Building Code of Australia, Volume 1, F4P1, and
comply with the light and ventilation requirements set out in the Building Code of Australia, Volume 1, F6P1–F6P5,

if the building is a mixed use development that also contains a Class 2, 3 or 4 portion—the altered area must be separated from the Class 2, 3 or 4 portion by building elements that comply with the fire resistance performance requirements set out in the Building Code of Australia, Volume 1, C1P2 and C1P8.
Subclause (2)(b) is also a standard specified for that development if the alteration involves an area of more than 500m2 of a tertiary institution.

The construction, installation or alteration of a mechanical ventilation system on a building that is used for any purpose (other than a dwelling house) is development specified for this code if it is not carried out in a heritage conservation area or a draft heritage conservation area.
The standards specified for that development are that the development must—
be located at least 3.5m behind the building line from any lot boundary, and
comply with the Noise Policy, and
be located not more than 1m above the ridge of a pitched roof or 3m above a flat roof, and
not relate to the cooking of food at the premises by barbecue or charcoal methods, and
if it is located on bush fire prone land—be constructed or installed so that any opening is sealed against the entry of embers.

If the mechanical ventilation system is a regulated system within the meaning of the Public Health Act 2010, the system must comply with the requirements of that Act and the regulations made under it, including AS/NZS 3666.1:2011, Air-handling and water systems of buildings—Microbial control, Part 1: Design, installation and commissioning.

An external alteration to, or the repair or replacement of, an existing shop front or awning, or the construction of a new awning, on a building that is used for any purpose other than for the purpose of a dwelling house is development specified for this code if it is not carried out in a heritage conservation area or a draft heritage conservation area.
The standards specified for that development are that the development must—
not result in an increase in the gross floor area of the building, and
not reduce the area of the window or other clear glass of the shop front, and
not reduce the level of transparency of the shop front, such as by using obscure glazing, and
not reduce the existing level of access to the building for people with a disability, and
in the case of the replacement of an awning or the construction of a new awning—be no less than 2.7m high at any point measured above ground level (existing), and
in the case of the replacement of an existing awning fascia—have a vertical depth for the replacement fascia not greater than the vertical depth of the existing awning fascia, and

in the case of the construction of a new awning—have a vertical depth for the awning fascia not greater than the average of the vertical depths of the immediately adjoining awning fascias or, if there are no adjoining awning fascias, 350mm, and
be no closer than 450mm to the edge of any kerb or alignment of any path on which vehicles travel, and
be designed and certified by a professional engineer, and
in the case of the replacement of an awning or the construction of a new awning—be constructed of non-combustible material if it is located on bush fire prone land, and
in the case of the alteration to, or the repair of, an awning—not be carried out unless the awning complies with the requirements set out in the Building Code of Australia, Volume 1, B1P1 and B1P2.
A structure on public land or on or over a public road requires the prior approval of the relevant authority under the Local Government Act 1993 or the Roads Act 1993, respectively.
The construction or installation of a skylight or roof window on a building that is used for any purpose other than a dwelling house is development specified for this code.
The standards specified for that development are that the development must—
be constructed or installed so that any opening created is adequately weather proofed, and
if located on bush fire prone land—be constructed or installed so that any opening is sealed against the entry of embers, and
if located on land in a heritage conservation area or draft heritage conservation area—be constructed or installed within the plane of the roof and not be visible on the street elevation.

The construction or installation of a business identification sign or building identification sign that projects from the exterior wall of an existing building is development specified for the purposes of this code if—
it is not carried out on or in a heritage item or draft heritage item or in a heritage conservation area or draft heritage conservation area, and
it is carried out on land that is in a business, employment, mixed use, industrial or special purpose zone or Zone W4.
The standards specified for that development are that the development must—

not result in more than 4 business identification signs (which may refer to more than 1 business within the building) or building identification signs (or both) of this type for the building so long as only one sign is visible on each elevation of the building, and
not project beyond the parapet or eaves of the building to which it is attached, and
if located in an industrial zone or Zone E4 or E5—be no more than 2.5m2 in area and not project more than 1.5m horizontally from the facade of the building, and
if located in any other zone—be no more than 1.5m2 in area and not project more than 0.75m horizontally from the facade of the building, and
be erected with the lower edge at least 2.6m above ground level (existing), and
be securely fixed to the wall in accordance with—
AS/NZS 1170.0:2002, Structural design actions, Part 0: General principles, and
AS/NZS 1170.2:2011, Structural design actions, Part 2: Wind actions, and
if the sign is illuminated—
have its means of illumination, including any associated cables, concealed or integrated within the frame of the sign, and
not be animated, flashing or moving, and
comply with AS/NZS 4282:2019, Control of the obtrusive effects of outdoor lighting, and

if the sign is a business identification sign and is on land that is within a residential zone or within 50m of land that is within a residential zone and the sign faces the residential zone—only be illuminated during the following periods—
if the hours of operation of the business identified on the sign have been approved—during those hours,
if the hours of operation of the business identified on the sign have not been approved—between 7.00 am and 10.00 pm on any day.
A structure on public land or on or over a public road requires the prior approval of the relevant authority under the Local Government Act 1993 or the Roads Act 1993, respectively.
Subclause (1)(c) does not apply to development in connection with a tertiary institution.

heading.b: Freestanding pylon and directory board signs

block.txt: The erection of a business identification sign or building identification sign that is displayed on a freestanding structure that is mounted on the ground on one or more supports is development specified for this code if—
it is not carried out on or in a heritage item or a draft heritage item or in a heritage conservation area or a draft heritage conservation area, and
it is carried out on land that is in a business, employment, mixed use, industrial or special purpose zone or Zone W4.
The standards specified for that development are that the development must—
not result in more than one such freestanding sign for each street frontage of the lot on which the development is located that is more than 15m in width, and
not be higher than 6m from ground level (existing), and
not have an area for the sign of more than 8m2 unless paragraph (d) applies, and
if the development is located on premises with more than one commercial tenant—not have an area for the sign of more than 16m2, and
not be located within 3m of any protected tree, and
be constructed and installed in accordance with—
AS/NZS 1170.0:2002, Structural design actions, Part 0: General principles, and
AS/NZS 1170.2:2011, Structural design actions, Part 2: Wind actions, and
not obstruct the visibility sight lines of, or interfere with, any traffic control device, including traffic control lights, and
if the sign is illuminated—
have its means of illumination, including any associated cables, concealed or integrated within the frame of the sign, and
not be animated, flashing or moving, and
comply with AS/NZS 4282:2019, Control of the obtrusive effects of outdoor lighting, and

if the sign is a business identification sign and is on land that is within 50m of land that is within a residential zone and the sign faces the residential zone—only be illuminated during the following periods—
if the hours of operation of the business identified on the sign have been approved—during those hours, or
if the hours of operation of the business identified on the sign have not been approved—between 7.00 am and 10.00 pm on any day.
A structure on public land or on or over a public road requires the prior approval of the relevant authority under the Local Government Act 1993 or the Roads Act 1993, respectively.

content.txt: pt 5, div 1, sdiv 9, hdg: Subst 2017 (270), Sch 1 [44].

block.txt: Development, or the carrying out of works, that is or are ancillary to the use of land is development specified for this code if it is not carried out on a lot that—
contains a dwelling house, or
is a flood control lot.
The standards specified for that development are that the development must—
have an area of not more than 100m2, or 15% of the area of the site on which the development is carried out, whichever is the lesser, and
not have a building height of more than 5m, and
be located at least 1m behind the building line of any road frontage (except where the development is a front awning on a building), and
be located at least 3m from any boundary adjoining land on which a dwelling is located, and
not be located over a registered easement, and
not reduce vehicular access to, parking on or loading or unloading on or from, the lot, and
not reduce the landscaped area of the lot, and
if carried out in a heritage conservation area or in a draft heritage conservation area—
be located behind the rear building line and no closer to each side boundary than the existing development with which it is associated, and
not be carried out on a lot that adjoins a lane or a secondary or parallel road, and
to the extent that it is comprised of metal components—be constructed of low reflective, factory pre-coloured materials, and
if located on bush fire prone land—be constructed of non-combustible material, and

satisfy the requirements contained in an applicable development control plan applying to the land concerning its drainage systems and not interfere with the functioning of existing drainage fixtures or flow paths, and
in the case of a garbage bin enclosure—
not have a floor area more than 5m2, and
not be higher than 3m if roofed or 1.5m above ground level (existing) if not roofed, and
not be carried out under an awning unless the awning—
complies with the requirements set out in the Building Code of Australia, Volume 1, B1P1 and B1P2, and
is structurally sound.

heading.b: Earthworks, retaining walls and structural support

block.txt: Earthworks and the construction or installation of a retaining wall or other form of structural support are development specified for this code if they are not carried out on a lot that—
contains a dwelling house, or
is a flood control lot.
The standards specified for excavation work are that the work must—
be structurally sound, and
if the land is not identified as Class 3 or 4 on the Acid Sulfate Soils Map—not be more than 3m below ground level (existing), and
if the land is identified as Class 3 or 4 on the Acid Sulfate Soils Map—not be more than 1m below ground level (existing), and
be carried out at least 40m from any waterbody (natural), and
not result in a building being located over a registered easement, and
if it is on a lot adjacent to a rail corridor—be setback at least 3m from the corridor.
The standards specified for fill are that the fill must—
not raise the ground level (existing) more than 2m, and
be structurally sound, and
be located at least 40m from any waterbody (natural).
Earthworks that are more than 1m above or below ground level (existing) are structurally sound only if they have structural support that—
a professional engineer has certified as structurally sound, including in relation to (but not limited to) the ability to withstand the forces of lateral soil load, and
has adequate drainage lines connected to an existing stormwater drainage system for the site, and
does not redirect the flow of any water or cause sediment to be transported onto an adjoining property, and
is not higher than 3m, and
is separated from any other structural support on the site by at least 2m, measured horizontally, and
is not located over a registered easement.

heading.b: Driveways, hard stand spaces, pathways and paving

block.txt: The following development is specified for this code if it is not carried out on a lot that contains a dwelling house—
the construction or installation of pathways or paving,
the construction or installation of a driveway associated with access to a hard stand space, carport, loading bay or garage,
the construction or installation of a hard stand space, whether open or part of a carport.
The standards specified for that development are that the development must—
satisfy the requirements of any applicable development control plan concerning its drainage systems and not interfere with the functioning of existing drainage fixtures or flow paths, and
not require a cut or fill of greater than 2m from ground level (existing), and
if it is a driveway or hard stand space—

be constructed in accordance with AS/NZS 2890.1:2004, Parking facilities, Part 1: Off-street car parking or AS 2890.2:2018, Parking facilities, Part 2: Off-street commercial vehicle facilities and RMS Australian Standard Supplements, Australian Standard—AS2890, Parking Facilities, Parts 1–6 issued by Transport for NSW, and
be designed to allow all vehicles to turn around within the site and exit in a forward direction, and
be designed and certified by a professional engineer, and
if it is a driveway—have the consent required for a driveway under section 138 of the Roads Act 1993 from the appropriate roads authority, and
if the development is a hard stand space—
be associated with a driveway, and
be located at least 3m from any boundary that adjoins a residential zone, and

if it is a pathway or paving area to be used for pedestrian access—be designed or constructed in accordance with AS 1428.1—2009, Design for access and mobility, Part 1: General requirements for access—New building work.

heading.b: Click and collect bays, drive through facilities and goods collection lockers

block.txt: The construction, installation or alteration of a click and collect bay, drive through facility or goods collection locker, and associated directional signage, is development specified for this code.
Without limiting subclause (1), the conversion of a car parking space into a click and collect bay is development specified for this code.
Subclause (2) applies even if the conversion of a car parking space will result in less than the required minimum number of car parking spaces for the land.
In this Subdivision—
click and collect bay means a car parking space the main purpose of which is to enable goods, purchased online or by telephone, to be collected, returned or exchanged.
drive through facility means a building or place the main purpose of which is to enable purchased goods to be collected by the driver of a motor vehicle without leaving the vehicle.
goods collection locker means a building or place at which unstaffed and secured lockers are provided to enable purchased goods to be collected from the lockers.

required minimum number of car parking spaces means the minimum number of car parking spaces required under an environmental planning instrument, development control plan or condition of a development consent.

The standards specified for development for a click and collect bay are that the development must not reduce the number of car parking spaces on the land on which the development is carried out by more than the lesser of the following—
20 car parking spaces,
15% of the number of car parking spaces on the land.
The standards specified for development for a drive through facility are that the drive through facility must—
be located behind the building line of a road frontage, and
not be located adjacent to residential accommodation, and
not reduce the number of car parking spaces on the land on which the development is carried out.
The standards specified for development for a goods collection locker are as follows—
the maximum gross floor area of the goods collection locker is 15 square metres,
the maximum height of the goods collection locker is 3 metres above ground level (existing),
the minimum setback from a boundary with adjoining land is 3.5 metres.
A car park affected by development for a click and collect bay or drive through facility must comply with the following standards—
AS/NZS 2890.1:2004, Parking facilities, Part 1: Off-street car parking,
AS 2890.2:2018, Parking facilities, Part 2: Off-street commercial vehicle facilities,
AS 2890.3:2015, Parking facilities, Part 3: Bicycle parking,
AS/NZS 2890.6:2009, Parking facilities, Part 6: Off-street parking for people with disabilities.

The construction of a fence that is not located on the boundary of a road, other than a rear lane, is development specified for this code if it is not carried out on a lot that contains a dwelling house.
The standards specified for that development are that the development must—
be located on a side or rear boundary, and
not be more than 3m above ground level (existing), and
not be of solid construction.

Despite subclause (1), any fence located along the boundary of a site that adjoins land within a residential zone or a lane must be open for at least 75% of the area of the fence that is more than 1.8m above ground level (existing).
Development standards for fences that are exempt development are specified in Division 1 of Part 2.

heading.b: Development standards for land near Siding Spring Observatory

block.txt: All external lighting associated with development under this Part in the local government areas of Coonamble, Gilgandra, Warrumbungle Shire and Dubbo Regional is development specified for this code.
The standards specified for that development are that the development must—
be installed or constructed using a shielded light fitting, and
be downward facing, and
for each site—not exceed 50,000 lumens, and
for each individual light—not exceed a maximum colour temperature of 3,500 kelvin.
In this clause—
shielded light fitting means a light fitting that does not allow light to shine above the horizontal plane.

heading.b: Conditions applying to complying development certificates under this code

block.txt: A complying development certificate for development specified under this code must be issued subject to the conditions specified in Schedule 8.

Clause 1.18(1)(b) states that to be complying development for the purposes of this Policy the development must be permissible with consent under an environmental planning instrument applying to the land on which the development is carried out.

In addition to the requirements specified for development under this code, adjoining owners’ property rights, the applicable common law and other legislative requirements for approvals, licences, permits and authorities still apply. For example, requirements relevant to development in this code may be contained in the Act, the Environmental Planning and Assessment Regulation 2000, various State environmental planning policies, the Protection of the Environment Operations Act 1997, the Roads Act 1993 and Acts applying to various infrastructure authorities. If the development is in proximity to infrastructure, including water, stormwater and sewer mains, electricity power lines and telecommunications facilities, the relevant infrastructure authority should be contacted before commencing the development.

content.txt: pt 5A, note 2 (previously Part 5A, note): Ins 2013 (706), Sch 1 [177]. Renumbered as note 2, 2017 (270), Sch 1 [47].

block.txt: In this Part—
business zone means Zone E1, E2, E3, MU1, B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, B6, B7, B8, IN4, SP1, SP2, SP3, SP5 or W4.
industrial zone means Zone E4, E5, IN1, IN2 or IN3.
specified purpose—see clause 5A.2.
In this Part, a requirement in relation to a building is a development standard that must be met for development in relation to the building to be complying development under this code.
For the purposes of this Part, each of the following is a specified purpose—
amusement centres,
boat building and repair facilities,
commercial premises,
community facilities,
depots,
entertainment facilities,
function centres,
health consulting rooms,
industries,
information and education facilities,
local distribution premises,
medical centres,
recreational facilities (indoor),
storage premises,
vehicle body repair workshops,
vehicle repair stations,
veterinary hospitals,
warehouses or distribution centres,
waste or resource transfer stations.
However, for the purposes of this Part, each of the following is not a specified purpose—
data centres,
funeral homes,
markets,
potentially hazardous industries, and potentially offensive industries, within the meaning of State Environmental Planning Policy No 33—Hazard and Offensive Development,
pubs,
registered clubs,
restricted premises,
retail premises that sell firearms within the meaning of the Firearms Act 1996,
roadside stalls,
sex services premises,
small bars.
Development for a specified purpose on land in an industrial zone or a business zone is development specified for this code.

Despite subclause (1), development involving the erection of a new building for a specified purpose is not development specified for this code on land in Zone E1, E2, MU1, B1, B2, B3, B4, B8, IN4, SP1, SP3, SP5 or W4.
Despite subclause (1), development for the purposes of waste or resource transfer stations is development specified for this code only if carried out by or on behalf of a public authority.
The standards specified for the development are set out as follows—
Division 1A specifies development standards applicable to development for a specified purpose on land in an industrial zone or a business zone,

Division 2 specifies further development standards applicable only to development for a specified purpose on land in an industrial zone that involves the construction or alteration of, or addition to, a building,

Division 3 specifies further development standards applicable only to development for a specified purpose on land in a business zone that involves the construction or alteration of, or addition to, a building.
Divisions 2 and 3 do not apply to development involving internal alterations only, if the development does not increase the gross floor area of the building.
A complying development certificate for development specified for this code—
must be issued subject to the conditions specified in Schedule 8, and
is taken to satisfy a requirement under this Policy for a permit, approval or development consent to remove or prune a tree or other vegetation on a lot if—
the tree is not listed on a register of significant trees kept by the council, and
the tree or vegetation is within 3m of a building, and
the tree or vegetation has a height that is less than 8m.
A change of use of premises to specified purposes may be complying development under this code even if the change of use is carried out on land referred to in clause 1.19(5).
A change of use of premises on the following land is not development specified for this code—
part of Lot 121, DP 876962 and part of Lot 101, DP 1043160, 5 Viscount Place, Warwick Farm, as shown coloured light purple on the Liverpool Local Environmental Plan 2008 Key Sites Map,

Lot 1021, DP 812335, 63 Mulgoa Road; Lot 1, DP 1043008, 73 Mulgoa Road; Lots 151 and 152, DP 863625, 83 and 109 Mulgoa Road; Lot 12 and part of Lot 13, DP 710086, 123–135 Mulgoa Road; Lot 1, DP 1064526, 1 Retreat Road in Penrith.

heading.b: Certain development on Cockle Creek Smelter and Incitec site excluded from code

block.txt: The construction of a building for the purposes of warehouses or distribution centres, or industries, other than heavy industries or artisan food and drink industries, on land identified as “former Cockle Creek Smelter and Incitec site” on the Cockle Creek Smelter Land Map within the meaning of State Environmental Planning Policy No 55—Remediation of Land, is not development specified for this code.
Internal alterations to an existing building used for a specified purpose may be complying development under this code, even if the development is carried out on land referred to in clause 1.19(5).

heading.b: Development standards for both industrial and business zones

content.txt: pt 5A, div 1A, hdg (previously Part 5A, Div 4, heading): Ins 2013 (706), Sch 1 [177]. Subst 2021 (777), Sch 2[20]. Renumbered 2021 (777), Sch 2[30].
pt 5A, div 1A (previously Part 5A, Div 4): Ins 2013 (706), Sch 1 [177]. Renumbered 2021 (777), Sch 2[30].

block.txt: The development must not be carried out at premises that are a manufactured home, moveable dwelling or temporary structure.

If the development is on land to which a local environmental plan made under the Act, section 3.20 applies, the development must comply with the applicable standards specified under clause 5.4(4), (6), (7), (7AA) and (10) of the plan.

If the development is to be provided with water supply or sewerage services, or both, by a water utility, the applicant must obtain a notice or other form of written advice from the relevant water utility, or an entity authorised to do so by the utility, that specifies the works or other requirements to be completed as part of the development.
If the development is for the purposes of a manual collection point, the land on which the development is carried out must not contain underground storage tanks.
The development must not involve development of a kind referred to in the Environmental Planning and Assessment Regulation 2021, section 163(1)(a), (e) or (f).
The development must not result in—
the erection of a building over a registered easement, or
the clearing of more than 1,000m2 of native vegetation.
The development must not be a controlled activity within the meaning of the Airports Act 1996 of the Commonwealth, Part 12, Division 4.

Controlled activities include the construction or alteration of buildings or other structures that causes an intrusion into prescribed airspace, which is generally airspace around airports. Controlled activities cannot be carried out without an approval granted under regulations made for the purposes of the Airports Act 1996 of the Commonwealth, Part 12, Division 4.

heading.b: Miscellaneous development standards for particular specified purposes

block.txt: Food and drink premises must—
comply with AS 4674—2004, Design, construction and fit-out of food premises, and
have a maximum capacity of no more than 100 patrons, and
display a sign indicating the maximum capacity.

content.txt: cl 5A.6C (previously cl 5A.23B): Ins 2021 (777), Sch 2[21]. Renumbered 2021 (777), Sch 2[30]. Am 2022 (768), Sch 1[43].

heading.b: Maximum gross floor area for particular specified purposes

block.txt: The maximum gross floor area for retail areas included in artisan food and drink industries is the lesser of the following—
the maximum gross floor area that applies under another environmental planning instrument,
30% of the gross floor area of the building,
The maximum gross floor area for industrial retail outlets or ancillary office premises is the lesser of the following—
the maximum gross floor area that applies under another environmental planning instrument,
30% of the gross floor area of the building,
The maximum gross floor area for goods repair and reuse premises is—
for a building on land in a business zone—500m2, and
for a building on land in an industrial zone—5,000m2.
The maximum gross floor area for each of the following is 1,000m2—
amusement centres,
creative industries,
entertainment facilities,
function centres,
recreational facilities (indoor).

content.txt: cl 5A.6D (previously cl 5A.23C): Ins 2021 (777), Sch 2[21]. Renumbered 2021 (777), Sch 2[30]. Am 2022 (47), Sch 1[14].

block.txt: All areas for the storage and handling of chemicals, fuels and oils on-site must be designed with appropriate bunded areas that—
have impervious flooring, and
have sufficient capacity to contain 110% of the largest container stored within the bund, and

are designed in accordance with pages 40–44 of the document entitled Storing and Handling Liquids: Environmental Protections, Participants Manual published by the Department of Environment and Climate Change NSW in May 2007.

content.txt: cl 5A.6E (previously cl 5A.23D; previously cl 5A.14): Renumbered 2021 (777), Sch 2[22] [30].

block.txt: For a building with a gross floor area less than 500m2 in Zone E1, E2, MU1, B1, B2, B3, B4, B8, IN4, SP1, SP3, SP5 or W4 that existed before 1 February 2022—
car parking must be provided in accordance with an existing condition relating to car parking that applies to the use of the land, or
if there is no existing condition relating to car parking—the development must not reduce the number of car parking spaces on the land on which the development is carried out.
Otherwise, car parking must be provided—
in accordance with any relevant requirements contained in an environmental planning instrument or development control plan applying to the land, or

if there are no relevant requirements referred to in paragraph (a)—in accordance with the document entitled Guide to Traffic Generating Developments, Version 2.2, published by the Roads and Traffic Authority in October 2002.

If a contribution in relation to car parking in compliance with a contributions plan under the Act, Division 7.1 is imposed as a condition of approval under the Environmental Planning and Assessment Regulation 2021, section 156, the contribution may be made instead of complying with subclause (1) or (1A).
New car parking must be constructed to comply with the following standards—
AS/NZS 2890.1:2004, Parking facilities, Part 1: Off-street car parking,
AS 2890.2:2018, Parking facilities, Part 2: Off-street commercial vehicle facilities,
AS 2890.3:2015, Parking facilities, Part 3: Bicycle parking,
AS/NZS 2890.6:2009, Parking facilities, Part 6: Off-street parking for people with disabilities.
If car parking is in connection with a tertiary institution, the following additional development standards apply—
must not increase or reduce the number of car spaces currently approved for the land,
if the parking area is on grade, provide at least 1 tree with a mature height of at least 8m for every 6 cars.
Consent from the relevant roads authority may be required under section 138 of the Roads Act 1993 for the building of any kerb, crossover or driveway. See clause 1.18(1)(e).
This clause applies to development that—
provides a new loading bay or new driveway, or
involves alterations or additions specifically to an existing loading bay or driveway.
The loading facilities must be contained wholly within the lot on which the development is carried out.
Loading bays must—
be located behind the front building line of the building, and
not be located adjacent to residential accommodation.
Driveways within the lot on which the development is carried out must be designed so as to enable vehicles to leave the lot in a forward direction.
Ingress to and egress from the site, driveway widths, turning circles and the dimensions of all loading bays must be designed in accordance with—

AS/NZS 2890.1:2004, Parking facilities, Part 1: Off-street car parking or AS 2890.2:2018, Parking facilities, Part 2: Off-street commercial vehicle facilities and RMS Australian Standard Supplements, Australian Standard—AS2890, Parking Facilities, Parts 1–6, and
the document entitled Guide to Traffic Generating Developments, Version 2.2, published by the Roads and Traffic Authority in October 2002.
The standards specified for excavation work are that the work must—
be structurally sound, and
if the land is identified as Class 3 or 4 on the Acid Sulfate Soils Map—not be more than 1m below ground level (existing), and
if the land is not identified as Class 3 or 4 on the Acid Sulfate Soils Map—
for a site area less than 10,000m2—not be more than 3m below ground level (existing), or
for a site area equal to or more than 10,000m2—not be more than 6m below ground level (existing), and
be carried out at least 40m from any waterbody (natural), and
not result in a building being located over a registered easement, and
if it is on a lot adjacent to a rail corridor—be setback at least 3m from the corridor.
The standards specified for fill are that the fill must—
not raise the ground level (existing) more than—
for a site area less than 10,000m2—2m, or
for a site area equal to or more than 10,000m2—6m, and
be structurally sound, and
be located at least 40m from any waterbody (natural).
Earthworks that are more than 1m above or below ground level (existing) are structurally sound only if they have structural support that—
a professional engineer has certified as structurally sound, including in relation to (but not limited to) the ability to withstand the forces of lateral soil load, and
has adequate drainage lines connected to an existing stormwater drainage system for the site, and
does not redirect the flow of any water or cause sediment to be transported onto an adjoining property, and
is not higher than—
for a site area less than 10,000m2—3m, or
for a site area equal to or more than 10,000m2—7m, and
is separated from any other structural support on the site by at least 2m, measured horizontally, and
is not located over a registered easement.
All stormwater drainage collected as a result of the development must be conveyed by a gravity fed or charged system to—
a public drainage system, or
an inter-allotment drainage system, or
an on-site disposal system.
All stormwater drainage systems within a lot, and the connection to a public or an inter-allotment drainage system, must—
if an approval is required under section 68 of the Local Government Act 1993—be approved under that Act, or

if an approval is not required under section 68 of the Local Government Act 1993—comply with any requirements for the disposal of stormwater drainage contained in a development control plan that is applicable to the land.

content.txt: cl 5A.6I (previously cl 5A.28): Ins 2013 (706), Sch 1 [177]. Renumbered 2021 (777), Sch 2[30].

heading.b: Development standards for bush fire prone land

block.txt: This clause applies—
to the construction or alteration of, or additions to, a building on a lot that is wholly or partly bush fire prone land, and
in addition to all other development standards specified for this code.
See clause 1.19A for additional provisions relating to bush fire prone land.
The development may be carried out on the lot only if—
the development conforms to the specifications and requirements of Planning for Bush Fire Protection that are relevant to the development, and
the lot has direct access to a public road or a road vested in or maintained by the council, and
a reticulated water supply is connected to the lot, and
a fire hydrant is located less than 70m from the location on the lot of the proposed development, and
mains electricity is connected to the lot, and

reticulated or bottled gas on the lot is installed and maintained in accordance with AS/NZS 1596:2014, The storage and handling of LP Gas and the requirements of relevant authorities (such as the requirement that metal piping be used), and
any gas cylinders on the lot that are within 10m of a dwelling—
have their release valves directed away from the dwelling, and
are enclosed on the hazard side of the installation, and
have metal connections to and from the cylinders, and
there are no polymer sheathed flexible gas supply lines to gas meters adjacent to any dwelling on the lot or an adjoining lot.
The requirements relating to the construction of buildings in bush fire prone areas set out in the Building Code of Australia also apply.

heading.b: Complying development on flood control lots

block.txt: Development under this code must not be carried out on any part of a flood control lot, other than a part of the lot that the council or a professional engineer who specialises in hydraulic engineering has certified, for the purposes of the issue of the complying development certificate, as not being any of the following—
a flood storage area,
a floodway,
a flow path,
a high hazard area,
a high risk area.
Development that is carried out under this code on any part of a flood control lot must meet the following requirements—

if there is a minimum floor level adopted in a development control plan by the relevant council for the lot, the development must not cause any habitable room in the dwelling house to have a floor level lower than that floor level,
any part of the building that is erected at or below the flood planning level is constructed of flood compatible material,

any part of the building that is erected is able to withstand the forces exerted during a flood by water, debris and buoyancy up to the flood planning level (or if an on-site refuge is provided on the lot, the probable maximum flood level),
the development must not result in increased flooding elsewhere in the floodplain,
the lot must have pedestrian and vehicular access to a readily accessible refuge at a level equal to or higher than the lowest habitable floor level of the building,
vehicular access to the building will not be inundated by water to a level of more than 0.3m during a 1:100 ARI (average recurrent interval) flood event,
the lot must not have any open car parking spaces or carports lower than the level of a 1:20 ARI (average recurrent interval) flood event.

The requirements under subclause (2)(c) and (d) are satisfied if a joint report by a professional engineer specialising in hydraulic engineering and a professional engineer specialising in civil engineering states that the requirements are satisfied.
A word or expression used in this clause has the same meaning as it has in the Flood Risk Management Manual, unless it is otherwise defined in this Policy.
A section 10.7 certificate from a Council will state whether or not a lot is a flood control lot.

heading.b: Development standards for land near Siding Spring Observatory

block.txt: This clause applies—
to all external lighting associated with development under this Part in the local government areas of Coonamble, Gilgandra, Warrumbungle Shire and Dubbo Regional, and
in addition to all other development standards specified for this code.
The development must—
be installed or constructed using a shielded light fitting, and
be downward facing, and
for each site—not exceed 50,000 lumens, and
for each individual light—not exceed a maximum colour temperature of 3,500 kelvin.
In this clause—
shielded light fitting means a light fitting that does not allow light to shine above the horizontal plane.

content.txt: cl 5A.6L (previously cl 5A.30A): Ins 2017 (270), Sch 1 [49]. Renumbered 2021 (777), Sch 2[30]. Am 2023 (79), Sch 1[2].

heading.b: Development standard for development involving awnings

block.txt: This clause applies to development to which this code applies that—
includes the construction or installation of an awning, or
includes the replacement or alteration of, or otherwise affects, an existing awning, or
is carried out under an existing awning.
The awning must—
comply with the requirements set out in the Building Code of Australia, Volume 1, B1P1 and B1P2, and
be structurally sound.

content.txt: cl 5A.6M (previously cl 5A.30B): Ins 2019 (621), Sch 6[42]. Renumbered 2021 (777), Sch 2[30]. Am 2023 (83), Sch 2.2[4].

block.txt: This clause applies to development to which this code applies that involves the erection of a building, if the building does not have an existing garbage and waste storage area.
A garbage and waste storage area must be provided as part of the development.
The garbage and waste storage area must—
be screened, and
be located behind the primary road frontage building line, and
not be located in car parking, loading bay or landscaped area, and
not be located on a side of the building that faces an adjoining lot on which there is a dwelling, and

comply with the following appendices in the document entitled Better Practice Guidelines for Waste Management and Recycling in Commercial and Industrial Facilities, ISBN 978-1-74293-944-5, published by the NSW Environment Protection Authority in December 2012—
appendices A and B, for the size and location of garbage and storage areas and the size of waste receptacles,
appendices C and D, for the design of openings of waste storage areas and loading bay turning circles for waste removal vehicles,
appendix E, for standard signs for waste storage areas,
appendix F, for the design and operational capacity of waste storage areas.

heading.b: Development standards for industrial zones only

block.txt: The maximum gross floor area for a building is 50,000m2.
The maximum floor space ratio for a building is—
the maximum floor space ratio that applies under another environmental planning instrument, or
if there is no maximum floor space ratio referred to in paragraph (a)—1:1.
The maximum building height for a building is the greater of the following—
the maximum building height that applies under another environmental planning instrument,
If the development has a boundary with a classified road, the building must have a setback from the boundary with the classified road of—
at least 10m, or

if a greater setback is applicable in those circumstances under another environmental planning instrument applying to the land on which the building is erected—at least the setback specified in that instrument.
If the development has a boundary with a primary road that is not a classified road, the building must have a setback from that boundary of—
the average distance of the setbacks of the nearest 2 buildings that—
have a boundary with the same road, and
are located within 40m of the lot on which the building is erected, or
at least 10m,
whichever is the lesser.

If the development is on a lot that has a boundary with a parallel road that is not a classified road, the building must have a setback from the boundary with the parallel road determined in accordance with subclause (2).
If the development is located on a corner lot, the building must have a setback from the boundary of the secondary road of at least 3m if the secondary road is not a classified road.

If the development is on a lot that is subject to a proposed road widening under a local environmental plan, the building must have a setback from the boundary with the road, after acquisition for the road widening, of at least—
if the road widening is for a local road—10m, or
if the road widening is for a classified road widening, a future classified road widening or a local road future classified road—4.5m.

Despite subclauses (1)–(4A), an addition or alteration to an existing building may have a setback from the boundary of any road that is not a classified road at the same distance as the setback of the existing building from that boundary.
Despite subclauses (1)–(4A), the requirements of this clause do not apply to the existing parts of a building.

Despite subclauses (1)–(6), if a setback is specified in a development control plan applying to the lot on which the development is located, the building must have the setback specified in the development control plan.

heading.b: Setbacks of development from side and rear boundaries

block.txt: If the development is a new building, or the alteration of or an addition to an existing building, on land that adjoins a lot in a residential zone, the building must have a setback from the boundary of the adjoining lot of—

for a building with a gross floor area of not more than 1,000m2—at least 3m, plus an additional metre for every whole metre by which the building exceeds 4.5m in height above ground level (existing), or

for a building with a gross floor area of more than 1,000m2 but not more than 5,000m2—at least 5m, plus an additional metre for every whole metre by which the building exceeds 4.5m in height above ground level (existing), or

for a building with a gross floor area of more than 5,000m2 but not more than 10,000m2—at least 20m, plus an additional metre for every whole metre by which the building exceeds 4.5m in height above ground level (existing), or
for a building with a gross floor area of more than 10,000m2 but not more than 50,000m2—at least 50m, with a maximum building height of the greater of the following—
the maximum building height that applies under another environmental planning instrument,
18m above ground level (existing).

If the development is a new building, or the alteration of or an addition to an existing building, on a lot that adjoins a public reserve, the building must have a setback from the boundary with the public reserve of at least 3m and the area of that setback must be a landscaped area.

If the development is a new building, or the alteration of or an addition to an existing building, on a lot that adjoins an environmentally sensitive area, the building must have a setback from the boundary with that environmentally sensitive area of at least 10m and an area of at least 3m in width of that setback must be a landscaped area.
Despite the other provisions of this clause, the requirements of this clause do not apply to the existing parts of a building that are not being altered or added to.
If the development is carried out on a lot that has a boundary with a railway corridor, the new building or addition and any ancillary development must be located at least 3m from that boundary.

heading.b: Front facade material finishes for new buildings

block.txt: A new building must—
as part of a facade that faces a primary road— have a door or window, and
as part of the facade of the front of the building—
have a front door, or
have an entry with an awning or portico, or
be distinguished by the use of different building materials.

Sun shading devices, screens or canopies must be provided for each glazed wall or window in a new building if the glazed wall or window faces in a direction that is between north and east or north and west.
All glazing in a new building must be of low reflective glass.

heading.b: Building elements within the articulation zone for new buildings

block.txt: The following building elements are permitted within an articulation zone for a new building—
an entry feature or portico,
an awning or canopy over a door or window.
A building element within the articulation zone of a new building—
must not reduce the required landscape area, car parking spaces or driveway, and
may extend 2m into the minimum required front setback, but must not be more than 25% of the width of the front facade of the building, and
must not be more than the maximum height of the building.
If the development includes development for the purposes of an ancillary caretaker’s flat, the flat must—
for development that is—
the construction of a new building—form part of the new building, or
the alteration of or addition to an existing building—be an addition to the existing building, and
comply with the relevant requirements contained in Volume 1 of the Building Code of Australia that are applicable to a Class 4 building, and
have a floor area not exceeding 100m2.
The development must not include more than one caretaker’s flat per lot.

A landscaped area complying with the following specifications must be provided along each boundary of a lot on which the development is carried out with any adjoining road (except in areas necessary for vehicle and pedestrian access)—
at least 3m in width or, if the setback from the road boundary is less than 3m, the width of the setback, and
with a soil depth of at least 1m, and

if the width of a lot is more than 10m at the primary street frontage—with a species of trees planted at 3m intervals along that frontage that are capable of achieving a height of at least 8m at maturity and at least 2m within 2 years of the occupation of the development.
If the development adjoins a residential zone, the setback area referred to in clause 5A.11(1) must have in it a landscaped area, adjacent to the boundary with that zone, that is—
for a building with a gross floor area of more than 1,000m2 but not more than 5,000m2—at least 3m wide in that setback, and
for a building with a gross floor area of more than 5,000m2 but not more than 10,000m2—at least 5m wide in that setback, and
for a building with a gross floor area of more than 10,000m2 but not more than 50,000m2—at least 10m wide in that setback.
The landscaped area required under subclause (2) must have trees and shrubs planted evenly across its length and width with, for every 3m2 of the area—
1 tree of a species capable of achieving a height of at least 8m at maturity and at least 2m within 2 years of the occupation of the development, and
1 shrub of a species capable of achieving a height of at least 2m within 5 years of the occupation of the development and no more than 5m at maturity.
This clause does not apply to development that is the alteration of, or addition to, an existing building if the development does not—
increase the footprint of the building, or
decrease the landscaped area on the lot.

heading.b: Development standards for business zones only

block.txt: The standards specified for development under this Division are that—

if the development is an alteration of, or addition to, a building on land in Zone E1, E2, MU1, B1, B2, B3, B4, B8, IN4, SP1, SP3, SP5 or W4—the development must be behind the front building line of the building, and

if the development involves the erection of a building in Zone E3, B5, B6 or B7—the design of the development must be consistent with the relevant design criteria set out in the Business Zone Design Guide, published by the Department of Planning, Industry and Environment in December 2021 and available on the NSW planning portal.
any new facade created by the development that faces any street must have a surface comprised of not more than 50% glazed materials which must be low reflective glass.
Despite subclause (1)(b), the requirements of this Part prevail to the extent that the Business Zone Design Guide is inconsistent with this Part.
The maximum gross floor area for additions to a building on land in Zone E1, E2, MU1, B1, B2, B3, B4, B8, IN4, SP1, SP3, SP5 or W4 is the lesser of the following—
50% of the gross floor area of the building,
if the building—
is used as retail premises—1,000m2, or
is not used as retail premises—2,500m2.
The maximum gross floor area for a building on land in Zone E3, B5, B6 or B7 is 10,000m2.

Despite subclause (2), the maximum gross floor area for a building resulting from development on land to which the Sydney Local Environmental Plan 2012, clause 7.32 applies and used for the purposes of specialised retail premises or vehicle sales or hire premises is 1000m2.
The maximum floor space ratio for a building is—
the maximum floor space ratio that applies under another environmental planning instrument, or
if there is no maximum floor space ratio referred to in paragraph (a)—1:1.
Development must comply with landscaping requirements contained in a development control plan that applies to the development.
Development on land in Zone E3, B5, B6 or B7 must meet the requirements in this clause relating to—
site coverage, and
landscaped areas.
The percentage of an infill lot that must be open space is as follows—
for a building of 1 storey—at least 50%,
for a building of 2 storeys—at least 45%,
for a building of 3 storeys—at least 40%,
for a building of 4 storeys—at least 35%,
for a building of 5 storeys—at least 30%.
At least 50% of the open space of an infill lot must be landscaped area.
For a building of 1 storey on a freestanding lot—
at least 60% of the lot must be open space, and
at least 25% of the open space must be landscaped area.
For a building of 2 storeys on a freestanding lot—
at least 65% of the lot must be open space, and
at least 30% of the open space must be landscaped area.
For a building of 3 storeys on a freestanding lot—
at least 65% of the lot must be open space, and
at least 35% of the open space must be landscaped area.
For a building of 4 storeys on a freestanding lot—
at least 70% of the lot must be open space, and
at least 40% of the open space must be landscaped area.
For a building of 5 storeys on a freestanding lot—
at least 70% of the lot must be open space, and
at least 45% of the open space must be landscaped area.

If there is more than 1 building on a lot, the number of storeys for the purposes of this clause must be determined in accordance with the Business Zone Design Guide dated December 2021 and published on the NSW planning portal.
In this clause—
freestanding lot means a lot whose total nearby side setback distance is at least 15% of the lot’s total nearby lot width.
infill lot means a lot that is not a freestanding lot.
open space means the part of a lot not covered by buildings.
total nearby lot width, in relation to a lot, means the sum of the widths, measured at the lots’ boundary with the adjoining road reserve, of—
the lot, and
the 5 lots, excluding vacant lots, to both sides of the lot.
total nearby side setback distance, in relation to a lot, means the sum of the side setbacks of—
the 5 lots, excluding vacant lots, to both sides of the lot, or

if the 5 lots, excluding vacant lots, to the side of the lot are not all in the same zone as the lot—all lots until the zone boundary, excluding vacant lots, to the side of the lot that are in the same zone.
If there is a dwelling on an adjoining lot, the maximum building height for a building is 8.5m.
If there is not a dwelling on an adjoining lot, the maximum building height for a building is the lesser of the following—
the maximum building height that applies under another environmental planning instrument,
The maximum height of any ancillary development must not be more than 5m.
The minimum building setback for a building from a boundary with a parallel road that is a classified road is—
the minimum building setback that applies under another environmental planning instrument, or
if there is no minimum building setback referred to in paragraph (a)—3m.
The minimum building setback for a building on land subject to a proposed road widening under a local environmental plan is—
if the road widening is for a local road—10m, or
if the road widening is for a classified road widening, a future classified road widening or a local road future classified road—3m.
The minimum building setback from an adjoining lot used as residential accommodation within 3m of the land on which a building is erected is—
for a part of the building that is not more than 3m in height above ground level (existing)—1.5m,
for a part of the building that is more than 6m in height above ground level (existing)—4.5m.
Subclause (3)(a) does not apply if there is no residential accommodation on the ground floor facing the building.
The minimum building setback of a building from a railway corridor is 2m.
The requirements of this clause do not apply to a part of a building that is not being altered or added to.
A window in a building must have a privacy screen for any part of the window that is less than 1.5m above finished floor level if—
the window faces a building used for residential accommodation on an adjoining lot, and
the wall in which the window is located has a setback of less than 6m from the boundary of that adjoining lot.
